## 2026-09-10 (round 19) — the worklist notes, and what Hunter's parser assumes

Artifacts: worklist `6220ad23` · unbarred roots `f91b6513-6ca5-4364-bf7f-c852c5d6a1aa`.

### 🔴 THE finding: the dictionary has THREE block openers; the parser knows two

Measured over all 789 dictionary pages, by what sits at the column margin:

| at the column margin | count | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `T8` headword | 1,603 | a main entry — **parser opens an entry** ✅ |
| `T11` sense number, then `T9` | 5,949 | a numbered sub-entry — **parser adds a sense** ✅ |
| `T9` form, no number | **4,372** | a derived-form index entry — **parser swallows it** ❌ |

The third is a *separate entry*, and **3,351 of the 4,372 carry a cross-reference arrow within
three rows** (`an–sun–in [PF] be gathered in a place → sun:2`). A `T8` opener essentially never
does — 2 of 1,603. So the arrow is very nearly diagnostic.

In the records: **4,375 unnumbered senses carry a cross-reference; exactly 1 numbered sense does.**
**3,910 of them sit inside an S09-flagged entry — 89% of S09's damage is this one pattern.**
The book has roughly 6,500 entry blocks, not 2,133.

⚠️ The geometry is unambiguous and the parser already computes it: a numbered sub-entry puts the
**number** at the margin and indents the form ~9pt; an index entry puts the **form itself** at the
margin. `klhiw`'s 148 absorbed senses, `manu`'s 137 and `ansinis`'s run are all this.

### The maintainer's worklist notes, classified

| # | note | class | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ansinis` `antua` `aniamin` | "just the next headword… missing a pattern" | **the T9-at-margin opener** | ⬆ found, not yet fixed |
| `Akiko` | "not a root if there are *no* numbered entries following" | root test | S05 already flags 7; rule confirmed |
| `a__280` | subscript `2` belongs to `a`, not to "ature"; a second `a` hallucinated | homograph subscript | real parse bug |
| `filhaq` | subscripts imply ≥2 identical headwords, numbered in order | homograph | validator rule to add |
| `filhaq` `rima` | the book fails to change fonts; two head phrases run together | **source typo, needs corroborating signal** | open |
| `aki` | code-switching inside an English definition | `_is_citation` | already handled |
| `fa` | Thao creeper names (binbin, marumiz, quay, qula) are part of the definition | E02 false positive | narrow the rule |
| `fizfiz` | `(Linn.)` + Latin binomial — delete, no @notes | parenthetical class | POL-024 follow-up |
| `Sage` `Wane` `iseg` `tai'eg` | e/o are fine in names and loanwords | E01/E03 false positives | exempt capitalised + loans |
| `rima` | repeated `1a` is the book's error; numbers are stripped anyway | none | no action |

### Hunter's parser — the assumptions worth naming
1. **Two openers, not three** (above). The single largest defect.
2. **`finish()` required both source *and* translation** — an example without a translation left
   the corpus with no trace. Now logged in the discards ledger.
3. **Hardcoded geometry**: `x0 < 300` for the column, `continuation_x` 114/306, `note_x` 130/323.
   Absolute points, never measured per page.
4. **Font names hardcoded with no guard** — printed p. 291 is set in Book Antiqua and was
   silently invisible (fixed: `FONT_ALIASES` + `KNOWN_FONTS`).
5. **Three parentheticals fixed by string literal** (`(itia`, `alternatively /tilha/`,
   `(recorded`) — the general class was not modelled. Superseded by `QC/utilities/parentheticals.py`.
6. **`translation_started` is sticky per row** — once English appears, every later Thao run on
   that row is relabelled translation, so a second example starting mid-row is absorbed.
7. **`standardize_blust` strips every `Mn` mark**, taking Blust's stress acute with it.

## 2026-09-10 (round 18) — the maintainer's question: bar-less roots

**Question:** "are there any unambiguous roots (that is, ones that are followed by numbered
entries starting with a 2) that are neither surrounded by || nor followed by (PAN *...)?"

**Answer: yes — 28** with neither, plus 4 more that have the etymology but no bars.

⚠️ **They were silently typed as free words.** 23 of the 32 carried *no finding at all*: S06
("a free word whose first sense is numbered") cannot fire, because the leftover colon sits in
front as an unnumbered sense; S04/S05 (the bound-root invariants) never ran.

### The rule is the colon, not the bars
Verified on the rendered page, not just the text layer — `|acay|` prints bars, `antua:` and
`qtit:` do not:

| header | count |
|---|---|
| `|acay| (PAN *aCay `die, dead'):` | 8 |
| `|ailhi| (PAN *wiRi `left side'):` | 519 |
| `kuza (PAN *kuja `how?'):` | **4** |
| `antua:` | **30** |

All four end in a colon and define nothing. Barred roots carry T10 `\ue000` sentinels around a
T8 headword; the 32 have a bare T8 headword and a T7 colon, no T10 span — a real print
difference, not a dropped glyph.

⚠️ **"Starts at 2" is not the marker either.** `Matansún:` is marked identically and runs
**1a, 1b**. The test is the empty first sense, nothing else.

### Fixed in the pipeline (`c12b5fd`)
`render()` drops the colon-sense and types the entry B whatever the header looked like; records
now carry `root_marker` (`bars` | `colon` | null). `CodeAndDocs/test_entries.py` holds all four
header shapes plus the `Matansún` exception.

```
format_A 1606 -> 1572 · format_B 527 -> 561 · senses 12240 -> 12206
S03 37 -> 33 (four spurious, from the leftover colon) · S04 65 -> 66 (hala p.395, real)
entries with a finding 448 -> 445
```
List: `CodeAndDocs/unbarred-roots.tsv` (34 rows).

### 🔴 Found en route, NOT fixed — 139 fields lose Blust's stress acute
Blust marks stress with an acute (`Matansún`, `Amúy`, `dadú`). PyMuPDF draws it as a separate
`\x13` overlay span positioned *on top of* its vowel, so the overlay's x-range sits **inside**
the preceding span's. `parse_entries.feed` joins headword spans on `|prev.x1 - span.x0| <= 2.5`,
which that overlap defeats: the headword closes early and the accent is routed into the
definition.

```
Matansún  spans: T8 'Matans'(302.4-350.4)  T8 'un'(350.3-366.6)  T8 '\x13'(350.8-358.1)
          |366.6 - 350.8| = 15.8 > 2.5  ->  headword 'Matansun', definition '́:'
```
**139 fields: 59 headwords (`Alis\x13`, `An\x13`, `bak\x13` — truncated as well as unaccented),
55 sub-entry forms, 22 definitions, 3 etymologies.**

✅ **The published XML is not affected** — `example.thao` and `example.english` are clean (0 of
139); the examples go through `join_spans`, which reorders the overlay correctly. The damage is
confined to the unpublished entry apparatus.

**The fix needs a call.** Reordering is not enough: `Alis` is a single span, so putting the
overlay before it gives `Ális`, accent on the wrong vowel. The overlay has to be *merged into*
its base span at the character offset its x0 falls at (proportional width), at row level. That
changes `normalized_rows` output and so the locked extraction — hence not done unasked.

## 2026-09-10 (round 17) — missing sense numbers filled in the pipeline; S09 surfaces 294 boundary failures

Dev repo `explore/entry-grammar` @ `21e2586`. Worklist republished (448 entries).

**Ruling applied:** a sub-entry with no printed number is not something to record and leave —
the number is recoverable from position, so the pipeline fills it. **345 inferred**, marked
`number_inferred` so the record never claims the page printed it. `ana-faw` → 4,
`ana-i` → 5, exactly as the maintainer said.

⚠️ **A blanket rule would have been wrong in both directions**, and nearly was — the naive
version would have numbered **2,597** senses:
- **Never invent a number the entry already prints.** The first attempt collided and S08
  went 16 → 103. Filling a gap before a printed `3` with another `3` is a worse record than
  one sense with no number.
- **Stop after three consecutive unnumbered sub-entries.** Past that the cause is not a
  printing slip. `klhiw` (p.478) had absorbed **148** of them — the `k-m-a-*` forms, which
  belong to another entry whose header was never detected. Numbering those 3–150 would have
  buried the defect.

### 🔴 S09 — new rule, **294 entries**
"A run of unnumbered senses — probably a missed entry boundary." This class was **completely
invisible before**: the senses simply had no number and nothing looked at runs of them.
Worst: `klhiw` 148, `manu` 137, `mismis` 77, `tmaza` 60, `kimzi` 58, `inanuru` 51.
**This is where the remaining damage is** — S04 (65) and E10 (38) are small beside it.

```
findings 208 → 497 (S09 is 294 of the increase) · entries with a finding 172 → 448
```
More findings, better information. Baseline accepted.

### On what the parser keys on (maintainer's summary, confirmed)
Font is the primary signal but is known to be unreliable, so it is corroborated by:
- **length** — an example is never one word (`_is_citation`)
- **location** — an entry opens only at the start of a row (`first_in_row`); a headword sits
  at the column margin (`x0 <= margin+4`); a sense number at/near it (`+10`); a homograph
  index sits *below* the baseline (`y0 > headword.y0+1`); headword spans are contiguous
  (`|x1-x0| <= 2.5`); note and body indents are *measured per page*, not hardcoded
- **ordering/state** — `mode` (definition|example|note); `translation_on_this_row` (Thao
  after English on a line is a citation); `row_has_xref` (everything after an arrow is the
  reference); a sub-entry arriving when the sense already has content opens a new sense
- **font aliasing** — p. 291's family mapped onto the roles the rest of the book uses

Precision on the maintainer's third bullet: it is not "examples before translations"
globally — each example is immediately followed by *its own* translation, an alternating
pair inside a sense.

## 2026-09-10 (round 16) — the maintainer's three worklist notes fixed four systematic misparses

Dev repo `explore/entry-grammar` @ `cdad60f`. Worklist regenerated:
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/6220ad23-43bf-4a9b-8cf6-38628e9b6ed1

**All four had one root cause**: the parser trusted font alone, and printed p. 291 is set in
a different family where the faces carry different roles.

1. **A headword is never mid-line.** `→ |faw|:2` was opening a new entry at the target,
   because that page draws the bar in Century as an em dash, not the italic Type 3 face. A
   bar or arrow away from the start of a row now marks the rest of that line as a
   cross-reference, and the whole reference is assembled onto the sense that made it —
   `punuq:2`, not three fragments, with the colon and digit no longer stranded on the end of
   the previous definition. **4,378 cross-references**, and **4,385 phantom senses go**:
   they were the targets, carrying `:2` as their entire definition. Verified no content
   lost — the removed senses' definitions were literally `":2"`.
2. **Sense numbers on p. 291 are in the plain face**, which aliases to the translation font,
   so they were read as translation text — *"…where it fell 3"*. A bare number at the column
   margin, first on its row, is now a sense number in that face too.
3. **Homograph entries exist** — `a₁` "future marker" vs `a₂` the linking particle,
   distinguished by a digit tucked *below the baseline* right after the headword, which was
   being read as a sense number. **38 of them**, now recorded as `homograph`.
   (⏳ The second `a` carries no subscript in the text layer, though the book prints `a₂`.)
4. **An example is never one word** — the maintainer's rule. A lone Thao word with no
   translation is a term cited inside an English definition ("the wood of the *lina* tree")
   and is recorded as a `citation`, not an example.

**Not fixed, because the book is wrong**: `ana-faw` and `ana-i` carry no printed sense
number where 4 and 5 belong.

```
senses 16,625 → 12,240 · examples 8,409 → 8,406 · findings 218 → 208
entries with a finding 178 → 172 · 1,961 of 2,133 clean (92.0%)
```

⚠️ **The worklist notes were keyed by list position** (`e0000`…), so any regeneration would
have attached them to the wrong entries. Re-keyed to `headword__page`; the three existing
notes migrated in one atomic batch. Baseline accepted for the new shape.

Every number the run produces, committed: entry/sense/example/note counts, characters

corpus reads as the wrong language.

Against the derived English list as well as Thao's letter inventory.

### "NOTE:" leak test (L01) — 0 findings
A note's marker is consumed when the note opens, so finding `NOTE:` / `NOTE` / `note:`
anywhere in a JSON value would mean a marker had been read as content. Nothing fires.

### 🔴 The bold check (E10) found a real parser bug
Maintainer's observation: **in an example the exemplified word is set bold** (T5
bold-italic; the rest is T6 italic). Confirmed on p.290 — the entry is `a` and every
example sets its `a` in T5. Each example now carries an `exemplifies` field.

It reported **166** examples with no bold word, and they were one bug: an italic Thao term
cited *inside* an English translation — "The wood of the **lina** tree does not rot
quickly" — was read as a new example, cutting the translation in half and leaving a
fragment that exemplified nothing. `extract_source.py` has had that rule for a while; this
parser did not.

```
examples  8,534 → 8,409     E10  166 → 41     E07  11 → 4     findings  341 → 209
```

### Where it stands
**1,963 of 2,133 entries (92.0%) parse with no finding.** 209 findings over 170 entries:
S04 77 · S03 29 · S08 15 · S02 13 · S07 13 · S05 9 · E10 41 · E07 4 · E01/E03 6 · S01/S06 2.
Consumption still **100.0%** (1,255,820 of 1,255,890 characters; 70 skipped, itemised).

Dev repo `explore/entry-grammar` @ `bd022b7`. **Dictionary only** — the interlinear texts
are a different structure and stay `extract_source.py`'s business.

- **`CodeAndDocs/validate_entries.py`** — content + structure + consumption.

- **`CodeAndDocs/entry-findings.tsv`** — one row per finding.

### Three things the parse had to learn that no earlier script modelled
1. **A headword split across spans** — `|aca|`+`|y|` is `acay`.
2. **Lettered sub-senses** — `afu` runs `1a, 1b, 1c` before `2` and `3`.
3. **NOTE sections** (535 of them): the marker is in the *label* face, the body in the
   *translation* face — the same face an example's English uses, so it is told apart by
   parser state, not by font.

## 2026-09-10 (round 11) — the two schemas, stated; and the invariant that validates them

Maintainer declined the font test (the font of a published book will not change) and pointed
out I had asked them to confirm schemas I never wrote down. Both fair. Reading two real
entries side by side makes the distinction obvious:

```
fatu (PAN *batu `stone; testicle')        |ailhi| (PAN *wiRi `left side'):
stone; testicle                           2 tana–ailhi  left side
nak a fatu  my testicles                    ihu i–saháy nak a tana–ailhi … 
2 fatu a shapa  scrotum                   3 maka–tana–ailhi  further to the left
3 qalha fatu  be stony, …                   numa sa tata i–saháy maka–tana–ailhi …
  i–nay a pruq qalha fatu  This ground …  4 tau–na–ailhi  turn to the left
4 kin–fatu  gather stones, …              NOTE: Almost certainly from PAN *wiRi …
```

**Format A** — the headword is a free word. It has its own definition, which is sense 1 and
is printed unnumbered; derived forms are senses 2, 3, 4…
**Format B** — the headword is a *bound root*. That is what the bars and the trailing colon
mark. It has no definition of its own, so numbering starts at 2 with the first derived form.

**One JSON shape serves both.** `format` records which; the difference is a validation
profile, not a different structure.

### The invariant, measured over all 2,133 entries
| | entries | numbered | first number = 2 | contiguous 2,3,4,… |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **A** (free word) | 1,606 | 812 (+794 single-sense) | 810/812 | **807/812 = 99.4%** |
| **B** (bound root) | 527 | 518 | **518/518 = 100%** | **504/518 = 97.3%** |

So the schemas are not a guess — the book obeys them.

### The defect list falls out: **28 entries**
- **A, non-contiguous ×5** — `k` p.446 `[2..9, 11]`, `tmaz` p.998, `a` p.280 `[1]`,
  `shawiki` p.903 `[3]`
- **B, non-contiguous ×14** — and the shape is diagnostic: `bukbuk` p.329 `[2, 2]`,
  `bahi` p.314 `[2, 3, 4, 2]`, `baruku` p.320 `[2..10, 2]` — **two entries merged**, the
  second restarting its own numbering. An entry-boundary failure, exactly as predicted.
- **B with no numbered senses ×9** — a bound root must have derived forms; zero is a defect.

Sharper than round 8's 98-signature residue, because an invariant beats a signature census.

⏳ Awaiting: confirmation of the two schemas before emitting one JSON per entry and working
the 28.

## 2026-09-10 (round 10) — how bold/italic are decided: they are not

Asked how the extractor identifies italics and bold. **On 99.9% of the book it does not.**

- PyMuPDF reports **`flags=0` for every span on every Type-3 page** — no italic bit, no bold
  bit. `size=0.1` for all nine fonts too, so size carries nothing either.
- The font names are `T4`…`T12`. Opaque. Nothing in them says "italic".
- So the code never reads style. It reads the **font name** and applies a hand-made lookup:
  `SOURCE_FONTS = {"T5","T6"}`, `TRANSLATION_FONT = "T4"`, `SUBENTRY_FONT = "T9"`,
  `GLOSS_FONTS = {"T3","T11","T10"}`, `FOOTNOTE_MARKER_FONT = "T9"` — **three bare constants
  with no comment on how they were established, and nothing that tests them.**
- The one exception is printed p. 291, which is TrueType: there the file *does* say —
  `flags=22` = bold+italic+serifed, and the names are self-describing
  (`BookAntiqua-BoldItalic`). That is why its alias map could be written confidently.

### The check nobody had run
Measured what each font actually carries (printed pp. 280–690, unambiguous function words):

| font | tokens | English | Thao | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| T4 | 57,359 | 19.8% | 2.4% | **English** ✓ `TRANSLATION_FONT` |
| T7 | 59,914 | 15.6% | 3.3% | **English** (definitions) |
| T6 | 25,079 | 10.1% | 35.6% | **Thao** ✓ `SOURCE_FONTS` |
| T5 | 6,224 | 3.0% | 3.6% | no signal — carries single content words only |
| T8 / T9 | 1,670 / 14,018 | ~4% | ~3% | headwords: content words only, no signal |
| T10 / T11 | 3,012 / 10,345 | 0% | 0% | delimiters, numbers, labels |

Corroborates the mapping where the data has power; **silent, not contradictory**, for fonts
that only ever carry one content word.

⚠️ **Fragility worth naming:** `T9` is both `SUBENTRY_FONT` and `FOOTNOTE_MARKER_FONT` —
one font name, two roles, told apart only by "is it a bare digit sitting higher than the
line". A positional heuristic on top of an undocumented font table.

⏳ Offered, not built: a test asserting T4 is English-dominant and T6 Thao-dominant, which
would catch a future font remap the way nothing does today.

## 2026-09-10 (round 9) — VERIFIED: the scrape loses nothing; copy-paste does

The maintainer pasted the last paragraph of printed p.6 from a PDF viewer, showing scrambled
order, character-spaced runs, `fth` for `fifth`, **and whole phrases missing** — and asked
whether the extraction could really be coming off that PDF without OCR.

### The pipeline reproduces the real text exactly
Fed printed p.6 through `page_rows()` / `join_spans()` / `decode_type3()`:

```
At present the dating of the Taiwan Neolithic to the late fifth millen-
nium hangs precariously on a single radiocarbon date of circa 6,300 B.P. from
the site of Pa-chia-ts'un near Tainan (K.C. Chang 1969, Bellwood 1997), but
the general chronology assumed here fits with the larger archaeological picture
from southeastern China and accords with the deep and fundamental diversity
among the Formosan languages.
```

Normalized word-level comparison against the maintainer's "actual text": **IDENTICAL**.
Nothing is missing from the text layer — a viewer's copy-paste follows *content-stream
order*, which is what drops and scrambles.

### Whole-book proof that clustering loses no glyph
Compared the character multiset of naive `get_text()` against position-aware clustering,
**all 1,117 pages**: 1,578,761 vs 1,576,957 characters. 685 pages differ — and the
difference is **entirely the accent overlay**:

```
PDF p.41   only in naive order : {'a': 2, 'u': 4}      ← accent glyph orphaned and lost
           only in clustering  : {'á': 2, 'ú': 4}      ← accent composed onto its vowel
```

**685 pages differ, all 685 contain `\x13` (the accent glyph), 0 differ without it.**
So clustering never loses a glyph; it *recovers* 1,804 accents naive order drops.

### No OCR anywhere
`requirements.txt` is PyMuPDF + lxml. No tesseract/easyocr/paddle/textract/pdf2image
installed or imported. `pdf_text.py` is 161 lines doing: y-clustering into visual rows,
x-sort within a row, a 2.2pt gap test that rejoins TeX's split words (`radio carb on` →
`radiocarbon`), positional accent-overlay handling, ligature decode, line-break
de-hyphenation.

**Keep this:** the assistant's *scraping* was genuinely sophisticated. What it never did was
**validate the result** — which is why every failure in this audit was silent. The lesson is
not "the scrape is untrustworthy" but "nothing asserted the scrape was right".

## 2026-09-10 (round 8) — provenance proven; 2 decode gaps found; the two entry formats identified

Dev repo `explore/entry-grammar` @ `ccd2a24`. **The maintainer's skepticism about the
scrape was well placed and found a real gap.**

### Provenance, proven not asserted
- `CodeAndDocs/[OA] Thao Dictionary.pdf` and `Private/…` are the **same inode** (22375310),
  SHA-256 `bd769bc6…`, 6,046,093 bytes, 1,117 pages — matching `source-lock.json` exactly.
- **The font names are the PDF's own, not mine.** `page.get_fonts()` on PDF p.290 declares
  nine **Type 3** fonts literally named `T4`…`T12`; PDF p.301 declares **TrueType**
  `BookAntiqua`, `CourierNewPS-*`, `Century`, `PMingLiU` with `WinAnsiEncoding`.
- **Yes, it needs a great deal of repair.** Raw `get_text()` on p.290:
  `pish{tubu`, `bu\x0balo\nes`, `\x0csh?`, `mo\x0ccation`, `mark\ner`, `sw\neet`,
  `p\notato\nes` — TeX Type-3 output with no usable ToUnicode. `decode_type3` is that repair.
- **And p.301 needs none:** raw text is already
  `ana-i iza sa m-ihu shapa wa hulus / Give me your leather jacket`. Which is exactly why it
  is a replacement page and why it was invisible.

### 🔴 Two decode gaps the challenge exposed
The italic face **T10** has two glyphs with no ToUnicode that came back as ordinary letters:
- **`j` = `|`**, the bar bracketing a headword. Proof: the running head of every Type-3 page
  reads `jacayj` where the re-typeset p.291 prints `|anak|` in the same position.
- **`!` = `→`**, the cross-reference arrow (`→punuq:2`).

They cannot be fixed in `decode_type3` (font-blind; `j` is a real letter in `Lujan`).
`repair_span_text()` applies them per span; the bar uses a private-use sentinel because
`decode_type3` maps a literal `|` to the em dash it is in every other face.
✅ **Neither ever reached the published XML** — T10 is neither an example nor a translation
font (`|`=0, `→`=0 in FORM/TRANSL/PHON).

### The bar IS the format discriminator
With it, `entry_grammar.py` reduces **2,046 of 2,144 main entries — 95.4%** — to exactly the
maintainer's two formats:

| | entries | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **A** `WORD [XF] definition …` | 1,536 | 71.6% |
| **B** `\|WORD\|: N. var [XF] def …` | 510 | 23.8% |

Residue **98 entries / 48 signatures**, named with page in
`CodeAndDocs/entry-format-residue.tsv`. Largest: **13 entries reducing to a bare `HEAD`** —
a headword whose whole body was attributed elsewhere; first thing to look at.

✅ **Resolves round 7's open question.** `HEAD SENSE+ NUM` was *not* sub-entries mis-typed as
headwords — it is a real format-A shape. What had been mis-typed is the citation `|word|`
*inside* a definition, which `_reduce_cite` now folds back into its definition.

⏳ Next: emit one JSON per entry against the format-A / format-B schema, and treat every
missing or unexpected field as a parse defect — the maintainer's approach, per format.

## 2026-09-10 (round 7) — printed p.291 was invisible; parenthetical tooling; entry grammar

**Artifact:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/969648aa-38bb-49f4-8053-c10276571d7d
Dev repo `fix/policy-conformance` @ `2a76257` (12 commits) + `explore/entry-grammar` @ `ac42b67`.
FormosanBank: `feature/parentheticals` @ `206dd6e43` (3rd branch). All UNPUSHED.

### 🔴 The p.290 splice was a symptom: **printed p. 291 is typeset in a different font family**
Book Antiqua with Courier hyphens, not the Type 3 faces. **Every classification in
`extract_source.py` is by font name, so the page was invisible** — all 14 of its examples
unextracted, and the record open when it began survived across it and absorbed the first
translation on printed p. 292. It is the **only** dictionary page like this (census of all
1,117 PDF pages; the pp. 1070+ block is the out-of-scope English–Thao index).

`FONT_ALIASES` maps the family onto the roles (bold-italic/italic → Thao example, plain →
English, bold → sub-entry) and rewrites the Courier hyphen as an en dash so `append_wrapped`
does not eat a line-final morpheme hyphen. **Two hardcoded thresholds became measurements**
— the page sets its columns ~15pt right of every other, which cut every translation in its
right column short and made each new example read as more of the previous translation.
Nothing outside p.291 changed.

⚠️ **Guard added, as asked:** a dictionary page carrying text but none of it in a
recognized font now **raises**, naming the fonts found. Blank pages exempt.

    examples 8,354 → 8,368   S 8,803 → 8,818   W 55,687 → 55,788   M 74,248 → 74,391
    source coverage 0.107% unaccounted (15 of 14,071) — **no example among them**

### Parenthetical tooling (`QC/utilities/parentheticals.py`, new branch)
Both maintainer rules, in shared code, 23 tests:
- **paired** — equal non-zero counts on the two sides ⇒ same subject, not translator's
  notes. `split_in_step()` expands the translation with the source, so the out-variant of
  `azazak (sa pagka)` / `a child (a chair)` no longer says "a chair". **28 records.**
- **note** — an opening marker (`lit.` `answer to` `said` `viz.` `e.g.`) or, unpaired, ≥6
  words. **484 TRANSL now carry @notes** (170 literal + 314 source notes); before, only the
  170 `(lit.` ones were found. V122 4,878 → 4,267.
- **inline** — 1,642 translations keep a parenthesis (supplied words, short naturalistic).
  ⚠️ **`(pl.)`/`(incl.)` deliberately stay inline** — attached to a pronoun; "We (incl.)
  are early" loses its sense without it.

Census behind the thresholds: 64.3% ≤2 words · 15.5% marker-initial · 5.7% long-no-marker ·
13.4% 3–5 words · 1.2% paired.

### Entry grammar (`explore/entry-grammar`, exploratory)
**Does the code work this way? No.** `extract_source.py` is a streaming font/position
heuristic that never asserts what it read was a well-formed entry — which is exactly why
every failure this audit found was silent.

`entry_grammar.py` reduces the span sequence against:

    ENTRY = HEAD [ETY] SENSE+
    SENSE = [NUM] [SUB] [LBL] DEF [BODY] [NOTE] (XREF NUM?)*
    BODY  = (EX TR)+

**1,988 of 2,132 main entries (93.2%)** reduce to `HEAD SENSE` / `HEAD SENSE+` — the
maintainer's two formats. 52 signatures total; **residue 144 entries / 49 signatures**,
named with page in `CodeAndDocs/entry-format-residue.tsv`.

⏳ The biggest shape, `HEAD SENSE+ NUM` (528, 24.8%), ends with a sense number whose sense
was attributed to the *next* entry — because **some sub-entries are typeset at the column
margin in the headword face** and "bold at margin" cannot tell them apart. Needs a look at
the printed page to decide whether the grammar or the typing is wrong.

⚠️ **`p0881-e009` — the maintainer corrected me, not the curation.** The alternation is

**The resolver had proposed exactly that; my prose in the report was the error.** Worth

All eight corrected in `slash-alternatives.json` and rebuilt. **W 55,670 → 55,687,
M 74,221 → 74,248**, S unchanged at 8,803, 0 HARD, 39/39 dev tests pass.

### Tests (maintainer asked for these explicitly)
- `tests/utilities/test_slash_alternative_rulings.py` — all eight as regression cases,
  **four assertions each (32)**: `resolve_scope` reproduces the ruling, `audit` reports the
  wrong curation, `audit` accepts the ruled reading, no ruled reading repeats a word.

  `test_visually_reviewed_slash_scopes`, **which had enshrined two of these wrong scopes as
  reviewed and correct**.

### Resolver fix — six of eight were already right; the two misses shared one cause
Material printed on **both** sides of the slash, in two shapes, both producing a reading
that repeats a word:
- `ma-pitu-'un iza nak a qamishan / yaku a qamishan` — `a qamishan` printed twice, read as
  a one-sided suffix → `... nak a qamishan a qamishan`
- `kan qca-i / kan p-acay-i ihu` — `kan` heads both alternants → `... kan kan p-acay-i ihu`

Three changes to `_affix_scope`: strip material printed on both sides before enumerating
and re-attach it; **reject any candidate whose reading repeats a word** (the only available
signal for the second shape); and rank the **balanced** candidate before the shortest —
`kan qca-i`/`kan p-acay-i` beats the shorter lopsided `kan qca-i`/`kan`.

`audit-curation` now returns **8 SA005** (was 16) + 12 SA006. The 8 are Blust printing two

rule cannot narrow. ⏳ The **12 SA006** (readings sharing one slashed translation) are open.

## 2026-09-10 (round 5) — both discards diagnosed and recovered; the parenthetical census

**Artifact (updated in place):** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/969648aa-38bb-49f4-8053-c10276571d7d
Dev repo `fix/policy-conformance` @ `d359dab` (9 commits). Corpus now **8,803 S / 55,670 W /
74,221 M**. 39/39 tests pass. `extracted-records.json` reports **no discards at all**.

### 1. Printed p.835 — the text WAS in the scrape; it was misclassified
The example's English (`I never see the dog`) is set in the **definition face T7**, not the
example-translation face T4, and the T7 admission rule required a T4 span on the same row.
**Swept all 789 pages for that exact shape — exactly one row has it**, so the failure cost
one example and could not have cost more. Recovered as `blust-dict-p0835-e006`; ids on that
page shift by one from e006.

⚠️ **The naive fix broke two other records.** Admitting every definition-face-only row also
absorbed definition text into `blust-dict-p0399-e015` ("as in walking") and `-p0461-e010`
("common in serial verb constructions:"). Row shape alone cannot tell an example's
translation from a definition continuing over a line; what distinguishes them is whether an
example is open **and still has no translation**. That test lives in the caller, so the run
is now *tagged* rather than classified and `extract_dictionary` decides.

### 2. Printed p.905 — an entry with four parts, the fourth discarded
`shdu uan sa tumbush ma-qitan sakp-in` / `Clothes lice are easy to catch` /
`(lit. Clothes lice are easy to be caught)` / `(recorded with [duwan] for what I take to be
shdu uan)`. The first three were handled; the fourth was cut by a hardcoded `(recorded`
split and thrown away. It is Blust's transcription note, so it now becomes the record's
`source_note` → `FORM/@notes`. **Both parentheticals of that entry now survive, in the two
different places they belong.**

### 3. How parentheticals are handled — the census
**2,431 parentheticals across 8,519 translations**; 2,082 translations carry one.
- `(lit. …)` **195** → `TRANSL/@notes`. **Complete**: no `(Lit.` or `(literally` spellings
  exist to miss, and no translation carries two.
- `(recorded …)` **1** → `FORM/@notes` (new this round).
- everything else **2,235** stays inline. Not one thing:
  - **~800 supply a word the Thao lacks** — `(and)` ×593, `(it)` ×53, `(they)` ×28,
    `(him)` ×27, `(he)` ×24, `(them)` ×19, `(I)` ×17, `(we)` ×15. Ordinary practice.
  - **naturalistic elaboration** — POL-024 says explicitly not to flag these.
  - ⏳ **~120 are usage/elicitation metadata** — `(answer to …)` ×28, `(said, e.g., in
    anger …)` ×26, `(e.g. …)` ×37, `(pl.)` ×23, `(of inquiries about …)` ×7. Neither a
    literal paraphrase nor naturalistic elaboration. **POL-024 names two classes; this is a
    third, and it is unruled.**

⏳ **POL-026 gap the census exposed:** where the Thao has an optional `(x)`, both expanded
sentences take the same English *including its own parenthetical*. `yaku m-agqaqili sa
azazak (sa pagka)` / `I was carrying a child (a chair) on my hip` → the out-variant has no
`sa pagka` but still says "a chair". **32 of the 179** optional records have a translation
parenthetical at all; some plainly need no split (`ata (tu) karkar-i` / `Don't chew (it)!` —
unrelated parentheses). Per-record judgement.

### 4. New test: translation coverage → 2 spliced records
Ran the coverage test on the English side (is a record's translation on the page it
claims?): **2 of 8,353** have a tail from elsewhere — `blust-dict-p0290-e012`
*"Give me money starting their own families)"* and `-p0399-e015`. Cause: the open record
survives a page boundary (which it must — a two-column entry legitimately continues on the
next page), and printed p.291 has no examples at all, so the next translation-face run met
belonged to a different entry. **Left unfixed and recorded** — the guard needs more than a
page-boundary flush and the population is two.

## 2026-09-10 (round 4) — ❗ NOT RULED (corrected 2026-09-11): Thao /f/ as [f], not [ɸ]

> **Correction, 2026-09-11.** This entry was headed *RULED*. It records no
> question from the maintainer and no answer in their words, unlike every
> other ruling here, and asked directly the maintainer said **"I don't recall
> agreeing to that."** I cannot produce their agreement, so there is none:
> the change is a **proposal**, `feature/thao-f-labiodental` is held unpushed,
> and nothing may depend on it. What follows is the case for it, not a decision.

**Artifact (updated in place):** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/969648aa-38bb-49f4-8053-c10276571d7d
FormosanBank `feature/thao-f-labiodental` @ `eec92f0a8` (off `main`, independent of
`feature/slash-alternatives-and-quote-parity`). Dev repo `fix/policy-conformance` @ `4d9d1a4`
(7 commits). All UNPUSHED.

**Ruling.** `Orthographies/Ortho113/Thao.tsv` maps `f → f`. Follows Blust, who collected
the data: p.18 lists the symbols whose values are NOT customary as exactly `' g c sh z lh`
and /f/ is not among them; p.41 gives the value — *"The phonemes /f/, /s/, /sh/, and /h/
are voiceless fricatives — labiodental [f], dental [θ], palatal [ʃ], and glottal [h]"*.
More recent orthographies write [ɸ]. Test `test_thao_f_is_labiodental` cites both pages.

**Blast radius (measured, not estimated).** Ortho113 is Thao's designated standard, so this
changes the *standard* PHON of every Thao corpus: **5,554 PHON elements carrying 8,298
occurrences of ɸ** — ILRDF_Dicts 2,486, ePark 2,978, Li-Conjunction-Thao 50,
Presidential_Apologies 40. **No other language's table uses ɸ at all**, so nothing outside
Thao moves. Those tiers regenerate on each corpus's next pipeline run; not rewritten here
(corpus data → own PR per corpus).

⚠️ **Left alone deliberately:** `Orthographies/{Ortho94,MinEd,Li}/Thao.tsv` also map
`f → ɸ` and are the *source* profiles behind original PHON — Li-Conjunction-Thao builds
its original PHON with the Li profile. Each states its own document's analysis and I have
not read those documents. All three carry the identical value, which looks more like one
copied default than three independent analyses. **Worth checking against their sources.**

**Caveat recorded** in the corpus README's `Notes and Issues` (and flagged for the GitBook
page when one is written), quoting Blust for the value *and* its instability: *"In casual
speech /f/ is commonly pronounced as [h], as in /fukish/ [fukiʃ], [hukiʃ] 'head hair' … It
is likely that /f/ to /h/ is a sound change in progress, as it has begun to produce
hypercorrect forms from bases which earlier had /h/."* He also records /f/ heard as /u/ or
/lhu/. The note says explicitly that **neither PHON tier represents any of that variation**
— both give the citation form.

Corpus rebuilt against the corrected table: 4,248 lines change, **0 ɸ remain**, standard
and original PHON agree again. 37/37 dev-repo tests pass.

- `extract_source.py --check` → **Extraction matches extracted-records.json** (4.2 s).
- **Coverage:** 16 of 14,044 Thao source-font runs on printed pp.280-1068 unaccounted

### 🔴 Three NEW defects only the source could reveal — all FIXED (`d2fb6b3`)
1. **Italic glosses were dropped.** The gloss line uses T10 (italic) where Blust leaves a
   Thao word untranslated; the aligner took only T3/T11. `funfun,`→None, `funfun.`→'.',
   `funfun?'`→"?'." . 13 glosses corrected, 4 words gained one, V065 29→25.
2. **Footnotes were never read.** The row filter needs T3/T11/T12; a footnote carries
   T8/T9/T10. Three exist across the five texts, now on `TRANSL/@notes` at the W:
   `funfun,` = "the fruit of the tree Castanopsis indica.", `Zintun` = "Sun-Moon Lake.",
   `kintuktuku,`/`kintunaway,`/`pakalhuri,` = "kinds of snails". A marker sits to the
   RIGHT of its gloss, so it attaches to the last token starting at or before it.
3. **`/f/` was wrong.** Blust p.41: "/f/, /s/, /sh/, and /h/ are voiceless fricatives —
   **labiodental [f]**, dental, palatal, glottal". The profile had `f → ɸ`.
   **1,379 original PHON tiers corrected.**

### Rulings applied
- **Item 1 (`Tongpú`)** — no `standardize.py` change, as instructed. Noted that the
  result is not "unaddressed" but *rewritten* (`Tonngpu`, PHON `t*nŋpu`, 4 sentences);
  a corpus-local `ng → ng` conversion row would neutralise it without shared code.
- **Item 3 (14 mid-quotation translations)** — traced to the page: the opening backtick
  **is not in the PDF text layer at all** (a ~6pt gap, no span). Not an extractor bug.
  No data repair made; `quote_parity` detects them (22 records) so a repair can be
  evidence-driven.

### Built
- **Q1** `QC/utilities/slash_alternatives.py` — `resolve_scope()` (morpheme tier →
  translation slash → ranked shared prefix/suffix) + `audit()` with 7 rules. Over the 92
  curated records: **0 HARD, 28 SOFT** (16 uneven substitutions incl. all 8 real ones,
  12 shared slashed translations). Word-order variants suppressed by a containment test.
  13 tests.
- **Q4** `quote_parity()` in `classify_quotes.py`. **It helps a lot:** `form_unopened`
  goes 40 → **2** once the attestation dictionary is passed, and those 2 are exactly
  `t05s018`/`t05s051`. Isolates all 6 `form_unclosed` and 22 `transl_unopened`. 7 tests.
- **Q6** `CodeAndDocs/extract_entries.py` — **1,873 main entries, 14,836 sub-entry
  headwords, 16,927 definitions, 7,695 labels, 256 PAN/PMP etymologies** →
  `entry-records.json` (2.9 MB). Nothing in the XML uses it yet. ⏳ `source-lock.json`
  still excludes "dictionary definitions" from the authorized scope — needs your ruling.
- **Q9** W/M tiers: **2,542 → 55,666 W, 0 → 74,215 M**. ⚠️ `validate_glosses` 35 → **127,379
  SOFT** (127,364 are V064/V065), XML **5.2 MB → 38 MB**, and V061 finds 9 words whose
  cleaned FORM has a dash the M tier lacks — the source's nine em-dashes, flattened by POL-011.

### Explained
- **Q2** a T4/T5/T6 span = PyMuPDF's unit of text in one font; the extractor uses font
  name as its only signal (T8 headword, T9 sub-entry, T11 sense number, T7 definition,
  T5/T6 Thao example, T4 English, T10 italic). **Asterisks DO exist in the source** — in
  T7, as PAN reconstructions `(PAN *aCay ...)`. POL-016/017 hold by scope, not by rule.
- **Q3** text-layer scrape, no OCR; the junk is Type-3 custom encoding, mapped by
  `decode_type3` (`\x0c`→fi, `\x12`→θ, `\x13`+vowel→accent, `{|\"`→`–—""`).
  ⚠️ The map does **not** cover Blust's IPA: `ʔ ŋ ʃ ð ɬ` come back as `? n s d " l"`.
- **Q7** `y0 < 685` = distance in points from the page top; the footnote at y=657.8 was
  **inside** the band — my earlier guess was wrong. It was the T3/T11/T12 row filter.
- **Q8** validator design: rate-based per file like V143; only tokens attested in one
  language and absent from the other; score contiguous runs of 3+ at an edge, not single
  tokens; exclude parenthesised material (all 6 false positives were POL-024
  parentheticals). Depends on `attestation.txt`.
- **Q13** ⚠️ **You were right and I had it backwards** — listing an accented letter
  *protects* it from the shared stripper. The four rows are removed; `_accents.py` does
  the work; PHON unchanged. Blust p.18's exception list is exactly `' g c sh z lh`, the
  complement of your list, so `g = ŋ` confirmed and **`f` is not an exception**.

### ⏳ OPEN
- **`Ortho113/Thao.tsv` still maps `f → ɸ`** while the Blust profile now says `f`. Standard

### 🔴 Four NEW defects found while answering
1. **`Tongpú` → `Tonngpu`.** The conversion rule `g→ng` rewrites the `g` inside the

### Answers worth keeping
- **Q2** zero `*` anywhere in 8,519 records — but by *font scope*, not by an exclusion
  rule. Widening the scope would need one added.
- **Q3** text-layer scrape (PyMuPDF `get_text("dict")`), **no OCR**; Type-3 custom
  encoding is what makes it look like OCR.
- **Q4** Blust's `` ` ``…`'` quotation is well evidenced: 154 of 195 records have
  matching opener counts in the Thao and its English. Only `` ` `` (176) and `'` (1121)
  occur. 40 of the 45 unbalanced Thao records are the lexical glottal `riu'`/`qriu'`.
- **Q5** **eight** grammatical gloss labels, not four: SA 252, LIG 141, TU 62, FUT 48,
  DAI 10, NA 5, YA 4, TI 1. 372 hyphenated gloss tokens / 250 distinct — but
  `Tou-she`, `we-excl.`, `New-Year.` are real English hyphens, so no blanket replace.
- **Q6** no headwords; the extractor *detects* them (fonts T8/T9) and discards the text.
  Recoverable in ~10 lines, needs a re-run. ⏳ scope call: authorization says "texts and
  example sentences", excludes "definitions" — a headword is neither.
- **Q8** built the Thao/English boundary test both directions: **zero real hits**
  (every hit is Thao `but`, or Blust's own `(cicu = the dog)` citations).
- **Q9** the policy is **POL-023**; gloss-less M is sanctioned (V064 SOFT, "reported,
  never fatal"). Building W/M from the hyphens: 2,542 W → **55,666 W**, 0 M → **76,563 M**.
- **Q10 — your procedure works, and the answer is clean.** Presidential_Apologies'
  132 hyphens are **100% Sinitic transliteration** (`guan-cu-min-cok`, `cing-hu`,
  `kok-ka`); ILRDF's 39 split into transliterations + morpheme leakage; **Blust has
  zero loanword hyphens** — all 16,644 are morpheme boundaries, and he writes `Tongpú`
  unhyphenated. Attestation test: STRIP 1,672 types/10,149 tokens; KEEP 5 types — and
  all 5 are ILRDF's own leakage, so the genuine KEEP set is **empty**.
- **Q11 — I was wrong in round 1.** Ortho113 lists `aa ia ui ai ii uu au iu ua` as
  vowel sequences, so `naak`/`kmaan`/`shduu` ARE conformant. Recommend **no** glide
  conversion rule: Blust argued `y`/`w` are phonemic with contrast evidence. What
  survives is that ILRDF/ePark carry *both* spellings in one standard tier (POL-002).
- **Q13** accent stripping is **already** the shared `QC/utilities/_accents.py` (same
  module standardize imports); the `á í ú ó` rows are its input, not a fork. Customary
  values: 14/16 agree. **`g` = /ŋ/ is proven by the data** — `g` ×1227 almost always
  before a velar/uvular (`mi-lhugqu`, `pagqa`, `magkaci`), and `ng` occurs 4 times
  total, all in `Tongpú`. ⏳ `f`: table says `ɸ`, Blust's list says `f` — but
  `Ortho113/Thao.tsv` also says `ɸ`, so change both or neither.

`62b42b118`. New corpus: Blust 2003 *Thao Dictionary* (Academia Sinica OA PDF) —
13 files, 8,802 S / 2,542 W / 0 M / 11,317 TRANSL / 22,688 PHON, 55,666 tokens,
`ssf` + `dialect="Thao"`. Would grow Thao 102,042 → 157,708 tokens (**+55%**).
Nothing modified in the dev repo or in `Corpora/`.

### Verified good

- **Zero HARD findings** from `validate_xml` / `validate_text` / `validate_glosses`.
  SOFT: V133 ×8,005 (hyphens — see F8), V122 ×4,878 (all in English TRANSL, POL-024),

  `standardize` → `add_phonology`; 13/13 files `cmp`-equal to the committed XML.

  `expanded-records.json`: 7,867 dash-only, 765 identical, 129+35+6 quote-glyph.
- **POL-016/017 clean** — zero `*` in the 8,519 extracted records and in the XML.

### 🔴 Blocks a port PR

| # | finding | policy |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | `regenerate.py --formosanbank` hash-pins a second checkout to `3a3c47c22` and **hard-exits** against `main` (5 of 9 locked files moved) — while producing identical output. Delete the lock; add `provenance.json`. | POL-048, POL-052 |
| F2 | `@copyright` = 96 chars of free text, not `CC BY-NC 4.0`. V160/V161 aren't implemented so nothing caught it. Grant is time-limited to 2034-01-31 — CC can't express that. | POL-042 |
| F3 | No `generate_xml.sh`, no `provenance.json`, no `## Rights` block, no `Notes and Issues`. | POL-044/047/052/055 |
| F4 | `normalize_blust_quotes()` forks `classify_quotes.py`, because **Thao has no `reference/Thao/attestation.txt`** (one of 4 languages whose empty dict was deleted). | POL-046 |

### Data findings (bounded worklists)

- **F5 — 8 sentences with an unpaired quote.** Blust's quotations span sentence
  boundaries; the normalizer is sentence-scoped and returns early with no backtick.
  Openers: `blust-dict-p0772-e005`, `-p0804-e019`, `-p1018-e013`,
  `blust-text-t05-s033`, `-s049`, `-s097`. Orphan closers: `blust-text-t05-s018`,
  `-s051`. (41 of the 43 remaining word-final `'` are the genuine root `riu'`/`qriu'`.)
- **F6 — example density trough**, pp. 555–629 at 3.1/page vs 10.6 mean. An
  alphabetical trace identifies it as the `m-` prefix section (cross-reference
  headwords). Probably benign; one look at printed pp. 580/610 settles it.
- **F7 — 23 PHON with `*`**, all `e`/`o` in loanwords/names (`Kiutsok`, `Bob`,
  `Toalu`, `iseng`) — Ortho113 Thao has 3 vowels. Original PHON is better than
  standard PHON here.
- **F8 — V133 isn't language-aware.** C012 deliberately keeps Thao hyphens; V133
  flags all 8,005 anyway.
- **F9 — two silent discards** in `extract_source.py`: records with no translation,
  and translations truncated at `(recorded…`. Neither counted.

### How it compares to existing Thao

Character rates match ILRDF/ePark within ±15% on every phoneme letter; **no new
characters**, and none of the incumbents' Cyrillic/Han junk. One outlier: `-` at
64.0 per 1,000 chars vs 0.2 (ILRDF) / 1.5 (ePark). Type overlap ladder:
14.8% → **38.2% de-hyphenated** → 41.1% glide-folded; new-token coverage
66.5% → **84.7%** → **87.8%**. Only 2 duplicate sentences (vs ePark).

⚠️ **Finding against the bank, not the port:** ILRDF_Dicts and ePark ship
`iaku`/`yaku`, `ianan`/`yanan`, `thau`/`thaw`, `naak`/`nak`, `izai`/`izay`,
`kmaan`/`kman` side by side in their *standard* tiers. `Ortho113/Thao.tsv` declares
`y`, `w`, `i a u` only — no i-glide, no u-glide, no long vowels. The new corpus is
the conformant one.

### ⏳ OPEN — five calls

1. Do Blust's morpheme hyphens stay in the standard tier? (30% of tokens)
2. Confirm POL-026/027 expansion for dictionary examples (283 derived sentences,
   identical translations)?
3. Repair the 8 broken quotations — extractor fix, `manual_edits.xml`, or document?
4. Does `Ortho113/Thao.tsv` gain `e` and `o`? (registry change → own PR)
5. Open an issue for the ILRDF/ePark glide inconsistency?

### Not verified

No network here: the PDF was never opened (`download_source.py` timed out, `Private/`
empty). The audit covers `build_xml.py` + the shared cleaners, **not** the PDF
extraction. The repo's `source-fidelity-review.json` samples 11 locations across 789

regions" — vacuous. Nothing counts the source. `test_extraction` and `test_xml` error
here; `test_source_lock` and `test_expansion` pass. **Before port:** run

## 2026-09-10 — Maintainer: combine the three into ONE PR. Done — `corpus/gitbook-paiwan-followups`.

*"Is it possible to merge those branches locally to each other then push and
merge a single branch via PR? … it's very time-consuming to do so many PRs in
order."* — **Yes, and it is done.**

### ⚠️ POL-049 note, decided rather than dodged

POL-049 says a corpus PR does not change shared code; shared changes get their
own PR **merged first**. Its stated rationale is (a) a shared change gets
*buried* in a big corpus diff and (b) it *couples merge order*. **Neither holds
here:** the combined diff is **5 files / 83 insertions**, and combining
*removes* the merge-order coupling instead of creating it. Maintainer's call,
taken explicitly (POL-050 spirit) and stated in the PR body so it is visible
rather than drift — not a precedent for burying shared changes in real corpus
diffs.

### The branch

`corpus/gitbook-paiwan-followups`, off `origin/main` (`13133170f`), 0 behind,
worktree `…/scratchpad/wt-B`. Merge noise flattened to **three linear commits**,
one per concern, so it still reviews as three things:

```
93d5394ad clean_xml: --warnings_dir keeps the per-run report out of published XML/
912848d72 FormosanBankGitBook: keep the cleaner report out of published XML/
9e08ddefe Correct the Paiwan GitBook README's coverage and notes
```

Files: `QC/cleaning/clean_xml.py`, `tests/cleaners/test_cleaner_warnings_dir.py`,
`Corpora/FormosanBankGitBook/CodeAndDocs/generate_xml.sh`,
`Corpora/FormosanBankGitBook/CodeAndDocs/.gitignore`,
`Corpora/FormosanBankGitBook/README.md`.

### The payoff of combining: verified as one tree

A full `generate_xml.sh` run now leaves **`git status` completely empty** —
report in `CodeAndDocs/`, nothing in `XML/`, all six XML files byte-identical.
Before this branch the build always left an untracked `XML/cleaner_warnings.csv`.
That end-to-end check was not possible while the flag and its use sat in two
PRs waiting on each other.

The three single-purpose branches (`feat/clean-xml-warnings-dir`,
`corpus/gitbook-paiwan-warnings-dir`, `docs/gitbook-paiwan-readme-corrections`)
are kept locally in case the PR needs splitting after all.

reverted **all** of Hunter's prose. Correct resolution here was per-file:

## 2026-09-10 — PR #159: how the GitBook tables update (answer: by hand), and the two red checks

**Report (rev 4), §08:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/967d0a65-7041-4e29-af7a-293d17e1dbfc

### How and when the stats tables update — verified, not remembered

| What | Who | When | Checked? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FormosanBank/statistics/*.csv`, history, PNG | `corpus-metrics.yaml` | **automatic**, push to `main`, auto-commits | it *is* the generator |
| GitBook corpus-page stats block | `update_corpus_stats.py` **by hand** | whenever someone remembers | ❌ **nothing** |
| GitBook aggregate tables in `corpora/README.md` | same script, same run | same | ❌ **nothing** |
| 4 wiring points (page/nav/list/stats-map) | `manage_corpus_pages.py` | at publication | ✅ `corpus-page-lint.yaml --strict` |
| `policies.md`, audio-permissions page | `sync_upstream_docs.py` | on upstream change | ✅ `tests.yaml` / `test_upstream_doc_sync.py` |
| Page prose (Copyright / Processing / Notes) | a human | whenever | ❌ nothing |

`manage_corpus_pages.py` says so itself: the stats block is *"auto-filled by
update_corpus_stats.py … not edited here"*, and its `CheckResult` marks stats
issues `informational (separate pipeline)`. **The lint that runs cannot see stale
numbers.** No workflow invokes `update_corpus_stats.py`; it is a plain script with
one flag (`--stats-dir`, default sibling `../FormosanBank/statistics`).

### 🐛 Consequence: 4 pages are stale on GitBook HEAD *right now*

Ran it in a throwaway worktree against FormosanBank HEAD, before #159 merges:
`HundredPaiwanTexts.md` (1), `NTUFormosanCorpus.md` (14), `corpora/README.md` (26),
`huteson-rukai-survey.md` (8), `ntu-paiwan-asr.md` (4). `FormosanBankGitBook.md`
is correctly at 1,855.

⏳ Suggest a `--check` mode on `update_corpus_stats.py` wired into
`corpus-page-lint.yaml` (which already checks out FormosanBank) — turns a habit
into a red build. **Own PR, not #159.**

### What #159 needs on the GitBook

CSV: `pwn,Eastern,…,1855,1855,1855,6,102,0,0,204,0,0` → `…,2007,2007,2007,6,105,0,0,210,0,0`.
Script then rewrites the page (Word count / English / Mandarin 1,855 → 2,007) and
6 numbers in `corpora/README.md` (Paiwan 422,594 → 422,746; per-corpus column
60,118 → 60,270; eng/zho rows to match). Prose, by hand: `## Copyright` →
`CC BY-NC 4.0`; `## Corpus Processing` `make_xml.sh` → `generate_xml.sh` +
provenance link; `Corpus Notes` → `Notes and Issues`; and say the source is
`Website PWN-v1.2.pdf` **and why** (§07). Plus the two pwn-page fixes.
**Order:** merge FormosanBank → let `corpus-metrics.yaml` commit the CSV →
*then* run the script. #159 touches no policy text, so no `sync_upstream_docs.py`.

### The two red checks

- **`Rights Delta / compare-rights` — expected.** The POL-044 gate firing on
  `'CC-BY-NC' -> 'CC BY-NC 4.0'`. No bypass label by design; maintainer override
  is the only route. Nothing to fix.
- **`hf-audio-parity` — NOT #159. Re-run it.** The corpus has zero AUDIO
  elements. `git diff c5f6d1cef origin/main -- audio_sources.json audio_extras.json
  audio_permissions.json AUDIO-PERMISSIONS.md QC/validation/validate_hf_audio.py`
  is **empty**. The workflow only fires because the PR touches `Corpora/**/*.xml`;
  it then validates the whole org. `validate_hf_audio.py` passed locally on
  current `main` **and** on the merged tree (exit 0, *"Audio parity passed for all
  public audio datasets"*). Cause is almost certainly anonymous rate limiting:
  the script builds `HfApi(token=False)` and makes an unauthenticated
  `list_datasets` + a `list_repo_files` per public non-audio dataset/model/space —
  dozens of anonymous calls, **no retry, no backoff** — and the workflow sets
  `HF_TOKEN: ''` deliberately. My third consecutive local run timed out where the
  first two passed in seconds — **and the same command at the same commit,
  re-run after a pause, passed** (`Audio parity passed for all public audio
  datasets`, exit 0). So: `main` ✅, merged tree ✅, `c5f6d1cef` itself ✅.
  **Proven transient. Just re-run the check.** ⏳ Worth its own small PR
  (retry-with-backoff on 429, or authenticate the *listing* calls while keeping
  the anonymous *reachability* assertions anonymous). Not a #159 finding.

markdown **bullet lists**; `(ILRDF)` is lost because it sits outside the link
text (`[Indigenous Languages…](url) (ILRDF)`); `…a ziriu.(tja pacunan` is a
line-wrap artifact of `…a ziriu. ([tja pacunan…](url))`. And the markdown carries
**structure** — H1/H3/paragraph/list-item and link targets — that the PDF throws
away irrecoverably.

⏳ **The call:** #159 *entrenches* the PDF (pins it by SHA-256, builds
`source_audit.py` around it, README says the build needs "no network source
refresh"). Recommendation: source the Paiwan tier from `pwn/*.md` at a pinned
GitBook commit, keep the PDF as a corrections ledger via POL-030 manual edits,
and let markdown block structure carry S segmentation. **Honest counterweight:**
the pwn markdown still contains an untranslated stray —
`Anyone tjara pasusu tua kakudan nua FormosanBank…`, still on GitBook `HEAD`,
never fixed — which the PDF and the corpus do not. `Website PWN-v**1.2**.pdf`
looks like a later corrected deliverable from Xuan, so a naive markdown scrape
would import that defect. Don't swap one single-source story for another.

### ⏳ NEW F8 — `p5_languages` publishes English under `xml:lang="zho"`

Raised by the maintainer (*"That seems … not right?"*). **They are right, and my
first report got this wrong** — I called it "faithful to the source" because the
PDF's Mandarin column reprints the Latin list. It is faithful to the *PDF*, but
the Mandarin **edition of the site** translates every language name and has since
**2025-05-21** (`zh-TW/bei-jing/tai-wan-nan-dao-yu.md`, `a673e7d`):
`阿美語（Amis/Ami）` … `雅美語/達悟語（Yami/Tao，蘭嶼主要使用的語言）`.
The PDF predates the zh-TW edition, so its middle column had nothing to show.
21 tokens of English are now tagged `zho`. `p1_people` is the same in weaker
form: corpus `zho` = `主要的研究員有以下：Joshua Hartshorne…`, live Mandarin page
= `計畫主持人` / `諮詢委員會` with `宋麗梅`, `林川傑`, `阮玄`, `劉宇陽`.

### ⏳ NEW F9 — `p1_people` publishes "Advisory Board" as if it were a person

The Paiwan FORM runs `…Li-May Sung **Advisory Board** Chuan-Jie Lin…`. In the
English edition those are two labelled lists (`Principal Investigators` ×3,
`Advisory Board` ×5); the PDF column-flatten splices the heading inline.
`grep -rn "Advisory" pwn/` returns **nothing** — the Paiwan edition has one flat
list of eight and no group headings — so the published Paiwan sentence contains
an English phrase the Paiwan page does not have, counted as a Paiwan token.
Falls straight out of F7.

### ✅ F2 resolved by the markdown

The pwn page is headed `# kemuda itjen a pusaladj tua FormosanBank?` — that
string is the Paiwan **page title**, rendered as a question, so #159's pairing is
**correct**. The English page has `### **What must you do?**`; the Paiwan page has
no corresponding heading at all, so nothing was dropped in translation. Only the
README sentence is wrong: it should name `What must you do?` as the untranslated
heading, not `Contributing to FormosanBank`.

### 2026-09-11 — validators now see standard-tier variants; clean_filepaths guarded

Branch `fix/validators-see-variants` (`2af99a152`), full suite **1870 passed /
130 skipped**.

**Nine character-level standard-tier rules were checking the base FORM only** —
V110/V111/V112/V113/V114/V115 smart quotes, parens, repeated punct, dashes,
whitespace, quotes; plus V120 null, V126 equal-sign, V133 dash. All read through
`_s_standard_pairs` / `_s_standard_triples` / `_s_standard_form_text`, so one new
generator over every standard FORM fixed eight of them without touching a rule
body; V120 reads the tier directly and changed too.

**Deliberately not blanket.** A rule asking *"what does this sentence say?"* —
alignment, duplicate detection, tier-vs-tier comparison, PHON, counting — keeps
`find_base_form`, because a variant is a secondary reading and substituting it
changes the question. Still base-only: `_source_align`, `validate_audio`,
`validate_audio_quality`, `validate_duplicate_sentences`, the gloss rules, and
V123/V135/V140/V141. The split is per rule and the new generator's docstring
says why.

V126 2→4). WakelinTexts unchanged. Only those two corpora have standard-tier
variants at all — 216 FORMs across 25 files.

**`clean_filepaths.py` guarded** — the last tool that could damage data. It
`os.rename`s files, and `main` expands a corpora dir into its children, one being
CodeAndDocs; unguarded it would rename a POL-035 snapshot out from under the
ledger that references it.

Both test files verified to fail without their fix: 5 of 6 variant cases fail on

### 2026-09-11 — POL-059: published corpus layout (`XML/<Language>/`)

Ruled: **`XML/` is a directory at the corpus root, and every published XML has a
directory named for its language somewhere on its path below it** — the
`languages.csv` `Language` value, not the ISO code. Extra levels are fine on
either side: sub-corpora above (ePark, NTUFormosanCorpus), subdivisions of one
language below (`Safolu/XML/Amis/Safolu/`, `Siraya_Gospels/XML/Siraya/Matthew/`).

Branch `policy/corpus-layout-and-orthography-skip` (`bc9dac825`), same branch as
POL-058 — two branches both appending to the tail of POLICIES.md would conflict.

**Renames done in the same PR** (`c0004415a`) — the bank is now **14,571 of
14,571** conforming. `Glosbe/XML/{ami,tay,trv,xsy}` →
`{Amis,Atayal,Truku,Saisiyat}`; `HundredPaiwanStories/XML/*.xml` →
`XML/Paiwan/`. 108 pure renames, zero content change. **`trv` → Truku, not
Seediq** — the dialect attribute says Truku; the code alone would have filed it
wrongly.

**Statistics do not move** (maintainer asked): `corpus_counts` resolves language
from `xml:lang` + `dialect`, never from the path, so the per-(language, dialect)
aggregates are byte-identical before and after. Verified, not assumed.

**Three things depended on the old paths; a bare `git mv` would have broken all
three silently:**
- `Glosbe/CodeAndDocs/make_xml.sh` — 8 refs, passing each language dir to
  standardize/add_phonology with a different conversion table. Would have failed
  loudly, the benign case.
- `Glosbe/CodeAndDocs/quote_corrections.csv` — the durable POL-035 log; its
  `file` column named the moved files. 169 rows repointed, else the log cannot
  locate its own subjects and grows a second path convention on the next run.
- `QC/validation/find_missing_dialect.py` — non-recursive `glob('*.xml')` on a
  hardcoded path. After the move it matched **0 files and printed an all-clear**
  — the worst case. **Deleted rather than repaired** (`d20cc099b`), on the
  maintainer's call. It is superseded by **V036** (`text_dialect_valid`, HARD),
  which catches the same case *and* checks the dialect is valid for the language
  — verified side by side. Nothing called it; no test covered it; it arrived
  2026-03-15 in a HundredPaiwanStories commit with that corpus's path hardcoded
  and was never touched again. The current pair is V036 for enforcement and
  `validate_dialect.py` for the human read. Repairing it was my first instinct
  and the wrong one — it would have kept an uncalled, untested duplicate of a
  HARD rule alive to rot at the next layout change.

Validators after: HundredPaiwanStories 0 findings; Glosbe 4,157 V151 SOFT —
**identical to main**, pre-existing and unrelated.

~~Conformance measured before writing it: 14,463 of 14,571 files (99.3%).~~
Only two corpora depart:

| corpus | files | how |
|---|---:|---|
| HundredPaiwanStories | 100 | xml directly in `XML/`, no language dir |
| Glosbe | 8 | ISO codes — `XML/{ami,tay,trv,xsy}/` |

Those 8 Glosbe files are **exactly** the ones `orthography_extract` silently

### 2026-09-11 — `orthography_extract` path matching: two claims WITHDRAWN

*(Given its own heading because the maintainer went looking for "the path-regex
fix" and could not find it — it had been filed as "fix 2" inside the F2
discussion. Then they challenged both remaining claims, and were right about
both. Write-up rewritten:
`claudeplans/2026-09-10-orthography-extract-file-selection.md`.)*

`generate_corpus` matches the language name as a regex against the **directory
path** rather than against `xml:lang`/`dialect`. I claimed three consequences.
One was real; two were not.

- ✅ **Walks into `CodeAndDocs/`** — real, and **fixed in #242**. On Latham it
  read the POL-035 snapshot as well as the corpus: 296 characters instead of
  148, and a profile that changed *shape* because the duplicate pushed
  characters over the `>= 5` threshold.
- ❌ ~~**Pools unrelated corpora**~~ — **WITHDRAWN.** Siraya_Gospels,
  UtrechtManuscriptWordList and Latham-1862 each hold `XML/Siraya/` with Siraya
  text, and pooling them is *the intent*: `--corpus all` means all corpora, and
  a per-language reference profile is meant to draw on every corpus that has the
  language. I demonstrated it by walking `Corpora/` — which *is* the all-corpora
  mode — and called intended behaviour a bug. `--corpus <Name>` scopes, and works.
- ❌ ~~**Truku is unreachable**~~ — **WITHDRAWN.** The premise about the code is
  right, the conclusion about the data is wrong. 16 folders named `Truku` hold
  44 files, **all** resolving to Truku; 19 named `Seediq` hold 2,120, **all**
  Seediq. Across all **14,563** published files whose path matches some language
  name, **zero** resolve to a different language. The convention is kept
  perfectly.

**What actually survives: 8 files of 14,571**, all Glosbe, which lays out
`XML/{ami,tay,trv,xsy}` by **ISO code** where every other corpus uses the
language name — so `--language Amis` over all corpora silently omits Glosbe's
Amis file (3 Amis, 2 Atayal, 2 Saisiyat, 1 Truku).

⏳ **OPEN, small:** either fix the tool (select on `is_published_xml` +
`resolve_language`, which also makes `--by_dialect` honest, at the cost of
moving every profile) **or** rename Glosbe's four directories **or** decide
Glosbe's lexical/TM data does not belong in an orthography profile and note it.
Maintainer's call; it is a question about one corpus's directory names, not a
structural defect. My earlier "significant separate change" framing rested on
the two withdrawn claims.

**Lesson:** I read the code, saw that nothing consulted `dialect`, and asserted
a data consequence without measuring the data. Both withdrawn claims fell to a
single query over `Corpora/`.

### F2 — IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-10 (fix 1); fix 2 raised as an issue

Two separate defects; different fixes.

**1. The allowlist — one line, and it unblocks #158.** My earlier Truku caveat is
already solved upstream: `QC/corpus_counts.py:53` exposes
`LANGUAGE_NAMES = sorted(set(LANG_CODE_TO_NAME.values()) | {"Truku"})` — 19 names
derived from `languages.csv` plus Truku. `set(LANGUAGE_NAMES) - set(hardcoded)` is
exactly `{'Babuza-Favorlang', 'Pazeh'}`. So delete `orthography_extract.py:476-477`
and `from QC.corpus_counts import LANGUAGE_NAMES; langs = LANGUAGE_NAMES`. Own PR
(POL-049), merged first; then Latham's `extract_orthography_profiles.py` can be
deleted outright, removing one of the three POL-046 deviations.

**2. The real bug — file selection is a path regex.** `generate_corpus` (l.48) does
`re.findall(language_to_process, os.path.join(root))` — matching the language name
against the **directory path**, not `xml:lang`/`dialect`. Consequences: extracting
"Siraya" over `Corpora/` matches **52 files across 3 corpora** (Siraya_Gospels 49,
UtrechtManuscriptWordList 1, Latham-1862 2), silently pooling them; Truku is
unreachable (it's `trv`+dialect, which no path encodes); and a language only works
if a directory happens to be named after it — which is the *only* reason the Latham
shim succeeds. Fix: select on `resolve_language(xml:lang, dialect)` like every other
counter. **Own issue** — it changes what every existing orthography profile contains,
so it needs its own review plus a check on whether any published reference inventory
was built from a pooled profile.

**Fix 1 shipped:** branch `fix/orthography-language-registry`, commit `94425cf3e`,
off current `main`, touching only `QC/orthography/orthography_extract.py`,
`QC/corpus_counts.py` (a stale comment) and a new test file — POL-049 clean.

- New allowlist is a **strict superset** of the old: nothing removed,
  `Babuza-Favorlang` + `Pazeh` added. `--language All` now iterates 19 not 17.
- `tests/utilities/test_orthography_extract_cli.py` drives the real CLI.
  **Reverting the one line fails 4 cases** (both languages, the named regression,
  the static guard against the copy returning); the negative case and Truku pass.
- **1540 passed, 7 skipped** across tests/utilities, tests/orthography,
  tests/validators. ruff clean on touched files (CI does not run ruff; `main`
  already has 11 default-ruff findings in these two files).
- Real corpus: before = `error: Enter a valid Formosan language`; after =
  `Successfully extracted orthographic information for Favorlang from Babuza-Favorlang`.

**Trap found while proving it — changed the advice.** The CLI's *documented*
usage `--corpus <Name>` points at the corpus ROOT, and the path regex then walks
into `CodeAndDocs/`. On Latham that matches the POL-035 snapshot too: 2 files /
296 chars vs 1 file / 148. It does not just inflate counts — the duplicate pushes
characters over the `>= 5` threshold so the profile changes **shape** (corpus-root
run emits `base_characters`/`diacritics` and 14 unique chars; correct run emits
neither and 10). **15 corpora hold 16,968 XML files under `CodeAndDocs/`**
(Wikipedias 13,279, ePark 3,656).

So deleting the shim is safe **only if the run is scoped to `XML/`**. Verified that
invocation reproduces the shim exactly (same keys, `unique_characters`,
`word_frequency`):

    python QC/orthography/orthography_extract.py \
        --corpora_path Corpora/Latham-1862 --corpus XML \
        --language Babuza-Favorlang --kindOf original --by_dialect true \
        --output_dir "$OUTPUT_DIR/orthography"

**Fix 2 written up:** `claudeplans/2026-09-10-orthography-extract-file-selection.md`
— the three consequences (CodeAndDocs pollution, cross-corpus pooling of 52 files
under "Siraya", Truku unreachable), the suggested `is_published_xml` +
`resolve_language` fix, and the caveat that it moves every existing profile, so

Five times I reported a branch or a CI state from refs that were current when

### ✅ RULED 2026-09-09: the validator learns the deletion reading (POL-056 closed)

**FormosanBank `fix/conversion-table-deletions` @ `d42bccfb3`** (worktree
`/workspace/wt-deletions`) — 4 files.

`validate_conversion_table.py` read an empty cell and `NA` alike as "no rule", so
the only six rules in the bank that **delete** a letter were the ones nothing
audited: Bunun_MinEd `w`/`j`, Saisiyat_Tsuchida `’`, Sakizaya_94 `x`,
Tsou_MinEd `w`, Yami_Wakelin `?`.

It now loads them and reports each as a `deletion`, with the distinction that
decides acceptability — whether the **target orthography could have written the
phoneme**:

| table | reported |
|---|---|
| Bunun_MinEd | `w` → (deleted), losing w — the output cannot write w |
| Bunun_MinEd | `j` → (deleted), losing y — the output cannot write y |
| Tsou_MinEd | `w` → (deleted), losing w — the output cannot write w |
| Sakizaya_94 | `x` → (deleted), losing x — the output cannot write x |
| **Yami_Wakelin** | **`?` → (deleted), losing ʔ — the output writes ʔ as `'`** |

🔴 **The distinction immediately found one.** `Yami_Wakelin_113` deletes `?`, and
Ortho113 Yami *can* write that phoneme as `'`. The corpus's own GitBook page
argues at length that `?` there is a glottal-stop **letter, not punctuation**
("Do not strip it as punctuation"). The known nuance is positional — all of
Wakelin's occurrences are word-final, where Ortho113 cannot write it — so the
loss is probably right, but it is now *stated* rather than silent. Worth a
human's confirmation.

(Saisiyat_Tsuchida reports nothing because `Orthographies/Tsuchida/Saisiyat.tsv`
is missing — a pre-existing structural defect, one of the three the repo-wide
check already lists.)

**Design notes.** Deletions never block — they are judgements, not defects; the
Yami_Wakelin exit code is unchanged (1 before and after, for unrelated
mismatches). Because they never block they would have stayed invisible in
aggregate, and on a table that already fails the existing last-three-lines detail
would have scrolled them away, so `run_conversion_table_checks.py` now prepends
any reviewable deletion to that table's detail in **both** paths; its exit code
is unchanged and the job still never blocks. `load_orthography` is deliberately
untouched: in an orthography *profile* an empty IPA cell means the letter has no
value, the same as `NA`. Only a conversion table gives empty the deletion reading.

⚠️ **One existing test asserted the old contract** —
`test_load_conversion_table_reads_rows` said "NA and empty targets skipped". It
now asserts the ruling, alongside five new cases (audited-not-skipped,
cannot-write, could-have-written, never-blocks, not-also-a-coverage-gap).

**Verified:** `tests/validators` + `tests/utilities` **1,451 passed, 7 skipped**.

**GitBook `docs/standardize-rule-application` @ `12f1fa1`** gains a paragraph
recording that deletions are audited and how the two cases differ. (It also had

### 📌 Container vs Mac paths — my error, twice over

I handed Mac paths (`~/Documents/Projects/Formosan/...`) for commands the
maintainer runs **inside the container**, where the tree is `/workspace/...`. The
failed `cd` left the following commands running in the wrong directory, so
`git -C ../FormosanBank pull` hit the shared checkout and aborted on the
uncommitted templates. **Container paths for container commands.**

`sync_upstream_docs.py` lives in the **GitBook** repo, not FormosanBank. Inside the
container: `cd /workspace/FormosanBankGitbook` (or a fresh worktree at
`origin/main`) and pass `--formosanbank /workspace/FormosanBank`. On the Mac the
two repos are siblings, so the default resolves — but only if both checkouts are
current.

### 🔴 NEAR-MISS: my conflict resolution silently reverted PR #218

PR #218 (`qa/standardize-derives-variants`) landed while the branch was open and
rewrapped `apply_standard` in a `for form in s_element.findall(...)` loop, so the
standard tier's `ver="alt"` variants are transliterated too (POL-028). My branch
changed the same function, so the merge conflicted.

⚠️ **Resolving it, I left my pre-merge single-FORM `apply_standard` in the file
below the merged one, where it shadowed it.** Net effect: only the base FORM was
transliterated and a `ver="alt"` variant kept its accents — #218 reverted, in a
branch whose diff looked plausible.

**Caught by #218's own test**, `test_standard_variant_is_derived_from_the_original
_variant`, which is exactly why running the neighbouring suite after a conflict
resolution is not optional. The function inventory diff (`grep '^def '` mine vs
main) showed `def _marker` and `def apply_standard` twice, which is what located it.

Fixed in `5a4a3a1`-equivalent commit on the branch. Re-verified: **1,446 passed,
7 skipped**; Huteson rebuilds byte-identical.

*Lesson worth keeping:* after resolving a conflict in a file you also rewrote,
diff the **function inventory** against the other side, not just the hunks. A
duplicate definition is invisible in a hunk-level review and silently wins.

| `Li/Rukai.tsv` | `o` | one of two `o -> o` | identical values |

### ✅ Trailing newlines: no, they do not misfire

Maintainer asked. `csv.DictReader` parses the final row identically with or
without one — demonstrated, and self-evident from the fact that the sweep *found*
the dead `e -> e` row in a file that has no trailing newline. `standardize.py`'s
line-based hyphen check is likewise unaffected.

norm for about a third of them rather than an anomaly. I had added one to Saaroa
as a drive-by and **reverted it**, so the diff is purely the dead row and the file

### 🔴 CORRECTION: Amis_Church's `ng -> ɟ -> ng` was a deliberate ESCAPE, not a bug

Maintainer flagged `Amis_Church_113.tsv`: it wants `g -> ng` **without** turning
`ng` into `nng`, and achieved that by hopping through a spare symbol —
`ng -> ɟ`, `g -> ng`, `ɟ -> ng`. **My "fix" would have stranded the escape** and
left `ng` as `ɟ`. I had counted it among the 17 corrections; it was a regression.

**Adopted the maintainer's proposal**: `ng -> ng` (shield) ahead of `g -> ng`.
Under longest-first the digraph is staged first, so only a bare `g` is left to
convert. Verified equivalent to the old behaviour on every probe, including the
awkward `gngg -> ngngng`. The `ɟ -> ng` row is **kept**, so a literal ɟ still
converts exactly as before; zero Amis FORMs contain one.

**Re-swept end to end — old code + old tables against new code + new tables,
342 symbols:**

| | count |
|---|---|
| genuine misconversions corrected | **12** (was miscounted as 17) |
| `NA` cells no longer read as literal text | 10 |
| anything else | **0** |

The 12: `Puyuma_Cauquelin` `L`/`ɭ` `ll`->`l`; `Puyuma_MinEd` `ll`
`lrlr`->`ll` (×4); `Rukai_Church` `lh` `lrh`->`l` (×5); `Rukai_Li` `ə:`
`éé`->`ee`. **Amis_Church now shows zero change**, which is the point.

**Lesson worth keeping:** "every rule produces its own replacement" is a good
invariant *because* it forbids escape-and-restore — but I applied it before
asking whether any table was using the idiom deliberately. The sweep found the
pattern; only the maintainer knew it was intentional. Table intent is not
recoverable from the table.

POL-056 now records that the idiom is retired and that `Amis_Church_113` was
migrated with the change. The regression test covers both idioms.

### ✅ add_phonology was ALREADY correct — and more robustly than standardize now is

Maintainer asked whether `add_phonology` shares the bug. **It does not.**
`apply_phonology_mappings` (`QC/utilities/add_phonology.py:256`) is a left-to-right
**scanner**, not a sequence of replacements:

- `ordered = sorted(enumerate(mappings), key=lambda i: (-len(i[1][0]), i[0]))` —
  **longest source first**, stable by original row.
- It appends the replacement to an output list and advances the index past the
  matched letter, so **generated IPA is never re-scanned**. Its docstring says so:
  *"Apply longest grapheme mappings without remapping generated IPA."*
- `load_profile` already skips `NA` cells (`add_phonology.py:233`) — the reading
  standardize was missing.

Structurally stronger than placeholders: no Private Use Area needed at all. So the
fix brings `standardize.py` **into line with its sibling**, which is a better
framing for the PR than "new behaviour".

**Verified by sweep**, the same method as the conversion tables: every letter in
every orthography profile fed through the real function — **161 profile columns,
3,955 letters, 1 discrepancy**, and it is not a chaining bug.

### 🔴 CORRECTION: chaining is DOCUMENTED behaviour; the real defect is the digraph idiom

Maintainer challenged my "conversion rules chain" defect, recalling that
placeholder protection went in generally and that the tables were ordered
deliberately because of chaining. Checked, and **the maintainer is substantially
right and I was wrong.**

**1. Chaining is documented, intended behaviour.** GitBook
`developers/qc-pipeline/standardize.md` says it twice: *"doing ordered, global
Python `str.replace` for each `(original -> replacement)` pair"* (line 26) and
*"Replacements are literal and sequential, so order in the TSV matters — review
the diff."* (line 53). **I should not have called it an undocumented defect.**

**2. Placeholder protection does exist**, added in `162670a4d` "Centralize
reviewed source phonology profiles" — *the same commit that added
`Rukai_Li_113.tsv`*. It was **never general and was never reverted**: it applies
only to rules whose *source* carries a combining mark, and its own comment says
the purpose is surviving `strip_accents`, not preventing chaining. The
`Rukai_Li_113.tsv` order has never changed since that commit.

**3. The maintainer's memory of table ordering is the crux.** Table authors use a
**longest/digraph-first idiom** — `ll -> ll` before `l -> lr`, `lh -> l`,
`ə: -> ee` — expecting the earlier rule's output to be protected. Under sequential
replacement it is not, so the idiom silently fails.

**4. 17 rules across 5 tables are mis-converted today** (swept every table and
column, comparing each rule's own output against what the whole table produces
for that input):

| table | column(s) | input | intended | actual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amis_Church_113 | all 5 | `ng` | `ɟ` | `ng` |
| Puyuma_Cauquelin_113 | Nanwang | `L`, `ɭ` | `l` | `ll` |
| Puyuma_MinEd_113 | all 4 | `ll` | `ll` | `lrlr` |
| Rukai_Church_113 | all 5 | `lh` | `l` | `lrh` |
| Rukai_Li_113 | standard | `ə:` | `ee` | `éé` |

✅ **All latent — no corpus under `Corpora/` references any of these five tables.**

**5. The fix that works is placeholder-for-every-rule PLUS longest-source-first.**
Measured: today 0/17 correct; generalizing the placeholder alone 8/17 (the other 9
fail because the short rule is listed first); **placeholder + longest-first 17/17.**
So the shared-tool change is two lines of intent, not one, and it makes the
existing authoring idiom work as written rather than requiring every table to be
reordered by hand.

⚠️ **The `NA`-as-a-literal defect is unaffected and still stands** — undocumented,
proven empirically (`kakə` -> `kakNA`), and relied on by every table's `NA` cells
only because the NA'd letter never occurs in that dialect.

⏳ Own PR, per POL-049. Huteson's table is correct under today's behaviour either
way (its `e` row is first), so nothing blocks the corpus PR.
