### 🔴 CORRECTION TO THE MAINTAINER'S EXPECTATION: standardize.py DOES chain

Maintainer expected converted output not to be re-converted. **It is.**
`apply_standard` applies rules in file order with plain `str.replace`; only rules
whose *source* carries a combining mark get placeholder protection, and that exists
to survive `strip_accents`, not to stop chaining. Run against the real function:

```
[('ə','e'), ('e','é')]  ə first   kakə -> kaké   should be 'kake'
[('e','é'), ('ə','e')]  e first   kakə -> kake   correct
Rukai_Li_113 shape                kə:  -> kéé    should be 'kee' (long schwa)
```

⏳ **`Rukai_Li_113.tsv` is genuinely broken by this** (`ə: -> ee` fires before
`e -> é`). Latent — no published corpus builds with it. Fix: route EVERY rule
through a placeholder, not only diacritic ones. Shared code, own PR (POL-049).

Second, separate bug: **`NA` is not understood** (`standardize.py:485-495`) — it is
taken as the literal replacement string. Safe bank-wide only because the NA'd letter
never occurs in that dialect. Case-variant derivation widens it (`E -> NA`).

**Row order currently protects Huteson from both** (the `e` row first, Dona `NA`),
which is precisely why they want fixing rather than working around.

### ✅ All-caps: the maintainer was right, and the move fixes it

Capitalization robustness exists — `_case_variants.derive_case_variants` derives
Title and ALL-CAPS variants of lowercase rules, suppressing any capital that is a
distinct grapheme of the source profile. It was simply **switched off** for Huteson,
because `resolve_source_profile` requires the conventional filename and parent
directory and the table was in `CodeAndDocs/`. Moving it turns the mechanism back
on. No output change here (the corpus has zero uppercase FORMs), but the machinery
is now armed. My earlier remark that the bank's 69 all-caps "NA" strings were
"legitimate text, so the bug is not live" stands as a fact but was the wrong frame:
all-caps is supposed to be handled, and it is.

### 🔴 RETRACTED: `ee -> é`. Length and quality are separate questions

Maintainer asked why `ee` isn't `éé`. Fair — I had asserted `ee -> é` from ePark's
spelling alone. **Withdrawing that rule.** It matters because `éé` comes for free
once the profile's `e` cell is fixed (per-character `e -> é` doubles automatically),
whereas `é` needs a deliberate extra rule collapsing the doubling — and Ortho113
marks length precisely by doubling (`Rukai_Li_113`: `e: -> éé`).

**Inside Huteson:** all 11 Maga doubled vowels are **word-final**; Tona has 1 in 41
types and it is medial. That shape says *predictable final lengthening*, which a
phonemic orthography would omit — and it pairs naturally with Maga's non-final
syncope (`ukpuslɨ` ~ Tona `wakoposalə`).

**But ePark contrasts final length**, so its spellings are positive claims, not
omissions: 347 word-final doubled vowels in 27,724 Maolin tokens, including **13
word-final `éé`** (`apéé`, `atéé`, `avéé`, `cvéléé`, `palaléé`).

| Huteson | ePark long | ePark short | agree? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kɖoo` | kdroo 232 | kdro 2 | **yes** |
| `broo` | broo 5 | bro 1 | **yes** |
| `icoo` | icoo 2 | ico 101 | mostly no |
| `mamaa` | 0 | mama 60 | no |
| `ninaa` | 0 | nina 49 | no |
| `maa` | 0 | ma 195 | no |
| `ikee` | ikéé 0 | iké 421 | no |
| `knee` | knéé 0 | kné 205 | no |
| `pkee` | pikéé 0 | piké 30 | no |
| `luŋluŋee` | 0 | lunglungé 9 | no |
| `kosatepruu` | 0 | tepru 0 | no counterpart |

Two agree, eight disagree, one unknown — and the two that agree are the two where
Huteson's doubling survives into ePark, so the systems are not simply on different
length conventions. ⏳ **Three readings survive** (Huteson transcribes predictable
final lengthening ePark omits; the two sources genuinely disagree on eight words;
Huteson's variety differs). **Needs a Rukai phonologist, not a corpus.**

### ✅ What this does NOT change — quality vs length

| | standard FORM | PHON | quality | length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped today | `ikee` | `ikəə` | **wrong — [ə]** | asserts long |
| one cell fixed | `ikéé` | `ikee` | right — [e] | asserts long (open) |
| ePark | `iké` | `ike` | right — [e] | asserts short |

**Fixing the single profile cell (`e`/Maolin: `ə` -> `e`) is a strict improvement
however length resolves** — it corrects the thing that is demonstrably wrong and
leaves the genuinely open thing open. Today's state gets both wrong. That, plus a
short per-word list for the exceptions (`isierkɨ` keeps [ə]; `kosatepruu`
unresolved), is the minimal safe change.

Maintainer's structural read, checked and confirmed (with one correction).

**The profile is the identity map with exactly THREE exceptions**, not two:
`c → ʦ`, `y → j`, **and `e → ə`**. 22 of 25 rows are identity or NA.

**The conversion table is the profile composed with Ortho113 read backwards,
listing only the rows where that composition is not already the identity.**
I generated it that way from the profile and got the committed file row for row
(predicted set == actual set, exactly).

| Huteson | profile assigns | Ortho113 spells that phone | rule? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c` | ʦ | `c` | no-op — Ortho113 shares the convention |
| `y` | j | `y` | no-op — Ortho113 shares the convention |
| **`e`** | **ə** | **`e`** | **no-op — ONLY because the profile says [ə]** |
| a b d g i k l m n o p r s t u v w ɨ | identity | | no-op |
| `ɖ` | ɖ | `dr` | rule |
| `ŋ` | ŋ | `ng` | rule |
| `ʔ` | ʔ | `'` | rule (Dona) |
| `ə` | ə | `e` | rule (Dona) |

So `c` and `y` correctly generate no rule. **`e` generates no rule for the same
formal reason, but on a claim the data contradicts** — and that is the entire
defect. Change the one `e`/Maolin cell from `ə` to `e` and the conversion table
automatically gains `e → é` (Maolin; Dona NA, since Ortho113 Dona has no `é` and
Huteson's Tona has no `e`). Nothing else in either file moves.

⚠️ **Implementation detail for the fix.** `standardize.py`'s `apply_standard`
walks the table **in file order** with plain `str.replace` — no longest-match
sort. An `ee` row must precede the `e` row or `ikee` → `ikéé` instead of `iké`.
⏳ **Same hazard is already latent in `Rukai_Li_113.tsv`**: its `ə: → ee` row
fires before `e → é`, so a long schwa `kə:` comes out `kéé` rather than `kee`.
No published corpus builds with that table (grep over `Corpora/` finds no user),
so latent not live — but a real bug, own PR per POL-049.

### 🔴 Huteson is NOT plain IPA — and the `e` row is per-word, not a rule

Maintainer pushed on my premise, and was right to. Checking each symbol against
strict IPA: `c`→[ts] and `y`→[j] are **Americanist/practical values, not IPA**
(IPA `c` = voiceless palatal stop, IPA `y` = close front rounded vowel). It is a
**mixed system** — practical consonant values, IPA symbols where the practical
set has no letter (`ŋ ɖ ʔ ə ɨ`). **Correction: my earlier "Huteson wrote IPA"
was wrong**, so the `e` row cannot be settled by appeal to notation either way.

What survives that correction: no transcription of this kind, IPA or Americanist,
would ever contain `é` — so "`é` absent ⇒ [e] absent" is still a non-sequitur.
The circularity finding stands; only its justification changed.

**Settled empirically instead.** All 8 Maga word types containing `e`, matched
against ePark Maolin (Ortho113: `é`=[e], `e`=[ə]), identification confirmed by
gloss or sentence translation where one exists:

| Huteson | ePark | reads | confirmed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ikee` | `iké` | é [e] | gloss 有/在 'exist' |
| `knee` | `kné` | é [e] | gloss 這個/這裡 'this' |
| `pkee` | `piké` | é [e] | form, 30 tokens |
| `luŋluŋee` | `lunglungé` | é [e] | form, 9 tokens |
| `abrele` | `abrélé` | é é | gloss 辛苦 'tiring'; S transl 不感疲憊 |
| `pwabreve` | `brévé`/`ébrévé` | é é | S `mwa brévé` 回去; `mwa`=去 'go' |
| `isierkɨ` | `sierkɨ`/`siereke` | **e [ə]** | gloss 睡覺 'sleep'; S 她在房間睡覺. 3 ePark forms, all plain `e` |
| `kosatepruu` | — | ? | no ePark counterpart |

- `ee` → `é`: **4 of 4, exceptionless.** Clean rule.
- single `e` → `é` in 6 of 7 resolvable vowel slots; → `e` in `isierkɨ`.
- **The profile's blanket `e`→[ə] is contradicted in 6 of 7 resolvable types —
  but a blanket `e`→`é` would also be wrong.**

⏳ **Correction to my previous entry:** I wrote that "the `e`→`é` reading is much
the stronger." That over-corrected. **Huteson's Maga `e` is one symbol covering
two Ortho113 vowels**; no single rule resolves it. This is exactly the
WakelinTexts `ř` shape you ruled on 2026-09-07 — resolve per word what can be
resolved, let the rest pass through, accept `*` in the PHON that cannot. Applied
here: one rule (`ee`→`é`, 4 types) + a two-word list (`abrele`, `pwabreve`),
leaving `isierkɨ` as-is and `kosatepruu` unresolved. Smaller than Wakelin's, on a
corpus a hundredth the size. **Say the word and I will hand the PR a precise
worklist.**

⚠️ Note this is also why the mechanical derivation could not have got it right:
the answer is not in Ortho113's table, it is in the words.

### 🔴 Three things needing a maintainer ruling

1. **F1 — the orthography scheme is inside `CodeAndDocs/`.** `source_orthography/Rukai.tsv`
   + `huteson_source_to_ortho113.tsv` are not under `Orthographies/` (POL-039).
   Costs, all verified: `standardize.py` warns it cannot derive capital-letter
   variants (harmless today — 0 uppercase FORMs); `conversion-tables.yaml` only
   triggers on `Orthographies/**` so **CI never lints this table**; and
   **WakelinTexts, merged two days earlier, did the opposite** for the same
   problem without being cited (POL-050). Tension: POL-049 forbids the corpus PR
   touching root registries — so the clean fix is POL-049's own shape, a small
   separate PR adding `Orthographies/Huteson/Rukai.tsv` +
   `Orthographies/ConversionTables/Rukai_Huteson_113.tsv`, merged first.
2. **F2 — the Maolin standard tier does not converge with ePark's Maolin.**
   11 word types have meaning-confirmed counterparts they do not match. Sharpest:
   `ikee`/`iké` (421 bank tokens), `knee`/`kné` (205), `pkee`/`piké` (30),
   `lunglungee`/`lunglungé` (9) — **665 attestations of the `é` spelling, 0 of
   Huteson's.** `é` is 3.04% of bank Maolin characters (4,885/160,723) and **0%**
   here. Mechanism: the source profile declares Maolin has no [e], so Ortho113's
   `é`/`e` = [e]/[ə] contrast cannot be expressed; the corpus's own conversion
   audit prints `cannot encode: e` and the build proceeds. PHON makes it explicit:
   `knee → knəə` vs the bank's `kné → kne`. ⏳ **Is Maga's vowel here a long schwa
   (Huteson right — document it) or [e] (add the `e → é` rule `Rukai_Li_113`
   already has)?** Note Dona is fine, and `kdroo`/`broo` match the bank.
3. **F3 — the rights claim is asserted and CI will not question it.**
   `CC BY-NC-SA 4.0` is an exact vocabulary value with both POL-044 lines, but the
   evidence is a screenshot in a private `Basecamp` card. I ran `rights_delta.py`
   base-vs-head: **"No corpus licence changed." exit=0** — `rights-comparison.yaml`
   detects *changes* to existing corpora, so a **new corpus's licence is never
   interrogated**. Not POL-043 (nothing weakened); the opposite direction.
   ⏳ Needs your confirmation of the SIL grant. Also a real gap in the mechanism.

### ⏳ Lower-priority, mostly shared-code (own PRs per POL-049)

- **F4** `pytest.ini` sets `testpaths = ["tests"]`, so the corpus's 12
  source-fidelity tests are **not collected**; no workflow runs `validate.sh` or
  `audit_source_alignment.py`. The guard is real — I mutation-tested it and it
  catches both a changed gloss and a dropped letter — but it is opt-in. The
  transcription lives twice (Python literals + `manual_source_review.tsv`);
  203 field comparisons, 0 disagreements today.
- **F5** POL-036's standardized gloss (this is the bank's **first**
  `TRANSL[@kindOf="standard"]`) collides with V085 HARD, forcing a semantically
  wrong `ver="alt"` alongside it. V085 should treat differing `kindOf` as already
  discriminating.
- **F6** `source_manifest.md` points at a private Basecamp card for a report that
  is **publicly archived** (sil.org/resources/archives/9008). Build doesn't need

- **F7** Tona 4's original tier joins `saokwa mamitə` → `saokwamamitə` (disclosed,
  reviewer's call, plausible) and keeps W ids `001`/`003` with a gap, preserved

  published predecessor, so this PR is the last moment the gap can be closed.
- **F9** `orthography_extract.py` hard-drops chars/bigrams occurring <5 times
  (`:118`, `:165`). On 260 Maolin characters that deletes **7 of 22 letters**
  before any metric is computed, which is why the detector reports Jaccard 0.46 /
  bigram-cosine 0.32. Recomputed unfiltered, Huteson's letter set is a **strict
  subset** of the bank's in both dialects and Jaccard is 0.714. Not this corpus's
  defect; it is the clearest demonstration of the miscalibration in the bank.

### The data itself is well corroborated

Built a 9,551-entry form→gloss lexicon from the bank's *other* Rukai data and
looked Huteson's words up in it: `gili` = 弟弟，妹妹, `broo` = 飯, `kɨkɨ`/`kakə` = 我,
`titina` = 媽媽, `tatava` = 爸爸, `belebele` = 香蕉, `yakai` = 有；在, `kwanə` = 吃,
`nakoa` = 我；[受], `takanaw` = PN. **Not one contradiction.** This settles the
riskiest alignment (Maga 5's four words against four whitespace gloss tokens).
The 7 blank `na` cells are plausible — the bank glosses `na` as `[虛]` 470/493
times. The Maga↔Tona parallel set reproduces Maga's documented vowel syncope
(`ukpuslɨ` ~ `wakoposalə`, `blatɨ` ~ `balatə`) and independently corroborates the
source profile's complementary NA pattern (`aŋatu` ~ `ʔaŋato`; `kɨkɨ` ~ `kakə`).

⚠️ One cross-corpus divergence worth publicising, not fixing: Huteson glosses
`ki` as `NOM`; every other Rukai source in the bank glosses it `OBL` (832×) or
`GEN` (96×), never `NOM`. POL-001/POL-036 say preserve it, and the corpus does.

### The corpus is no longer original-tier-only

**2,189 standard FORMs and 2,189 PHON per tier, from zero.** New:

- `Orthographies/Wakelin/README.md` — **the reasoning, rule by rule, with the
  evidence for each**, as the maintainer asked

**`standards.csv` needed no change**, and my earlier claim that it "interacts"
was wrong. It maps Yami → Ortho113, which selects the **standard** tier's
profile; the original tier's comes from `add_phonology --orthography Wakelin`,
an entirely separate code path. Verified in the source, not assumed.

**Pipeline** gains four steps: `standardize --segmented-without-m-tier` (needed
because C012 uses M-tier presence as its proxy for "segmented", and some
sentences here print hyphens while publishing no morphemes), the `ř` word list,
the parenthesis resolution, and `add_phonology --orthography Wakelin`.

⚠️ **Two corpus-local steps edit the standard tier outside `standardize.py`**,
against POL-002, on maintainer rulings. Documented in both scripts and the
README with the cost stated: **a standalone `standardize.py` run reverts them**.
Both are strict — a rule matching nothing fails the build.

### The two things the derived tiers do not claim

- **`ř` maps to `*`.** Not one modern phoneme: of eleven words five resolve, to
  three different letters (`d`, `d`, `l`, `z`, `z`), six to nothing. The five
  known are standardized per-word; elsewhere `ř` passes through. **56 PHON carry
  a `*`** — 41 original, 15 standard.
- **Ortho113 cannot write a word-final glottal stop**, which the article does,
  so the standard tier loses it. A property of the target orthography.

Optional material becomes a standard + `alternate` FORM pair **on the word
only** (7 words); morphemes just lose their brackets (6); `(unctn)` is dropped
as annotation (2). ⚠️ I first put the alternate on the sentence too and caught
that it contradicts the slash ruling (alternates stop at the W) before

so `sira(unctn)` reached the standard tier as `sira(onctn)`.

**V121 28 → 14 HARD** — back to the pre-existing accepted count on the original
tier alone, so CI had no new HARD findings to block. V014 2189 → 0, V063 94 → 0,

**FormosanBank PR #204 merged** (`origin/main` `c07574888`); **GitBook merged**
(`origin/main` `17e2e333f`). Verified before deleting: both branches strict
ancestors of their `origin/main`, worktrees clean.

**Cleaned:** worktrees `/workspace/wt-wakelin2`, `/workspace/wt-gb-wakelin2` and
my scratch `/tmp/gbmain`; branches `fix/wakelin-monomorphemic-glosses` and
`docs/wakelin-monomorphemic-glosses`. `git worktree remove` refused the first on
an untracked `.DS_Store`; before forcing it I diffed every remaining file against
`origin/main` — the only differences were `__pycache__/*.pyc` and `.DS_Store`,
nothing unique — then removed it.

**What landed:** the Leipzig dot convention extended past parentheses, plus the
padded-`unan` deletions. Words publishing no morpheme tier **21 → 5**; M **1102
→ 1123**. Five survivors, all genuine: `Kangkang/S34`'s three (three gloss units
for two printed words) and `S39W5`/`S40W5` (the article glosses two of three
morphemes).

### 🔴 Lesson, stated third time and still costing time: FETCH BEFORE CLAIMING

The GitBook `corpus-page-lint` failure was diagnosed **wrong twice**, both times
from a stale `origin/main`:

1. I built a scratch worktree from a cached `origin/main` ref, ran `find` over
   it, and reported **"GitBook has no page for UtrechtManuscriptWordList"** and
   **"the failure is pre-existing on main"**. Both false — the page and its
   `CSV_TO_MD` entry were already on main.
2. Earlier, my local `--strict` lint passed because it defaulted to
   `/workspace/FormosanBank`'s working tree, which was several commits behind and
   did not yet contain the Utrecht corpus at all. A green check against a stale
   tree.

**The actual cause was trivial:** the GitBook branch predated the Utrecht work by
two commits, so linting it against the *current* FormosanBank main found a corpus
with no page **on that branch**. `git merge origin/main` fixed it.

Both failure modes are the same root error — reporting repository state from a
ref I had not just fetched. I logged this on 2026-09-07 after doing it with
branch counts, and then did it twice more. **Rule for next time: `git fetch`
immediately before any claim about what a remote contains, and pin
`--corpora-path` explicitly rather than letting a tool default to a working
tree.**

⏳ **Still open, unchanged:** the untracked
`claudeplans/2026-09-07-wakelin-orthography-proposal/` (decide whether to commit

worktree is gone), the 28 padded `unan` glosses on the `-em`/`-m` suffix
(`source_discrepancies.md` §F), and four merged remote branches left undeleted:

**Original-tier conversion (RULED).** Every XML-stage repair writes only the

(`create_standard` OVERWRITES an existing standard FORM), and `add_phonology.py`

borrow_segmentation (1 of 3). The OTHER TWO borrow_segmentation loops are
READERS -- safety guards that require both tiers and refuse a word whose standard
PHON is not reproducible -- and were deliberately left alone. Only
resolve_inline_parentheticals is wired into a run so far.

**Sentence sources differ from grammar in four ways**: top level is
{glosses, meta}; the running sentence is withheld in 3319 of 4430 records;
gloss column order is not fixed; and a record can hold several sentences.

**Steps 0-4 (measured one at a time), s-main / s-clean / s-p3:**
* 0 rebuild the sentence form from the gloss forms. My first gate tested
  `not s_form.strip()`, catching only the 1039 EMPTY ori and missing the 2280
  whose ori is punctuation only (a lone '.'). With the word-character gate:
  test 1 76.5 -> 100.0, test 3 24.1 -> 99.1, test 5 16.2 -> 91.3.
* 1 realign gloss columns (12028 rows). Kanakanavu writes Chinese first, Rukai
  English first, Bunun is MIXED WITHIN ITSELF (6820 vs 6450), so the gate is
  per row. NO TEST MOVED -- test 10 asks only whether SOME gloss carries Han.
  Added test 15 (a zho TRANSL carries Han): s-clean 52.1, s-p3 97.5, main 97.0.
* 2 split a record holding several sentences: only 4 records. My prediction
  that this was the test-3/5 lever was WRONG; step 0's gate was.
* 3 expand infixes (630). Needed a guard the grammar version lacks: do not
  expand a bracket group with no host letters outside it ('<L2J...L2J>',
  '<BREATH>') -- convert_infix_notation declines those for the same reason.
* 4 drop sentences marked ungrammatical by a bare leading '*' (16). This is
  where the 35 residual asterisks live; all are in this subcorpus.

**Test 8 corrected again**: a word-initial or word-final infix leaves no '-' in
the base (expand_infixes strips it), so recombination must try both placements.
This lifted EVERY column (main 99.8 -> 99.9, clean 99.9 -> 100.0) -- the
signature of a test defect, not a pipeline one.

## 2026-09-08 — p3 step 17 (infixes); tests 3/6/8 corrected

**Step 17 (RULED): expand infix notation into its own morphemes**, reusing
`expand_infixes` from the corpus's own utils.py. Order copied from main and it
matters: split on `-`/`=` FIRST, then expand infixes within each piece.
Expanding first yields a single base whose `-` marks the embedding point, which
cannot then be re-split (`k<um>a-kʉnʉ` would give base `k-a-kʉnʉ`, three pieces
against a two-piece gloss). 290 infixes expanded.

**Test 6 was RIGHT; the PIPELINE was wrong.** 150 of 158 test-6 failures were
infixed words with NO M at all (`t<um>ʉpʉ`, `c<in><Vm>ʉ’ʉra`): M generation was
gated on the form having more than one `-`/`=` piece, and an infix-only word has
none, so it never entered the loop and the infix was never expanded. Fixed in
the pipeline. p3 test 6 now 100.0 (main 98.0).

**Test 6 fix (genuine):** count only M that carry a FORM. A form-less M marks a
surplus gloss piece (test 12's business), not an implied morpheme. That was the
other 8 failures.

**Test 8 was misreporting BOTH columns.** An infix morpheme sits beside the base
in document order but belongs INSIDE it, at the `-` the base carries as its
embedding point, so joining forms left to right gives `um`+`ta` for `t<um>a`
instead of `t`+`um`+`a`. Any pipeline that expands infixes was penalised for
doing so. Test 8 now reconstructs by insertion, and recognises BOTH conventions:
angle brackets `<um>` (what expand_infixes emits, so what p3 writes) and
hyphen-flanked `-n-` (what the published XML carries -- 302 of them, zero in
angle form). Main was under-reported at 97.2; the true figure is 99.8.

**Test 3 similarity guard.** The one-to-one fallback previously advanced with NO
similarity check, so a walk that had slipped by one kept marching (comparing
word N with token N+1) and still balanced at the end -- a misaligned sentence
passed. 95 of 569 such advances were below 0.5 similarity, and the low ones were
plainly desyncs (`ap1_S_73`: W `na` vs S `cʉkʉ`, ratio 0.00). Now fails below
0.5. Costs p3 0.4 points; exposes `clean` truthfully at 43.0 (was 91.7).

Current: main / p3 -- test 3 98.0/98.4, test 5 68.0/68.5, test 6 98.0/100.0,
test 8 99.8/99.4, test 14 99.3/100.0.

⏳ OPEN: main's scripts p3 has not adopted that should still move numbers --
`borrow_segmentation.py` (biggest remaining lever on test 6/12: borrows
segmentation where one occurrence of a word is segmented and another is not),
`repair_empty_morphemes.py` (the 63 M with no gloss text), `convert_infix_notation.py`,
`propagate_clitic_boundaries.py` + `repair_unsegmented_standard_clitic.py`
(test 5, p3's weakest real number). p3 also emits no standard tier and no PHON.

**Test 3 alignment rewritten twice; wording corrected.** I described the fix as
treating a hyphen as a "sentence split", which was backwards. A clitic is ONE
word spanning SEVERAL sentence tokens (`ni-pu’a=kee` / `nipu’a kee`); the
`itiza` / `i` + `t-iza` case is the opposite -- SEVERAL words spanning ONE
token. Splitting the word form on `-` gave one word licence to eat more tokens,
the wrong direction, and dropped test 3 to 96.2. The walk is now symmetric:
group on either side when the text matches EXACTLY, allow a length-based span
only for a clitic-bearing word (delta <= 1), and otherwise advance one-to-one --
because a spelling difference between tiers is test 5's business, not test 3's.
An intermediate version that required exact text at every step collapsed test 3
to 76.0 by turning it into test 5. Final: main 98.3, p3 98.8.

**Step 7 confirmed runtime-computed**, not a hardcoded list: `build_attestation`
rescans grammar+sentence+story on every run. The only hardcoded vocabularies in
p3 are the approved closed lists (23 roles x 3 case prefixes, 5 compound
glosses, 6 prompt prefixes, 4 source annotations, 7 irreconcilable ids).

⏳ OPEN: 35 residual `*` in the `sentence/` subcorpus (bare `*` marking a whole
sentence or word ungrammatical, POL-016 -- not the paren notation). None in
grammar. Gap for when p3 extends beyond grammar.

## 2026-09-08 — p3 steps 8-11; CORRECTION on glottal normalization

**CORRECTION.** I claimed the glottal-stop letter must never be normalized.
That is wrong. POL-010 canonicalizes U+2018/U+2019 curly singles, U+02BC,
U+02BB, backtick and U+02C8 ALL to ASCII `'` -- the straight apostrophe IS the
glottal stop's canonical spelling, and POL-018 (single quotes are never
quotation marks) is what makes it unambiguous. Evidence: main's published
Grammar XML holds 6,238 straight apostrophes and zero curly ones.

**Step 11 (RULED): canonicalize punctuation** by reusing
`QC.cleaning.clean_xml.swap_punctuation` -- the repo's single implementation,
not a reimplementation. 717 S FORMs + 998 word cells changed; p3 now has 2,530
straight apostrophes and no curly ones. It moved NO test score: the tests
compare the sentence tier against the word tier within one tree, and the
variants were consistent within each sentence. It matters for POL-010
conformance, not for these numbers.

**ORDERING CONSTRAINT (important).** `swap_punctuation` maps `[` -> `(` and
`]` -> `)`. So normalization must run AFTER step 1 (bracket removal), never
before: normalizing first would hide the constituent brackets from step 1 AND
make them indistinguishable from POL-017's `*(X)` / `(*X)` optional/forbidden
parentheses. This is the one place "run clean_xml prior to anything else"
cannot be taken literally.

**Steps 8/9/10 (RULED).** 8: strip prompt prefixes -- vocabulary is `問：`
only, the sole form attested anywhere in the corpus (no `答：`). 9: strip role
labels from the S FORM using step 1's vocabulary, allowing trailing punctuation
(`Panayan中心語,`) -- 11 stripped. 10: move parenthesised source annotations to
@note rather than delete -- `（日語）` 11x = Japanese loanword, `（借詞）` 3x =
loanword, `（已發生）` 1x, `（需再確認）` 1x. Only the first two are etymology;
the others are semantic/editorial notes. Test 14 now 100.0% for p3 (main 99.3).

**soni!15 REVISES the step 4 ruling.** The record is `’akuni arapipiningi
soni!15`, glossed `soni` = 今天, free translation `今天不要出去！`. The `!` is the
sentence's own imperative punctuation; only `15` is the footnote. So step 4
should strip ONLY the digits and keep the punctuation, not "the S-final period
and numerals". NOT YET CHANGED -- awaiting confirmation.

**Test 3 characterization (89 failures).** 35 are the test's fault: a clitic can
be attached on BOTH tiers (`’acecu` / `’ace=cu`), so the sentence-token count
must be a RANGE -- from len(W) (all clitics attached) to sum(1+`=`) (all
separate) -- not an exact figure. 14 more are punctuation-only tokens in the S
FORM counted as words (`’uru .`). Projected: 94.8% -> 97.0% (range) -> 97.9%
(plus punctuation). The residual ~37 are real content differences (a W `sua`
absent from the sentence; `ka sinawal` spaced where the word tier has
`ka-sinawal`). NOT YET CHANGED.

⏳ OPEN: the 223 mismatched word pairs get a published list linked from
README/GitBook, distinguishing glossing convention from probable error
(`Pori`/`Pani` is plainly the latter). Not yet written.

⏳ OPEN: `matai’35` one-off via the source-repair mechanism. Not yet written.

## 2026-09-08 — pipeline2 frozen at 7 steps; p3 opened; tests 12-14 added

**p2 frozen** as a fixed baseline; **p3** (`pipeline3.py`) is the working column,
so a moving p3 against a still p2 shows what each new step buys.

Steps, in execution order (numbers are stable ids, not order):
3 pinned source-record repairs (1) -> 5 no W tier for unglossed sentences (106)
-> 2 A2 wordlists to sentence TRANSL (2036) -> 4 footnote markers off S FORM (6)
-> 6 English compound glosses joined with '.' (0 in grammar; all 3 live in story)
-> 1 constituent bracketing removed (294 cells, 3 rows) -> 7 gloss separator
converted only on an exact morpheme-count match (11).

**Test changes (RULED).** squash() folds case -- worth ~20 points on test 5 in
EVERY column, so it was a test defect, not a pipeline difference. Test 3 is now
clitic-aware (each '=' in a W absorbs one sentence token): 49.3% -> 94.8%, and
it was previously mismeasuring, not measuring. Test 7 scoped to M that have a
FORM. New test 12 (M has a FORM) makes surplus gloss pieces countable; new
test 13 (S has a W tier) is a tracker, not a target; new test 14 (S FORM has no
Han). `--na` marks a column unscoreable on a test rather than crediting a 100%
earned by never emitting the element -- used for `fix` on test 12.

**Test 3 x test 5 cross-tab** is diagnostic: 493 sentences fail 3 but pass 5
(clitic written separately in the sentence, attached in the word tier -- now
fixed by the clitic-aware rule), 183 pass 3 but fail 5 (morphophonology:
'para’akia' vs 'pa-ara-’akia' restores segments surface fusion removed).
Diacritics account for 58 test-5 failures (67.2% -> 70.6% if ignored).
No punctuation-only W cells exist in grammar, so the "isolated punctuation"
hypothesis does not apply here.

⏳ OPEN: **29 sentences with Han in the S FORM** (main has the identical 29):
3 `問：` prompt prefixes and 11 role labels in `ori` are druff and want Step 1's

## 2026-09-08 — pipeline2 (NTU Grammar rebuild): steps 1-3 ruled

Test-driven rebuild of the NTU Grammar pipeline, measured against
`claudeplans/report-audit-tools/grammar_xml_tests.py` (12 tests) in four
columns: main / has_gloss fix / clean (naive JSON->XML) / p2.

**Step 1 — strip trailing Chinese role labels (RULED, vocabulary approved).**
Restricted to a closed vocabulary rather than main's blanket CJK strip: 23 roles
x an optional case prefix (主格/屬格/斜格), which covers all 30 attested surface
forms including 主格處所 (whole-cell only). 212 cells affected, zero residue.

**Step 2 — A2 vocabulary lists (RULED).** An A2 record is a dictionary entry,
not a sentence: the headword becomes the S FORM, the Chinese becomes the
sentence-level TRANSL, and no W is emitted. 2,036 entries routed. This is what
main already does (`is_wordlist = "A2" in source.name`); the naive conversion's
failure to do it accounted for most of the gap on tests 2, 4 and 11.

**Step 3 — pinned source-record repair (RULED).** Kanakanavu 05 record 4 had the
free translation in the gloss column and a grammatical note in the translation
slot. Repaired by hand via a NEW repair list,
`claudeplans/report-audit-tools/p2_source_repairs.xml` — same contract as the
published `source_repairs.xml` (SHA-256 over the pre-repair record, fail-closed)
but separate, so pipeline2 accumulates its own repairs as found. ori is
`mima sua pa'ici sua cau`; both source annotations retained as notes.

⏳ OPEN: whether ori should end in a period (every other sentence in the corpus
does; the scrape has `cau（.` with the bracket and period transposed).

**Constituent brackets (RULED 2026-09-08, partly open).** Brackets and their
role labels are deleted together, as part of Step 1 — no spans go into the XML.
Brackets NOT explained by a label are not to be touched without investigation.
A row left with no gloss is deleted whole (`]基準體`). Kanakanavu 14 rec 8:
delete the `[` on row 9 and all of row 11 — no traces; this falls out of Step 1
once labels pair with their brackets, so no source_repairs entry is needed.
Sakizaya 04 rec 27: delete all brackets.

Investigation found TWO conventions, so the rec 27 ruling has wider scope than
it appeared: (a) Kanakanavu labelled brackets, where the label can sit mid-cell
before a clitic (`[tarukuka]中心語=musu`) or inside the closing bracket
(`no-noman中心語]`) — the end-anchored detector misses these; (b) 18 Sakizaya
blocks (ch. 4/5/6) bracketing NPs with NO labels at all, six of which carry
coindexation subscripts for binding (`[aku]i … [kaku]i`).

⏳ OPEN: does the rec 27 ruling extend to all 18 unlabelled Sakizaya blocks, and
what happens to the six coindexation subscripts? Not implemented pending this.

⏳ SUPERSEDED: **constituent brackets.** 39 non-A2 gloss blocks use `[...]` to bracket
a constituent, with a role label on the closing bracket
(`[kumakʉnʉ macu'u karu]主體 saa/sua [kumakʉnʉ 'aramʉ]基準體`). Of the 212 role
labels, 24 are constituent labels on a `]`, 5 mark a head *inside* a bracket
(`parai中心語`), and 183 are word-level. Main discards brackets and labels
entirely. Decision needed on whether pipeline2 preserves this annotation and
where. One block has unbalanced brackets (Sakizaya 04 rec 27: 2 open, 1 close).

### ⏳ Open

1. **⏳ FormosanBank-wide sweep: restore `reproduce.sh` as a strict wrapper.**
   ILRDF now has `refresh_source.sh` (re-scrape) and `make_xml.sh` (build; the
   authority pin is *informational*, and the build reports the commit and
   digest it produced). Missing is a third script that names the strict path:
   `reproduce.sh` pins the commit, refuses on mismatch or a dirty tree, calls
   `make_xml.sh`, and **compares the resulting digest against
   `docs/reproduction.md`, failing on drift**. Today that mode exists only as
   `FORMOSANBANK_STRICT_AUTHORITY=1`, which nobody will discover, and nothing
   actually checks the recorded digest — it is merely recorded. Maintainer
   ruling 2026-09-08: do this once, repo-wide, across every corpus with a
   `make_xml.sh`, not per-corpus.
2. **⏳ Grave and caron are absent from `ACCENTS_TO_STRIP`**, so one Paiwan `è`
   and one `ǔ` survive in the standard tier. Adding them moves 246 characters
   across Wikipedias and Siraya_Gospels; maintainer said not to do it as part
   of ILRDF. Needs its own PR.
3. **⏳ ILRDF audio on Hugging Face is stale, and renaming records makes it
   worse.** `AUDIO/@file` is derived from the sentence id, so every id change
   renames every audio file. HF holds `Amis_0.mp3` (main's names); #179 asks
   for `Amis_894f9b25a1d5dbe8.mp3`; v2 asks for
   `Amis_05d8d0fa-…-00155db40116.mp3`. **`hf-audio-parity` will be red on our
   PR, and would have been red on #179** — that workflow was added 2026-07-29,
   three weeks before #179, and is an ancestor of it. #179 addressed none of
   this: it deleted `audioDL.py`, changed the licence, and its QC report's
   "audio ownership audit PASS" only checks URL uniqueness inside the XML.

   The source audio URLs also moved upstream, `e-dictionary/MultiMedia/…` →
   `sys-dictionary/Storage/<guid>`, with **zero overlap**, so HF matches
   neither PR. A re-upload is needed whatever we decide.

   **Recommendation: name audio by the storage GUID, not the sentence id.**
   They are different namespaces (167,241 sentence GUIDs vs 132,268 storage
   GUIDs, 0 overlap), and 15,053 sentences carry more than one recording, so
   the sentence id cannot name a file uniquely — today a positional `_2`
   suffix papers over it, which means a source reordering silently swaps two
   files' identities while the XML still validates. Storage GUIDs are unique
   by construction and immune to both id changes and reordering.

4. **⏳ Headword append idiom.** `uculru(wa)` means uculru/uculruwa; two such
   records are dropped rather than guessed at. Fine as is, but a rule could
   recover them.

**POL-042 caught us mid-flight** — `@copyright` must be exactly a
`rights_vocabulary.csv` value, and `CC BY-NC` is not one. Anyone with an
in-flight corpus PR that sets a licence should check for the same problem.

## 2026-09-07 — #175 branch REBUILT on current main; and I repeated #175's own invented-provenance fault

### 🔴 Self-correction: I put an unverifiable commit SHA in the README

My README note said the 03A_01 XML *"existed briefly as an empty placeholder and
was deleted in commit `2288d4f`."* I took that verbatim from **#175's own ledger
`disposition` field** and did not check it. Checked now:

- `git cat-file -t 2288d4f` → **"Not a valid object name"**. No commit with that
  prefix exists in FormosanBank at all.
- `git log --all --diff-filter=D -- Corpora/Whitehorn_Collection/XML/` → **empty**.
  **No XML file has ever been deleted under that path in the repo's history.**

Caught by **`validate_port_readiness` P004** ("pinned commit … is not reachable"),
which treats a SHA in a README as a claim to verify. Sentence removed; the note
now asserts only what the scan and the repo actually support. This is exactly the
fault I charged #175 with — asserting provenance the artifacts do not carry —
committed by repeating its prose instead of checking it. **Rule for the rest of
the sweep: a SHA copied out of a PR is a claim, not a fact.**

`origin/main` had moved 24 commits (Wakelin #195, Montgomery #196, CI stats).

### 📚 Citations — main's string was right, just in the wrong attribute

Maintainer: *"the BibTeX citation didn't have .bib format!"* Correct. `main` had
**no `citation` attribute at all**, and an APA reference sitting in
`BibTeX_citation`.

**House style, surveyed across all 26 corpora / 14,565 files:** `BibTeX_citation`
is real BibTeX (`@…`) on **25 of 26** (only `NTU_Paiwan_ASR` is mixed — someone
else's problem), and `citation` is **APA** throughout. So main's APA string was the
right text for the wrong field.

| | on `main` | on the branch |
|---|---|---|
| `citation` | *absent* | `Joby, C. (2021). Utrecht Manuscript, Siraya-Nederlands woordenlijst / UM database [PDF document]. Neerlandistiek. https://…` |
| `BibTeX_citation` | APA prose | `@misc{joby2021utrecht, author = {Joby, Christopher}, …}` |

### 🟢 RULED: cite the article, not the database

Maintainer supplied the citation. Now published:

    citation        Joby, C. (2021). Revisions to the Siraya lexicon based on the
                    original Utrecht Manuscript: A case study in source data.
                    Historiographia Linguistica, 48(2-3), 177-204.
    BibTeX_citation @article{joby2021revisions, title = {...}, author = {Joby,
                    Christopher}, journal = {Historiographia Linguistica},
                    volume = {48}, number = {2-3}, pages = {177--204},
                    year = {2021}, publisher = {John Benjamins ...}}

Field order preserved exactly as given; **flattened to one line**, because XML
attribute-value normalization collapses newlines to spaces anyway and all 25
conforming corpora are single-line.

🔑 **This separates what to cite from what the build reads.** The `source`
attribute and `source_manifest.json` still pin the UM database PDF by SHA-256 — it
is the data file — and the README now says so explicitly under Citation. The
article is the scholarly reference.

Commit amended to **`d6707680a`**; rebuild, determinism and validators re-run,
**0 HARD**.

### The earlier conformance fixes (superseded above, kept for the reasoning)

#172 had already moved to real BibTeX; I made two further conformance fixes:
**`citation` recast in APA** to match the other 25, and the BibTeX author changed
from `{Christopher Joby}` to **`{Joby, Christopher}`** — the majority style (16 of
26) and the one that lets a name actually parse, since a braced full name is
treated as a protected literal and `\citeauthor` would render "Christopher Joby"
rather than "Joby". README citation updated to match. Commit amended to
**`6f83c5a11`**; rebuild, determinism and validators re-run, still **0 HARD**.

## 2026-09-07 — 📋 What is actually in column 7 (the keep/drop brief)

**519 of 1,061 rows filled (49%).** After stripping brackets, citations and
` - gloss` tails: 2 are a placeholder `-`, 5 are pure note with no Siraya, and
**512 carry real Siraya text.**

### 🔑 It is not the same kind of object as column 4

Column 4 differs from column 1 by a letter or two. **Column 7 differs by dialect,
orthography *and* morphological analysis.**

| col 1 (UM) | col 4 (vdV) | col 7 (Gospel) |
|---|---|---|
| `rickat` | `rickat` | `rĭkat` |
| `ougla` | — | `äwla` |
| `sillala` | `sillala` | `si-lala` |
| `gmithit` | — | `x‹m›itxid` |
| `smidada` | `smidada` | `sidada` |

Of the 512:
- **196 (38%) carry morpheme hyphens** — `ma-irang`, `si-lala`, `măka-kuna`, `pa-ta-äwing-an`
- **31 carry an infix bracket** `‹m›` — `k‹m›äth?`, `r‹m›avak`, `x‹m›itxid`
- **213 (42%) contain a character the corpus has never held** — `ä`×109, `ĭ`×84, `ŭ`×35, `ă`×27, `‹›`×17, `ǝ`×10, `’`×8, `ǐ`×7, `ÿ`×2, `ḡ`×2

### Residue after mechanical stripping

| n | state |
|---:|---|
| 406 | single clean token — **but 196 of these carry hyphens** |
| 57 | two words left (`sako-a-la-lingaw- an`, `cf. kaäwlung`) |
| 36 | two forms, comma or slash — `rama/dama`, `ilpŭd, ilput, ĭlput` |
| 15 | 3+ words — `taäwf to cover`, `ka tukad ta äwvan`, `avang ka talu` |
| 5 | empty — pure citation (`SMG dove`, `[maru Li 2010: 406]`) |
| 2 | placeholder `-` |

### ⚠️ Four structural problems with publishing it as `FORM kindOf="alternate"`

1. 🔴 **The dialect cannot be recorded.** `dialect` is a **TEXT-level** attribute and
   this corpus declares `dialect="Siraya"`. There is no per-FORM dialect, so a
   Gospel-dialect form would be published under the Siraya label with only `@notes`
   to say otherwise. Same shape as the `trv` Seediq/Truku problem.
2. **Morpheme hyphens at S level.** POL-014/015 put segmentation markers on W/M.
   This corpus has neither tier, so 196 alternate FORMs would carry morpheme
   boundaries in an S-level FORM — a convention nothing else in the bank uses.
3. **The infix notation is `‹m›` (U+2039/203A)**, not the `<m>` POL-014 uses. Either
   normalize, or admit a second notation.
4. **Nothing validates any of it.** There is no `QC/validation/reference/Siraya/`,
   and if one is ever written these 13 characters decide its inventory.

### 🟢 One worry that does NOT apply

**Token counts are unaffected.** `corpus_counts.select_sentence_form` takes
`standard` then `original` and never `alternate`, so 512 extra FORMs would not move
the corpus statistics or the `token-comparison` CI check.

## 2026-09-07 — 🔑 The bracket kind is decided by the COLUMN, not by the content. `bran[d]enende` resolved.

⚠️ **First, a correction to an assumption:** *"I assume all three cases are
working."* **Nothing is implemented.** The `[recte ie[e]ts]` demonstration was a
regex trap being shown, not a fix being tested — the blanket
`square_brackets_to_parentheses` is still what runs. The bracket ruling is recorded,
not written.

### 🔑 Split the 37 cells by column and the classification becomes structural

| column | cells | every single one is… |
|---|---:|---|
| **2 `um_belgica`** + **3 `vdv_dutch`** — the historical Dutch | **20** | **editorial apparatus about the manuscript** — `[sic]`, `[recte …]`, `[normaliter …]`, `[… scored through]`, `[LMD …]`, `[?racken]`, `[kopjen]`, `bran[d]enende` |
| **5 `english`** — *My English*, Joby's own | **17** | **Joby's own writing** — elaboration (`[animal] pen`, `sirih [betel nut]`, `[bed] bug`, `shoe[s]`) or his citations |

**No exceptions in either direction.** That is a much better rule than my content
classification: Joby does not emend his own English, and the manuscript's Dutch is
not his to elaborate. **Same typography, opposite jobs, and the column says which.**

### 🟢 So `bran[d]enende` is NOT a rule-4 case

`shoe[s]` is in col 5 — Joby's own optional plural, two genuine readings, split it.
`bran[d]enende` is in cols 2/3 — **an editor supplying a letter the manuscript
lacks.** It offers no alternative for a reader to choose between, so a `ver="alt"`
TRANSL would assert `branenende kole` as a Dutch translation of `vaga`, which it is
not.

**On "neither is an actual Dutch word" — the emended one nearly is.** The corpus's
own Dutch has `branden` 'to burn' (rows 268, 928, 970), `brandt` 'fire', `brant hout`
'firewood'. Period Dutch for 'burning coal' is **`brandende kole`**. So the
manuscript looks to carry a dittography — `brand·en·ende` for `brand·ende` — *on top
of* the missing `d`. `brandenende` is a recognisable scribal form of `brandende`;
`branenende` is not.

⏳ **Recommendation: publish the emended `brandenende kole`, with `@notes` recording
that the manuscript reads `branenende` and Joby supplies the `d`.** The reader gets
a readable gloss, the source reading is still on record, and nothing non-existent is
asserted as a translation.

### The ruleset, restated by column

**Cols 2 / 3 — always apparatus (20 cells)**
1. **supplied letter inside a word** → keep the letter in the text, note the supply — **2 cells** (row 110, both columns)
2. **an alternative reading of the whole word** → `ver="alt"` TRANSL — **3 cells** (133 `copien [kopjen]`, 516 `vilt hoen [velt hoen?]`, 1033 `raeken [?racken]`)
3. **everything else** → `@notes`, dropped from the text — **15 cells**

**Col 5 — always Joby's own (17 cells)**
4. **elaboration** → inline, `[ ]` → `( )` — **13 cells**
5. **citations** → `@notes` — **3 cells** (457 `[WNT …]`, 516 `[LMD patrijs]`, 981 `[Murakmi: …]`)
6. **`shoe[s]`** → two translations, `shoe` primary — **1 cell**

🟢 Trap 3 is dissolved: only `shoe[s]` splits, and its primary is not in doubt.

## 2026-09-07 — 🟢 RULED: the four-way bracket rule. Three implementation traps.

Replaces `translation_cleanup.square_brackets_to_parentheses` wholesale:

| kind | n | ruled |
|---|---:|---|
| editorial apparatus / citations | 15 | → **`@notes`, dropped from the TRANSL text** |
| naturalistic elaboration | 13 | → **stays inline**, `[ ]` → `( )` |
| `ie[e]ts` | 3 | → always inside a `[recte …]`, so **rule 1 carries it** |
| supplied letters `bran[d]enende`, `shoe[s]` | 3 | → **two translations**, `shoe` + `shoes` |
| alternative readings | 3 | → **`ver="alt"` TRANSL** |

🟢 This also disposes of the 76 self-inflicted **V122** findings: after it, the only
parentheses left in TRANSL are the 13 deliberate ones.

### ⏳ Trap 1 — the apparatus brackets NEST, and a non-greedy regex breaks them

    'jeest [recte ie[e]ts]'
       \[[^\]]*\]  ->  'jeest ts]'      <-- BROKEN, dangling bracket
       to the last ] ->  'jeest'         <-- correct

Three cells: **604, 910, 916**. Any implementation must match to the **outermost**
closing bracket, not the first.

### ⏳ Trap 2 — row 573 loses its translation entirely

`[alhoewel scored through]` is **100% apparatus** in both col 2 and col 3, and row
573 has no English. After rule 1 it has **no TRANSL at all**, only a note. It is
also `[?metuso]`, one of the 17 added records. Intended?

### ⏳ Trap 3 — which reading is primary under rule 4?

- `shoe[s]` → `shoe` looks primary, `shoes` the alt.
- `bran[d]enende kole` → the *written* form is `branenende`, the *emended* one
  `brandenende`. Here the emendation is presumably primary — the opposite way round.

POL-025 needs one primary and the rest `ver="alt"`, so the choice has to be stated.

### ⚠️ Scope note: column 7 has 21 more of these, doing two different jobs

Of its 123 bracketed cells: **90** are lowercase English glosses (stripped anyway
under "Siraya text only"), **5** are citations, and **21** are attached to a word —
but they split into two kinds the same rule cannot serve:

- **supplied letters** — `[ta]taväx`, `taäw[f]`, `m[a]-angal`, `m-ä[x]dăkŭn`,
  `pa-iup [h]iup` → rule 4 (two readings)
- **optional affixes** — `[m-]ui`, `[tu-]rbo`, `[tu-]hili`, `[ma-]parit`,
  `[ka-]ingox`, `[mi-]laklak`, `[pa-u-]tiri` → a *different* thing: an affix the
  Gospel form may or may not carry. POL-026 (optional material) is the closer fit.

⏳ Not urgent — column 7 is its own project — but the same four-way analysis will be
needed there, plus a fifth kind.

**Net TRANSL effect:** +3 alt (rule 4) · +3 alt (rule 5) · −2 removed (row 573) ·
15 apparatus notes added.

## 2026-09-07 — 🔴 NO, the brackets are NOT handled. One blanket rule, and it is the wrong shape.

Maintainer: *"there are parentheticals that need to be handled. Are they being
handled? How?"* **Answer: no.** There is exactly one rule and it applies to
everything:

    "translation_cleanup": {
      "square_brackets_to_parentheses": true,     <- every [..] becomes (..)
      "preserve_raw_in_notes": true               <- raw kept in @notes
    }

**None of the 37 bracketed translation cells is covered by a
`translation_decision`** — the 14 that exist are all slash-splits (`mat/matting`).
So every bracket in a translation is converted to a parenthesis and **published
inline**, whatever it contains. Verified by running `canonical_translation`:

| source | published today |
|---|---|
| `governuer [sic]` | `governuer (sic)` |
| `aansien [pissing scored through]` | `aansien (pissing scored through)` |
| `in de panne ieest branden [recte ieets]` | `in de panne ieest branden (recte ieets)` |
| `bran[d]enende kole` | `bran(d)enende kole` |

### 🔴 This contradicts POL-024, and it manufactures its own QC warnings

POL-024 says analytic material belongs in a **`ver="alt"` TRANSL or `@notes`, not
inline**; only *naturalistic* elaboration may stay. The blanket rule does the
opposite — it forces **everything** inline.

**And it is the sole cause of the V122 findings.** Counted in the published XML:
**38 `(` + 38 `)` = 76**, exactly the `V122 parens_slashes` total, across 35 TRANSL
elements. ⚠️ **So the README's disposition is wrong on the facts**: it calls them
*"balanced source parentheticals"*, but the source has no parentheses there — it has
square brackets, and this rule converts them. The warning is self-inflicted.

### 📋 The 37 cells, classified

Full list: [bracket-cells.tsv](2026-09-07-pr172-utrecht-bracket-cells.tsv).

| n | class | treatment |
|---:|---|---|
| **15** | **editorial apparatus / citation** — `[sic]` ×2, `[… scored through]` ×4, `[recte …]`, `[normaliter inkt]`, `[LMD …]` ×5, `[WNT …]`, `[Murakmi: …]` | ⏳ `@notes`, or dropped. **Not** translation. |
| **13** | **naturalistic / lexicographic elaboration** — `[animal] pen`, `sirih [betel nut]`, `[bed] bug`, `to wink [with the eyes]`, `dear [expensive]`, `[cloth, nets]`, `[hollowed out wooden vessel…]` | 🟢 POL-024: **may stay inline, and auditors must not flag them** |
| **6** | 🔴 **supplied letters** — `bran[d]enende`, `shoe[s]`, `ie[e]ts` ×3 | 🔴 **brackets must survive.** `bran(d)enende` turns a manuscript supply-mark into a parenthetical aside — a real corruption |
| **3** | **alternative readings** — `copien [kopjen]`, `vilt hoen [velt hoen?]`, `raeken [?racken]` | ⏳ POL-024/POL-025: a `ver="alt"` TRANSL |

*(Three cells are in two classes at once: `jeest [recte ie[e]ts]` at rows 604, 910,
916 nests a supplied letter inside an apparatus note.)*

⏳ **So the blanket rule needs replacing with a three-way split**, and the two
already-ruled cases (457, 981 → remove the bracket; 1017 → keep it) are instances of
the first and second classes, not exceptions. ⚠️ **The recovered text adds to every
class** — `[recte ieets]`, `[pissing scored through]`, `[hollowed out wooden
vessel…]`, `WNT: Naäarden`, the Adelaar and Li citations.

17,373 word-level rows, all carrying text:

| `top` outside `[145,550)` | 6,000 | 🟢 **boilerplate only** |

| kept | 11,314 | |

**Proof for the 6,000:** every one of the 75 pages carries **exactly 80** such words,
and once `Page N of 75` is normalised there is **exactly one distinct text** across
all 75 pages — the running title, the column headings, the key, and the footer
`06/04/2021 Page N of 75`.

ledger — *the extractor's own output*), the published XML on both sides,
`source_reconciliation.csv`, `source_decisions.json`. **Not** the PDF: it is

container, and there is no network to fetch it. Every "seen on the page" in these
entries is the **maintainer's** reading, recorded — I have removed one ambiguous
passive phrasing from the report that could have been read otherwise.

**🔑 Why this matters more than a caveat.** An audit of the ledger inherits every
one of the extractor's blind spots. **The 47 dropped lines were invisible to me for
exactly the reason they are missing from the corpus** — the ledger is the shadow,
not the thing. That is why the page-top bug was found by reading the source and not
by reading the output, and it is the strongest argument for reading the two against
each other before this corpus is published. The same limit applies to column 7,
which nothing here has checked against the page at all.

### 🔴🔴 CONFIRMED BUG — maintainer diagnosed it; **47 lines across 38 pages are dropped**

Maintainer: *"Maybe you are simply not stripping out the first row because the first
column is blank for that row?"* **Exactly right, and it is systematic.**

**Mechanism.** `extract_rows` only collects words into bands running from one
detected row start to the next, and `_row_starts` detects a start **only from a
column-1 line** (`if line["column"] != 1: continue`). Anything on a page **above the
first detected start** falls into no band and is silently discarded. A page whose
top line has a blank column 1 — the continuation of an entry begun on the previous
page — therefore loses that line's Dutch, English and everything else.

**Measured from the ledger's own coordinates.** A normal page's first row sits at
`top = 153.28`; one text line is 11.16pt.

| first row at | = lines low | pages | lines lost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 153.28 (normal) | 0 | 37 | 0 |
| 164.44 | 1 | 31 | 31 |
| 175.60 | 2 | 6 | 12 |
| 198.04 | 4 | 1 | 4 |
| | | **38** | **47** |

⏳ **The 7 multi-line pages are where content actually sits** — both known losses are
among them, and on the 1-line pages the previous entry's cells all look complete
(`wolcke`/`cloud`), consistent with an empty wrap line:

| pdf p. | lines | previous page's last entry | status |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 6 | 2 | 75 `attatallachang` — **no Dutch** | 🔴 loss (Dutch is on the dropped line) |
| 58 | 2 | 822 `kmoulaling` — **no Dutch, no English** | 🔴 loss (confirmed on the page) |
| **12** | **4** | 152 `vangara` | ⏳ check |
| 32 | 2 | 450 `havour` | ⏳ check |
| 56 | 2 | 796 `achqua` | ⏳ check |
| 61 | 2 | 865 `liddig pissing` | ⏳ check |
| 72 | 2 | 1013 `sillala` | ⏳ check |

🟢 **The fix is in `_row_starts`/`extract_rows`, and it is not "extend the first
band upward"** — the orphaned lines belong to the **previous page's last row**, not
to the first row of the current page. Either carry that band across the page break,
or stop requiring a row start to come from column 1.

### 🟢 FIX WRITTEN + TESTED — but ⏳ **CANNOT RERUN: no PDF, no `pdftotext`, no network**

Branch **`fix/utrecht-page-top-rows`** in `/workspace/wt-utrecht-audit`, commit
**`ad9a5f224`** (off PR head `a592064e0`). Not pushed.

`extract_source.py`: the last row of each page now also claims the **next** page's
leading orphan lines, via a new `_page_top_orphans()`. ⚠️ **Not "extend the first
band upward"** — the orphans belong to the *previous* page's last row. Row detection
is untouched, so **the row count cannot change**.

**Verified by fixture, since the real rerun is impossible here.**
`CodeAndDocs/tests/test_page_top_orphans.py` builds a synthetic `pdftotext -tsv`
document reproducing the geometry. Run against the **original** extractor it fails
on exactly the dropped cell; against the **patched** one all three pass:

    original:  1 failed, 2 passed   (the orphan 'twee' is lost)
    patched:   3 passed

🔎 **The fixture exposed a second property of the algorithm worth knowing:** a row
start is recognised **only when a column-2..5 word sits beside the column-1 one**.
My first fixture gave the page's last entry a column-1 cell alone and it was not
detected as a row *at all*. Row 822 survives only because it has `vdv_siraya` in
column 4. **So an entry with column 1 and nothing else is dropped whole** — a
distinct latent bug, unquantifiable without the PDF.

⏳ **Blockers to actually rerunning:** `Private/JobyUtrechtManuscript.pdf` is absent
(gitignored, POL-048), `pdftotext` is not installed, and there is no network to
fetch the PDF. **The rerun and its diff are the maintainer's to run.**

⏳ **When it is rerun:** `source_decisions.json`'s `rows_sha256` **will change** and
must be updated, or `load_source` raises *"source row payload SHA-256 drifted"* and
the build stops. Expected diff: content **added** to the last row of up to 38 pages;

### 🔑 Why the PDF would still help: `pdftotext` is NOT the lossy part

Maintainer: *"Are you saying the extractor isn't pulling all the text? If so, why
would having pdftotext and the pdf help?"*

**`pdftotext -tsv` emits every word in the text layer, each with page / top / left.
Nothing is lost there.** All four losses happen *downstream*, in
`extract_source.py`'s own row assembly:

| # | filter | drops | measured? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `level != "5"` | container rows, no text | not a loss |
| 2 | `top` outside `[145.0, 550.0)` | headers / footers | ❓ **never checked** |
| 3 | `left` outside `[50.0, 842.0)` (`_column_for_word` → `None`) | left and right margins | ❓ **never checked** |
| 4 | above a page's first detected row start | **47 lines** | ✅ measured, fixed on `fix/utrecht-page-top-rows` |

So the raw TSV is the complete text and the ledger is a filtered view of it. Reading
the TSV would let me (a) read the 47 dropped lines verbatim, (b) verify the fix
recovers exactly them, (c) **quantify filters 2 and 3, which nobody has looked at**,
and (d) check column 7 — the least trustworthy part of this audit — against the
actual text.

🟢 **I do not need the PDF itself, only `pdftotext -tsv` output.** One command, and
the result is plain text that can be handed over or committed.

    brew install poppler        # pdftotext ships in poppler, not under its own name
    pdftotext -tsv Corpora/UtrechtManuscriptWordList/Private/JobyUtrechtManuscript.pdf utrecht.tsv

### 🔴 NEW FINDING: `pdftotext` is an undeclared system dependency

`brew install pdftotext` fails — *"No available formula."* The binary ships in
**poppler**. This is a real gap, not just a papercut:

- `extract_source.py` calls `shutil.which("pdftotext")` and raises
  *"pdftotext is required to extract the source table"* — a clear runtime error, but
  only after the user has already fetched a 1 MB PDF.
- **`CodeAndDocs/requirements.txt` pins only `lxml==5.3.0`.** No system dependency is
  declared anywhere.
- **The README's Reproducibility section never mentions it**: it lists `pip install`,
  `mkdir Private`, `curl` the PDF, run `make_xml.sh`. A reader following it exactly
  hits the failure — as the maintainer just did.

⏳ **Fix with the other POL-047 work:** name poppler in the README (and note that the
formula is `poppler`, not `pdftotext`, since that is the actual trap), and state the
dependency where the build declares its others.

⏳ **Worth considering: commit the TSV.** The corpus commits only the *post-processed*
`source_records.json`, so step 1 remains unreproducible without a gitignored
`Private/` PDF (the POL-048 gap). Committing the raw TSV would close that properly —
and it exposes no more than the XML already published under the same CC BY-NC grant.

## 2026-09-07 — 🔴 RULED: the Utrecht column mapping. 3 of 7 columns wrong; a 10-row transposition found.

**Maintainer read the PDF and gave the spec.** Column 1 is correct/authoritative;
cols 2+3 are two Dutch translations with **vdV (col 3) as the standard** and col 2
as an **`alt` Dutch** where it differs (**not `dum`** — that is 13th century);
col 4 (vdV Siraya) becomes an **alternate FORM** where it differs from col 1; col 5
is English as normal; **col 6 (Murakami) ignored**; col 7 (Gospel Formulary) becomes
an **alternate FORM, Siraya text only** — ignore its translations and annotations.
Cols 8–10 ignored.

### Conformance of `main` and #172 against that spec

| col | source | ruled destination | `main` | #172 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `um_formosana` 1061 | `FORM` original | ❌ vdV in 17 rows | ✅ |
| 2 | `um_belgica` 1046 | `TRANSL nld ver="alt"`, **only where ≠ col 3 → 49 rows** | ❌ 1052 × `dum` | ❌ 1046 × `dum` |
| 3 | `vdv_dutch` 1046 | `TRANSL nld` (standard) | ✅ | ✅ |
| 4 | `vdv_siraya` 1060 | `FORM kindOf="alternate"` where ≠ col 1 → **123 rows** | ❌ absent | ❌ absent |
| 5 | `english` 1049 | `TRANSL eng` | ❌ tagged `en` | ✅ |
| 6 | `murakami` 1050 | ignore | ✅ | ✅ |
| 7 | `gospel_formulary` 519 | `FORM kindOf="alternate"`, Siraya only | ❌ absent | ❌ absent |

**Net effect of the ruling:** TRANSL **3,156 → 2,144** (1,046 `nld` + **49** `nld
alt` + 1,049 `eng`; the whole duplicate `dum` tier goes). Alternate FORM **0 →
642** (123 + 519).

### 🔴 FINDING: 11 rows publish the Siraya word as their Dutch translation

⚠️ **CORRECTION — my first diagnosis was wrong, twice.** I called it "columns 3
and 4 transposed by a band-boundary straddle at 280pt." **The maintainer is
right that this is impossible**: col 1 is band 70–140 and col 3 is band 215–280,
nowhere near each other, and a horizontal shift produces a *shift*, not a
transposition. Also the run is **eleven rows, not ten** — row 233 belongs to it
too (missed because its col 1 carries the `i.e.` apparatus while col 3 does not).

**What the data actually shows.** The table is **mirrored**: left to right the
four leading columns run `Siraya · Dutch ‖ Dutch · Siraya`, van der Vlis's cells
simply repeating the UM values wherever he agrees. **902 rows** carry that full
pattern (band3 == UM Dutch in 1,012; band4 == UM Siraya in 937). For
**rows 223–233** the second pair is *reversed* — `Siraya · Dutch ‖ Siraya ·
Dutch`. Rows 222 and 234 either side are normal.

**🔑 `main` has the identical anomaly on the identical eleven rows.** Two files
built a year apart by different hands from the same PDF do not invent the same
reversal on the same eleven consecutive rows. **So it is almost certainly in the
source table**, not in either extraction — a stretch where the spreadsheet's two
van der Vlis columns were filled in the other order.

Published consequence in **both** files, ids `W220`–`W230`:

    <S id="W220">
      <FORM kindOf="original">ama ka vacho</FORM>
      <TRANSL xml:lang="dum">bruydegom</TRANSL>
      <TRANSL xml:lang="nld">ama ka vacho</TRANSL>   ← the Siraya form, as Dutch
      <TRANSL xml:lang="eng">bridegroom</TRANSL>

Forms: `ama ka vacho`, `ina ka vacho`, `allack`, `tabung`, `topey`, `tagallack`,
`merauwey`, `rauwey`, `sama`, `sena`, `kinikapateijang kitbong`. Wrong either
way, and published since 2025-08-10.

**🟢 RULED — maintainer checked the PDF: all 11 are swapped in the source**,
including the two at the foot of p.16 (`ama ka vacho`, `ina ka vacho`). My reading
was right: it is **one run aligned to a manuscript page, not a PDF page** — it
begins exactly at manuscript page marker `12` (row 223; markers `11`@201, `12`@223,
`13`@246) and the PDF page break falls two entries into it, which is what made p.16
look clean.

**🟢 Remedy: a decision record, not code.** Extent is known exactly, so add a range
entry to `source_decisions.json` swapping the two vdV columns for rows 223–233,
alongside the existing `form_decisions`/`mapping_overrides`. No code change, no PDF
at build time. Under the new mapping vdV then agrees on all eleven → his Dutch
becomes `nld`, and they contribute **no** alternate FORM.

⏳ **Proposed shared check regardless: no `nld` TRANSL may equal its own `FORM`.**
Catches this run in both files *and* `main`'s two Dutch-in-FORM rows (824/885).

### 🟡 The `mokoqua` weirdness — explained, and it opens a bigger question

Maintainer flagged the `mokoqua` row on p.16. It is the PR's **row 221 `tbong`**,
inserted between `mokoqua` 'married man' and `kegaing` 'married woman', with **no
Dutch and no English at all**. On `main` it was not a record — it was the tail of
a single form `mokoqua tbong`.

**It is a real entry**: it carries its own Gospel equivalent `tbung, tbŭng
[spouse]` and its own etymology `*Cǝbung` Proto-South Formosan. Nobody gives an
etymology to a line-wrap. So the PR's split is right and `main`'s merge was wrong;
the oddity is that Joby gives this headword no gloss of its own. *(Incidental
extraction artefact, in columns we ignore: that etymology is cut across bands —
`*Cǝbung Proto-South` in col 9, `Formosan` in col 10.)*

### 🟢 The 17 recovered records: all genuine. Geometry settles it.

⚠️ **I briefly claimed row spacing couldn't tell a wrapped line from an entry, and
downgraded 5 of the 17 to "needs a call". That was wrong — I had the line height
wrong.** Maintainer: *"The gap between entries is generally larger than between
wrapped lines."* Correct, and the coordinates prove it.

**One text line is 11.16pt. Every gap between detected rows is a whole multiple of
it, and the smallest anywhere in 1,061 rows is 2.00 lines.** Nothing sits at one.
So an entry occupies **two** lines minimum and each wrapped line adds exactly one —
and the gap tracks the previous entry's length monotonically, which is a wrap model
and nothing else:

| gap | n | longest cell in the entry above (median) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2.00 lines (22.32pt) | 706 | 11 chars |
| 3.00 lines (33.48pt) | 220 | 22 |
| 4.00 lines (44.7pt) | 45 | 32 |
| 5.01 lines (55.92pt) | 5 | 55 |

`_row_starts` requires **≥20pt between row starts** — more than one line, less than
two — so **a continuation line cannot be promoted to a row.** Observed minimum
22.2pt shows the filter never misfired. **All 17 added rows sit at a clean 2.00- or
3.00-line gap.** So: `+17 recovered, nothing invented` stands as first reported;
`main` merged them because `main`'s builder did not do this.

**Scope of the proof:** it establishes the row *detection* is sound. It says nothing
about band assignment *within* a row — which is where 223–233 went wrong, and where
an error in a column that repeats nothing would leave no trace.

## 2026-09-07 — 🟢 RULED: #172 Utrecht rights = `CC BY-NC 4.0`. And: we are *not* changing Joby.

**Maintainer ruling.** *"Yes, CC BY-NC 4.0."* So POL-042 is satisfied by the PR's
value and the POL-044 override is authorized — ⏳ but see the note below: the red
check will say *"added"*, and the override should record that it is really
**`CC-BY-NC-ND ` → `CC BY-NC 4.0`**, i.e. a published `ND` restriction being
dropped, not a new corpus.

### Maintainer question: *"I don't think Joby has any OCR. I thought he sent us an excel file? If so, I'm not sure why we are making changes."*

**You are right that there is no OCR, and you are right to push — but the changes
are not changes to Joby. `main` was never Joby.**

**On OCR:** none, on the PR side. `extract_source.py` runs `pdftotext -tsv` on a
**born-digital** PDF (printed from a spreadsheet — the script's own comment says
so). A scan would return no text and the build's `EXPECTED_ROWS = 1061` assert
would fail. The residual risk is **layout reconstruction**, not character
recognition: the extractor assigns words to columns by x-coordinate bands and
joins them with a single space. That is what row 122 looks like.

**On the Excel: it is not here, and never has been.** No `.xlsx`/`.csv` for this
corpus exists anywhere in FormosanBank history. `main`'s file was added in **one
commit — `ae7402c98`, 2025-08-10, carolinemkowalski, "Create
UtrechtManuscriptWordList"** — with no script, no source file, no README. Its
provenance is unrecorded. ⏳ **If Joby sent an Excel, it never reached this
repo.** (Note POL-048 would prefer the PDF anyway: it is publicly fetchable and
hash-pinnable, so a third party can reproduce; an Excel living only in Basecamp
cannot be a build input.)

### 🔑 The decisive evidence: Joby's table carries three Siraya witnesses per row

`um_formosana` (Joby's corrected UM reading) · `vdv_siraya` (van der Vlis 1842) ·
`murakami` (Murakami 1933). **In all 17 spelling changes `main` matches van der
Vlis — and Murakami where it differs — and does *not* match Joby.**

The three bolded rows are Joby arguing the point **in his own words** — the `l/b?`

## 2026-09-07 — AUDIT: #172 Utrecht. Good corpus, cannot rebuild. And a correction to what I said on 2026-09-04.

Audited under `audit-dev-repo` in worktree `/workspace/wt-utrecht-audit`
(detached at PR head `a592064e0`, sparse). **Nothing modified.** Skill refreshed
first — see the entry below this one.

### 🔴 The blocker: the PR deletes an input its own build needs

**⚠️ Correction to the 2026-09-04 entry**, which said *"the committed
`source/source_records.json` is that step's output, so `generate_xml.py` alone
rebuilds the corpus — the entry point just needs a skip path."* **That is
wrong.** `generate_xml.py` also calls `load_predecessor()` on
`source_decisions.json → predecessor.path = "source/public_predecessor.xml"`,
and **that file is not in the PR.** Verified by running it:

    FileNotFoundError: .../CodeAndDocs/source/public_predecessor.xml

The predecessor is the 285,055-byte blob published at
`Corpora/UtrechtManuscriptWordList` on `main` — SHA-256 `75467c70…` matches
`source_decisions.json` exactly. The PR's **second commit is literally
`a592064e0 "remove the old predecessor"`**: it moves that blob to
`XML/Siraya/Utrecht_Manuscript.xml` and never re-commits it under
`CodeAndDocs/source/`.

**The fix is two lines and I verified it works.** Restore the blob from `main`
into `CodeAndDocs/source/public_predecessor.xml`, then:

    generate_xml.py --output …  →  cmp against committed XML  →  BYTE-IDENTICAL

So **no PDF and no `Private/` are needed to rebuild** — `extract_source.py`
(step 1, the only `Private/` consumer) just needs a skip path when
`source_records.json` is already present and its `rows_sha256` matches. POL-048
then passes outright.

### 🟢 What the PR is actually worth — more than the value audit said

The 5 Sep artifact said Utrecht *"is absent from `main` altogether."* Not quite:
`main` publishes it as an **extensionless file directly in `Corpora/`**, and
that file is

- **malformed XML** — no closing `</TEXT>` (the PR's loader literally appends
  one to parse it, and asserts the tag is absent);
- **schema-invalid** — 1,052 `W` elements as direct children of `TEXT`, no `S`;
- invisible to every `Corpora/*/XML/**` glob, so it has **no `statistics/` row**
  and has never been validated;
- `xml:lang="en"` on English `TRANSL` (not `eng`); `copyright="CC-BY-NC-ND "`
  with a trailing space; no `citation`, no `dialect`;
- carrying **4 duplicate ids** (`W2`, `W474`–`W476`) and one numeric-only id
  `725` that is not a legal XML ID.

The PR fixes all of that. It is a repair of a broken publication, not a new port.

### Content: verified, and better than `main` on every axis I could measure

| | main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| lexical records | 1,052 | **1,061** |
| distinct ids | 1,048 | 1,061 |
| TRANSL | 3,156 | 3,156 |
| standard FORM | 1,052 | **0** |

- **+17 recovered records.** `main` had merged adjacent source rows into one
  entry (`vignanang, euvanang`, `rauwat, rapas`, `touding, tousimer`, …). The
  PR splits them; I traced every one of the 9 I sampled to its own `S`.
  **Nothing dropped.**
- **−8 retirements, all genuine extraction garbage**: 6 spurious bare `samma`
  rows (page-flow bleed from `Deus samma`), one exact duplicate of `W2`, and
  `W351` = `samma` glossed 'heel' — a column misalignment whose real record
  survives correctly as `W350 gnouro` 'heel'. The real 'father' lexeme is
  present as `W231 sama`. **Verified lossless.**
- **2 records where `main` had a Dutch gloss sitting in the Siraya FORM**
  (`W816` = *schouldig zijn*, `W879` = *malkaar roepen laten…*). The PR gives
  `kmougitting` and `macklingit`.
- **12 `form_decisions`** strip editorial apparatus (`[deleted]`, `i.e. …`,
  `?raam`, `<m> verb infix`) into `FORM/@notes` — POL-016-consistent, and the
  raw text is preserved, not discarded.

### 🟡 The one (a)-concern finding, and a witness question for you

I ran the obvious hypothesis — that 22 forms changed because of OCR drift — and
it is **not** that. Of the 1,044 mapped records, **1,006 of `main`'s forms are
byte-identical to Joby's `um_formosana` column**; the 22 that differ are the
ones where **`main` took the van der Vlis 1842 column instead**. Six of those 22
are cosmetic (the PR trims the same editorial suffix anyway). The remaining
**14 are a deliberate change of source witness**:

| `main` (van der Vlis 1842) | PR (Joby's corrected UM) |
|---|---|
| `mattakong` · `tbong` · `smaladilong` · `mavavongog` | `mattakoug` · `tboug` · `smaladiloug` · `mavavougog` |
| `valangavong` · `tavarolong` · `cangirg` · `allincho` | `valongavong` · `tavarotong` · `canging` · `alincho` |
| `meilil` · `ninnam` · `magoupoupaag` · `kmoulimlimoug` | `meillil` · `ninnim` · `magoupoupgag` · `kmoubimlimoug` |
| `gmilingig` · `maccacogog` | `gmillingig` · `maccacocog` |

The README already rules on this — van der Vlis is *"a comparison witness, not
the authority for Joby's corrected Siraya forms"* — and the `ng`↔`ug` pattern is
exactly the minim confusion Joby was correcting. ⏳ **I think the PR is right;
it is your call to confirm.**

⏳ **One likely regression I cannot close without the PDF** (no network here):

    row 122   main: pasagoualalingauang     PR: pasagoualalingaua ng

The ledger's own `vdv_siraya` cell reads `pasagoualalingauang` unspaced. I
checked every row whose form ends in a ≤3-letter token — **13 rows, and row 122
is the only one where `um_formosana` and `vdv_siraya` differ by a space.** The
extractor joins PDF words with a single space, and the same row's
`gospel_formulary_equivalent` cell shows a wrap (`sako-a-la-lingaw- an`), so a
**cell line-wrap** is the likely cause. Needs one look at page 9.

**Clean:** POL-049 (touches no shared code), POL-046 (only source-specific
parsing is corpus-local), POL-041 (no W tier anywhere — normal), POL-051
(removals are enumerated with reasons in `source_reconciliation.csv` and

## 2026-09-07 — `ř` design settled (per-word + `*`); `(next.morning)` corrected

Branch **13 commits**, GitBook **8**.

### `ř`: standardize per word, star the rest — the corpus can have PHON after all

**Maintainer ruling.** Standardize `ř` word by word where the value is known;
leave it as written where it is not, accepting a `*` in the standard PHON. In
the orthography profile `ř` maps to **`*`** rather than to a letter. *"This
isn't ideal, but it's better than leaving this corpus entirely without PHON or
standard."*

`claudeplans/2026-09-07-wakelin-orthography-proposal/r_caron_words.tsv`:

| Wakelin | → standard | modern tokens | conf |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `ařwa` 'two' | `adoa` | 87 | high |
| `kařwan` 'other' | `kadoan` | 30 | high |
| `ařima` 'five' | `alima` | 64 | high (ruled) |
| `vařit` 'bamboo strips' | `vazit` 藤 | 9 | medium |
| `sipřutan` 'strike' | `sipzotan` 'whip' | 1 | LOW |

**9 of 15 `ř` tokens standardized; 6 keep `ř` and star** (`pasamuřna`,
`pasavuřen`, `pneřek`, `tiřarawa`, `vařangyam`, `řerchip`). Verified the
mechanism: `add_phonology` stars any character the profile does not map *and*
passes an explicit `*` through, so either route works — the explicit row is
better documentation, since an omission reads as an oversight.

**On a single IPA value** (the maintainer invited one): the least bad is **[ɽ]
retroflex flap** — all three modern reflexes are voiced coronals, and [ɽ] is
retroflex like `d` [ɖ], flapped like `z` [r], liquid like `l` [l], and is what
`ř` conventionally denoted in 1950s Americanist practice. I still recommend `*`,
because [ɽ] asserts a segment nobody has heard. The row is one edit either way.

**⏳ The blocker is now gone and the tables are landable in principle.** All
three original objections answered (glide rules expressible; `ř` handled by not
mapping it; coverage 78.7% is a judgement the maintainer has made). Remaining
work if it lands is listed in the proposal §6 — chiefly **verifying the column
contract** of the two TSVs against `standardize.py`/`add_phonology.py`, which I
have NOT done, and teaching the pipeline the per-word `ř` list (a shared-tool
extension, so its own PR under POL-049).

### Corpus: `(next-morning)` → `(next.morning)`

Maintainer correction to the source. One gloss for one morpheme, which the
transcription had split across two as `(next` + `morning)`. Now written with a
dot and placed whole on `pneřek`, same reasoning as `bamboo.strips`. The word
aligns and keeps its morphemes: **M-tier drops 23 → 22**.

⚠️ Other parenthesised multi-word glosses (`(one-after-another)`,
`(long-time-ago)`, `(stone-wall)`, ~15 more) keep their hyphens. The build counts
a parenthesised group as one unit and none is split across morphemes, so nothing
is broken; converting them for consistency would be a separate decision.

## 2026-09-07 — `-em` glossed PAR (33 M tiers recovered); `ř` resolved as *not* a letter mapping

Branch **12 commits**; GitBook **7**. `?` and the glide rules ruled agreed and
documented in README + GitBook.

### Implemented: the narration suffix

`-em`/`-m` glossed **`PAR`**, **during processing, not in the snapshot**, and
**before** the alignment check — so the words it repairs keep the morpheme tier
the suffix was costing them. **M-tier drops 54 → 23; 33 words recovered.**
37 W glossed. Only word-final qualifies (`m` is a prefix in `a-m-angay`).
Justified by Rau & Dong's 助/呢 on the modern cognate `am` and the bank's 4,679
`PAR` tokens; `-em` ~ `am` is the e~a correspondence the article's own note
predicts. Framed in the docs as *the article's note applied to the tier*, per
the maintainer, not a correction to the article.

Second rule added with it: **a morpheme gloss carrying half a parenthesis drops
the M tier** — `(next-morning)` split as `(next` + `morning)`. Those 2 words were
invisible while they were being dropped for miscounting; glossing the suffix
would have started publishing the broken halves.

🐛 **The morpheme-in-word invariant caught a sixth missed `ř`** — `pnerek` under
a word reading `pneřek`, hidden until `a-pneřek-em` stopped being dropped. Third
time that invariant has paid for itself.

### 🔴 `ř`: the answer is that there is no single answer

⚠️ **My first `ř` test was wrong — it omitted the glide rules.** Re-run with the
full ordered table (so `řw` resolves after `ř` is a real consonant):

| Wakelin | gloss | modern | via |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ařwa` | 'two' | **`adoa`** (87, 'two') | `ř`→`d` |
| `kařwan` | 'other' | **`kadoan`** (30, 'other') | `ř`→`d` |
| `ařima` | 'five' | `alima` (64, 五) | `ř`→`l` |
| `vařit` | 'bamboo strips' | `vazit` (9, 藤) | `ř`→`z` |
| `sipřutan` | 'strike' | `sipzotan` (1, whip) | `ř`→`z` |

That answers the maintainer's `kařwan` puzzle: it *does* have a modern
equivalent, `kadoan` 'other' — invisible before because `kařwan` was reaching
`karwan`/`kawan` rather than `kadoan`.

**Five resolvable words, three different modern letters; six unresolvable.**
Corpus-wide every candidate lands within 0.2 points (78.6–78.8%) because `ř` is
only 15 tokens — so aggregate attestation cannot decide, and gloss evidence
disagrees with itself. **Conclusion: `ř` is not a letter correspondence and must
not be a table row.** The `ř` row is deleted from the proposed conversion table;
it needs a per-word decision list, the shape the corpus already uses for its
alternations. ⚠️ Note raw frequency misleads: highest-count-per-word sends
`kařwan` to `kawan` (35) which is glossed 年 'year'.

### Correction to something I said

"Work from the Rau & Dong phonology" was not actionable and I should not have
offered it: the repo holds **only their XML corpus**, no grammar prose or PDF
(`Corpora/RauDong/CodeAndDocs/` is plots, `unique_characters.txt` and a script).
What actually decided the question was per-word gloss evidence from the corpus
itself, which is available and which I should have run first.
