## 2026-09-07 — #175: the ledger is transcribed FROM the published XML. Nothing produces it.

Maintainer asked where `source_records.json` comes from and whether code makes
it. Checked. **No code produces it, and its record fields are a verbatim
transcription of the XML that was already published.**

### Measured: ledger `records[]` vs `main`'s published XML, all 87

| ledger field | identical to `main`'s XML |
| --- | ---: |
| `output` | **87/87** |
| `language` | **87/87** |
| `source` | **87/87** |
| `audio_url` | **87/87** |
| `audio_file` | **87/87** |
| `dialect` | 41/87 *(the 46 are the intended change)* |

`recording_date` is a substring of `source` in **87/87** — so it is derived from
a field that is itself derived from the XML. `source_file` is the output
basename minus any `_N` part suffix in **84/87**, i.e. essentially mechanical.

**The only information in the ledger that the published XML did not already
contain:**

- `source_dialect_label` — 46 `North Western`, 2 `Southern`, 39 `null`. The one
  field that required a human reading the 71 scans. And the 2026-09-07 ruling
  has just made it inert for `@dialect` purposes.
- `sha256` + `pages` ×71 — mechanical, computed from PDFs already committed.
- One `disposition` paragraph for the excluded `Whitehorn_Paiwan_03A_01`.

The PR adds exactly two files (`generate_xml.py`, `source_records.json`). There
is **no ledger builder**, and neither the README nor the PR body says how the
ledger was produced or how to update it if a source PDF is ever replaced — the
hash check would simply start failing.

### 🟡 CORRECTION to my earlier framing

I called this *"reproduction is real"* and *"POL-048 satisfied outright."*
POL-048 is literally met — it builds from a FormosanBank checkout alone, no
private repo, no pinned second clone. But I should have been clearer that
**this is not reproduction from source.** The build reads the 71 PDFs only to
hash them; they are image-only scans with no text layer, so nothing could parse
them. The pipeline is *transcription-of-output → XML*.

Consequence: **`--check` verifies internal consistency, not fidelity.** A
transcription error would be self-certifying. (I checked — the five XML-derived
fields are 87/87 identical to `main`, so no transcription error exists today.)

That places Whitehorn squarely in **POL-035's "non-regenerable corpus"** branch,
where the ruling is *snapshot the XML into `CodeAndDocs/` and document it* —
which is what this actually is, and which is how
`claudeplans/rerun-standardize-readme-audit.md` already classified it
(*"XML/tables themselves are the hand product … n/a — POL-035 snapshot
instead"*). It is a **POL-035 snapshot plus an emitter**, presented as a
pipeline. The PR body's *"regenerate the 87 published records"* reads as
reproduction from source and should be reworded.

### What it is still worth — narrower than I said, but not nothing

1. **It is the only POL-038-legal path to change a published value here.** That
   is what makes the `CC BY-NC 4.0` update a one-line ledger edit instead of a
   hand edit of 87 files. Real, and immediately load-bearing.
2. **A machine-checked coverage contract** — 71 sources ↔ 87 records both ways,
   no orphans, no duplicate ids/outputs/audio files, every PDF hash-pinned. It
   is what surfaced the `03A_01` disposition (previously an empty XML deleted in
   `2288d4f` with no record).
3. Canonical formatting of 87 files.

What it does **not** buy: any independent check against the sources. Only a
human reading the scans can give that.

⏳ **New maintenance obligation, currently untooled:** the ledger is hand-
maintained from here on. Worth deciding whether that is acceptable or whether
the README should simply say the JSON is a committed snapshot of the published
XML (POL-035), which is the honest description.

## 2026-09-07 — Wakelin orthography, round 2: Ortho113 spec read; one of my claims overturned

Four maintainer leads, all four productive. Updated in
`claudeplans/2026-09-07-wakelin-orthography-proposal/`.

1. **`?` is a glottal stop — RESOLVED.** Ortho113 pp. 21-23 (§九 雅美) *removed*
   [ʔ] from the consonant table and moved it to the notes, which say `’` marks
   the glottal stop, "a consonant that causes a pause or breaks a syllable", and
   that the community **decided to keep it** while leaving it out of the tables.
   The maintainer's spot is decisive: the errata delete `?` **exactly twice**
   (A42, A43) and both are word-final **before the vowel-initial `u`** — the
   hiatus where a glottal is automatic. Of the 21 survivors, **8 are
   sentence-final and 10 precede a consonant**; only 3 precede a vowel. So it is
   a segment, not punctuation.
   ⏳ **The corpus README should be updated now**, independently of any table:
   it still says the glottal identification is unconfirmed.
   The conversion still deletes it, for a different reason — modern Yami writes
   `’` medially (668) and initially (306) but **word-finally 8 times in 135,435
   tokens, all apparent typos**. That is a **documented loss** in the standard
   tier, and a property of Ortho113, not a judgement about Wakelin.
2. **`ř` — still LOW, and now better understood.** Ortho113 defines a three-way
   `z`[r] trill / `r`[ɻ] approximant / `l`[l], which looked like a match for
   Wakelin's `l`/`r`/`ř`. It is not: **Wakelin's plain `r` already spans modern
   `r` (12 morphs) AND `z` (3: `zipos` 'relative', `zagaw` 'neck', `mazikna`
   'tired', all gloss-confirmed)**, while `l`→`l` is clean (10/11). Wakelin does
   not mirror the modern contrast, and `ř`'s three data points still go three
   ways. This is the one true blocker.
3. **🔴 I WAS WRONG about the glide rules.** I wrote that `Cw`→`Co` / `Cy`→`Ci`
   could not be expressed in the table format. **They can.**
   `standardize.apply_standard` iterates rows **in order** doing plain
   `str.replace`, so multi-character keys work and order is significant.
   Enumerating the 16 attested consonant+glide sequences as rows, placed after
   `ǥ`→`h` and `ch`→`c` and before the single-letter rows, reproduces the
   positional result exactly — **78.7% vs 78.6% of morph tokens, marginally
   better**. The 21-row table is written in that order and the order is
   load-bearing. **Lesson: check what the mechanism does before declaring a
   format limitation.**
4. **The `-em`/`-m` "narration suffix" has a standard gloss.** Rau & Dong gloss
   modern `am` as 助 'particle' (423x) and 呢 (369x), and `m` as 主焦 (62x); the
   bank-wide Yami data glosses `am` as **PAR**, 4,679 tokens. `-em` ~ `am` is an
   `e`~`a` correspondence the article's own "/e/ and /a/ fluctuate freely" note
   predicts. ⏳ **Worth a ruling**, because the prize is concrete: **35 of the 54
   words whose M tier was dropped for gloss misalignment are exactly this
   case**, and glossing it would restore their morphemes. But it would be an
   *editorial* gloss inferred from a modern cognate, against the standing rule
   that an unsupplied gloss is not published (which is why `unan` is dropped) —
   so it needs a deliberate decision and a `notes` marking, not a side-effect.

Recommendation unchanged — **do not turn the tables on** — but narrowed to one
blocker (`ř`) plus the 78.7% coverage question, since the format objection is
withdrawn.

## 2026-09-07 — Tang audio manifest salvaged from #168, source-only. Branch `corpus/tang-audio-manifest`

**Maintainer:** *"can we borrow the audio_manifest.json and verify_sources.py
… and leave the rest alone?"* Done. One commit **`e4b892053`**, rebased onto
`origin/main` `a64093535` (it went 4 behind mid-session; no overlap, clean
rebase, re-verified after). **Unpushed** — push is denied here. Worktree
`…/scratchpad/wt2`; GitBook `…/scratchpad/gb2`.

PR bodies were handed over **inline as heredocs**, not as `--body-file` paths:
the maintainer runs `gh` from a different container with no access to these
worktrees, and the earlier file-path form failed for exactly that reason.

### The gap it closes

**Nothing in the repository checked the audio's bytes — only its names.**
`validate_hf_audio` compares path *sets* plus `expected_audio_files`;
`download_audio.py` checks only that Git LFS resolved its pointers. `grep`
confirms **no `sha256` anywhere in the audio contract.** Audio replaced under
the same names passes every check we have.

### What was taken, and what was left

`audio_manifest.json` — byte size + SHA-256 per recording, with its Paradisec
item and source URL, pinned to the immutable HF revision. `verify_sources.py`
checks it three ways: committed metadata (default), the pinned revision
(`--live`), the WAVs on disk (`--local`).

**`--live` verifies 13.6 GB in one API call with nothing transferred** — HF
stores each LFS object under its SHA-256, so `lfs.oid` *is* the hash. Confirmed
against the live dataset: 30/30 exact on size and hash.

**Left behind entirely:** `prepare_audio.py`, the `post_download` hook, the two
`statistics/` rows that move only because of it, and the deletion of
`upload_hf_datasets.sh` (a real POL-046 item, but out of the requested scope —
⏳ still worth its own PR).

**Rebuilt, not copied.** The manifest was regenerated from the committed
metadata plus the live HF listing, then diffed against #168's source values:
**identical for all 30**. So #168's manifest was correct as committed.

**Two of #168's fields deliberately dropped.** The **licence** — audio inherits
the corpus `@copyright` and POL-045 says it is never recorded twice. **Frames
and durations** — not needed for identity (right size + right hash *is* the
right file), already owned by `statistics/audio_durations.csv`, and I could not
verify them here: HF's LFS redirect goes to a CDN this sandbox cannot reach, so
range-reading the WAV headers failed. Dropping them means **every value in the
manifest is one this branch verified**, rather than carried over on trust.

### Necessary supporting change

`make_xml.py` gains a `main()` guard. It ran its driver at *import* time, so
`verify_sources.py` importing `load_metadata`/`item_recordings` would have
regenerated the XML as a side effect. Alternative was duplicating the loader
(against POL-046). Output unchanged — rebuild byte-identical, `git status`
empty.

### Verified

- `verify_sources.py` and `--live` both pass against the live dataset
- **10 tests**, each corrupting one thing and asserting the specific complaint
  so no check can decay into a no-op: dropped recording, duplicate name,
  unknown item, source-URL drift, malformed hash, truncated revision,
  **drift between the manifest and the downloader's own pin**, and local audio
  with the right name but wrong bytes
- rebuild still idempotent; 5 files, +646 / −54
- **full repo suite: 1097 passed / 51 skipped**, exit 0

### Companion GitBook branch `docs/tang-audio-manifest` (`d0eb9fa`, off `5d0e393`)

Needed, not optional: the just-merged page says the deviation includes *"no
committed hash"*, which this branch falsifies. The bullet now narrows the
deviation to the **metadata extract** and records that the audio is pinned by
SHA-256 and that the published files are the 44.1 kHz stereo originals with
nothing resampled. `manage_corpus_pages.py check --strict` passes.

Note the corpus tests are **not collected** by the root pytest run
(`testpaths = ["tests"]`), matching Glosbe, HPS, Song and Yedda which also ship
their own. The README gives the command. ⏳ Whether corpus-local tests should
reach CI is a separate, repo-wide question.

⏳ **Not wired into CI**, deliberately: the natural home is
`hf-audio-parity.yaml`, which is shared code and would breach POL-049 inside a
single-corpus PR. Wants its own PR — and generalizing the manifest idea beyond
Tang is the more interesting version of that.

    git -C /workspace/FormosanBank        push -u origin corpus/tang-rights-and-pipeline
    git -C /workspace/FormosanBankGitbook push -u origin docs/tang-rights-and-pipeline

Both branches are refs in the shared checkouts, so those commands work from

### The generator was broken on `main`, and how

Reported in the #168 review without saying how; the answer is a **porting
accident**. `make_xml.py` was written for the dev repo, where it sat beside
`Audio/`, `Metadata/` and `XML/`. Porting moved it into `CodeAndDocs/` without
adjusting `SCRIPT_DIR`-relative paths, so it reads `CodeAndDocs/Audio/Truku`
and writes `CodeAndDocs/XML/Truku` — neither exists. Run today it dies on
`XML_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)` with `FileNotFoundError` (no `parents=True`);
survive that and it globs an empty directory, prints *"No .wav files found"*
and writes nothing. **POL-038 was not satisfied on `main`** — nothing committed
reproduced `XML/`.

Fixed two ways: paths resolve against the corpus root, and the recordings are
enumerated from the committed RO-Crate `hasPart` (30 WAVs / 4 items) instead of
by globbing audio. **The audio stops being a build input** — POL-048 without
downloading anything — and a rebuild can no longer silently skip a recording
whose WAV is missing. A file in `XML/Truku/` the metadata does not list is now
an error.

### Verified, by running it

- `generate_xml.sh` rewrites all 30 files; **`git status` empty** afterwards,
  twice.
- The licence commit's diff is **exactly 30 lines, one attribute each** —
  checked by normalizing the diff and counting: `30 +copyright="CC BY-NC 4.0"`,
  `30 -copyright="CC BY-NC"`. Nothing else in the XML moves.
- `rights_delta.py` reports the one intended line,
  `TangRecordingsOfTaroko: 'CC BY-NC' -> 'CC BY-NC 4.0'` ⇒
  **`rights-comparison.yaml` goes red and needs the maintainer override.**
  Designed friction (POL-044), not a defect.
- `validate_xml by_path`: **30 files, 0 issues.**
- `tests/corpora/test_provenance.py` **7 passed / 46 skipped** — Tang is now
  *tested*, not skipped, and is off `provenance_pending.txt`.
- **Full suite: 1071 passed / 53 skipped** at the original base, and
  **1095 passed / 53 skipped** re-run after the rebase onto `b88146902`
  (13m16s). Both exit 0; the +24 are main's own new tests.
- GitBook `manage_corpus_pages.py check --strict`: **OK**.

### Context worth keeping

Tang is **1 of 22** corpora whose published `@copyright` is out of vocabulary
after #194 (`FormosanBankGitBook`, Glosbe, HPS, ILRDF, Latham, Li-Thao,
Montgomery, NTU×2, Nowbucyang, Paiwan_Stories, RauDong, SEALS33, Safolu, Song,
Tang, Fey, Wakelin, Whitehorn, Wikipedias, WilangYutas, ePark). Per the same
day's ruling on #175 the normalization is done **PR by PR, not as one sweep**,
which is exactly what this branch does for Tang — and Tang is the easy case:
it lands the generator in the same branch, so the change is one constant in
`make_xml.py` plus a regenerate, never a hand edit of published XML (POL-038).
Also note **#194 shipped the delta gate but not
`V160`/`V161` nor `tests/corpora/test_rights_documentation.py`** — so nothing
today catches an out-of-vocabulary value or a missing POL-044 block.

### 🔴 CORRECTION — *"So we are not using a ledger, correct?"* We are.

Maintainer asked. I had written, in the README, the commit messages, the
GitBook page and this log, that the build reads "the Paradisec RO-Crate
metadata committed alongside it." **That is wrong, and it flattered the
reproduction.** Checked the four files:

- They are **not** RO-Crate documents. A crate has `@context` and `@graph`;
  these have neither. Each is one flattened entity wrapped as
  `{"metadata": {…}}` — 15.5 KB for all four items.
- **Every internal reference dangles**: `license`, `publisher`, `collector`,
  `operator`, `sourceOrganization`, `root`, `conformsTo` all point at `@id`s
  whose nodes were not kept.

So `CodeAndDocs/Metadata/` **is** a committed derived extract — a ledger in
everything but name. This branch did not create it (it came with the 2026-03
port, `9f3689e73`); what the branch did was promote it to being the build's
sole input, which is exactly why the label had to be right.

**The sharpest consequence: the corpus's licence is not derivable from its own
committed source.** `license` is `{"@id": "#license-3-a6e13b67"}`, which
resolves to nothing. That is why `COPYRIGHT` is a constant in `make_xml.py` and
why the POL-044 `Rights source` line is doing real work rather than restating
something a reader could check. Also: **no `refresh_source.sh`, no hash, no
pinned fetch** — nothing in the repository re-fetches the extract or verifies
it against the catalogue.

Fixed by rewording — README (a new *"What that metadata is, and is not"*
paragraph), the `make_xml.py` docstring and `COPYRIGHT` comment, the GitBook
Access Details bullet, and this entry. All three commits were rebuilt so the
messages match; re-verified afterwards (idempotent, `validate_xml` 30/0,
provenance 7 passed, all 30 TEXTs at `CC BY-NC 4.0`).

### RULED (2026-09-07): no `refresh_source.sh`; document it as a deviation instead

Maintainer: *"refresh_source.sh is not critical, because the original source is
never going to update. However, this should be logged in the README/GitBook as
something that is non-conforming and the reason given."* Done — a **Known
deviation** section in the README and a matching bullet on the GitBook page:
no refresh script, no committed hash, nothing checking the extract against the
catalogue; accepted because AIT1 is a closed deposit (recorded 1997, published
2016), so re-downloading an immutable record adds machinery without assurance.
POL-047 makes the script optional *"only where the source can be re-fetched"*
to useful effect. Both now state the guarantee explicitly: **the published XML
follows from the committed extract, not the extract from Paradisec.**

### ✅ CONFIRMED: the extract is upstream material, not our XML fed back in

Maintainer's real worry, and the right one to have about any committed ledger.
It does **not** sneak the published output back in as source. Four independent
checks, all one-directional:

1. **It contains strictly more than we publish.** `hasPart` enumerates **61
   parts — 30 MP3, 30 WAV, 1 PDF**; the corpus publishes only the 30 WAVs. An
   XML-derived file would list 30 and nothing else.
2. **A dozen fields the XML has no slot for**: `dateCreated 2008-09-20`,
   `datePublished 2016-03-19`, `originatedOn 1997-10-01`, `originalMedia
   "audio casssette"` — **the archive's own typo**, `contentLocation
   "Siyu-Lin, Hualien"`, `languageGenre "narrative"`, `languageAsGiven`,
   `recorder`, `publisher` as an NLA party URI. None of it is reachable from
   our TEXT attributes.
3. **RO-Crate graph internals** — `#license-3-a6e13b67`, `#identifier_domain`,
   `#place-Siyu-Lin, Hualien` — fragment ids that only mean anything inside a
   crate we do not hold. Nothing would invent them.
4. **Provenance and immutability.** Deposited in the corpus's **first commit**
   (`9f3689e73`, 2026-03-23) together with the XML, **byte-identical ever
   since** (SHA-256 compared against `origin/main`), and **no script in the
   repository writes them** — the only reference anywhere is `make_xml.py`'s
   read.

Information flows one way: everything in the XML derives from the extract plus
the single licence constant (proved — 30/30 byte-identical), and nothing in the
extract derives from the XML.

Incidental: `languageAsGiven "Truku"` and `inLanguage …/trv` mean two of
`make_xml.py`'s three constants are corroborated by the extract; only
`COPYRIGHT` is not. Reading them from it instead would cut the constants to one
with no output change. ⏳ Offered, not done — the user did not ask, and it buys
tightness rather than correctness.

### The MP3s: almost certainly access copies; we take the masters

Maintainer asked whether the 30 MP3s are just MP3 versions of the WAVs.
**Cannot be proved from what we hold** — the extract's `hasPart` entries are
bare `@id` strings with no `encodingFormat`, size or duration — and
`catalog.paradisec.org.au` is **unreachable from this sandbox** (connection
refused; only `github.com` and `huggingface.co` resolve), so no external check
was possible.

The circumstantial case is strong and one-directional:

- **Exact 1:1 stem pairing across all 30** — every stem has one `.mp3` and one
  `.wav`, no orphan MP3, no MP3-only recording. That is Paradisec's standard
  deposit shape (archival master + delivery derivative).
- `originalMedia` is `"audio casssette"` and the stems run `1A`/`1B`, `2A`/`2B`
  — cassette sides.
- `AIT1-001-1.wav` is **658,178,448 bytes ≈ 62 min** at 44.1 kHz/16-bit/stereo:
  one full cassette side.

**What we actually took, verified against the pinned HF revision**
(`6efaa2356…`, tree API): **30 WAVs, 13.59 GB, and nothing else audio** — plus
the same four JSON extracts (byte sizes 2682/2506/2554/7791, **identical to the
repo's copies**, so the extract travels with the audio too), a README,
`.gitattributes` and a stray `.DS_Store`. No MP3s, no PDF. **FormosanBank holds
the masters, not the derivatives** — the right way round. Incidentally this
independently confirms #168's 13.59 GB figure, which I had declined to assert.

⏳ **Loose end nobody has looked at:** `AIT1-001-2df.pdf`, the item's only
non-audio part, is held in no form here. It may be what the corpus description
means by *"slightly more meta-data at Paradisec, but not much."* Needs someone
with catalogue access.

Recorded in the README as a *"What the item holds that we do not"* section, so
the next reader of the 61-vs-30 figure does not have to ask.

### 🟢 CLOSED: the two email addresses in the extract are meant to be public

Maintainer (2026-09-07): *"I believe those email addresses are meant to be
public."* They are the archive's `collector`/`operator` contacts, carried

## 2026-09-07 — #175 clarifications: rights PR-by-PR (my sweep suggestion withdrawn); where "NW" actually lives

### Rights: PR-by-PR, deliberately

Maintainer: *"I'm doing the rights-comparison PR by PR. There are reasons. So
let's update to CC BY-NC 4.0 for all of Whitehorn."* 🟢 **My "do it as one
bank-wide shared PR" suggestion is withdrawn** — the 67-of-14,565 conformance
count stands as a fact but is not an argument for batching it.
Whitehorn → `CC BY-NC 4.0` on all 87 TEXTs, which is what #175 already does.

⚠️ **Note for a standalone version of this change.** `main`'s Whitehorn has no
build code, so editing the 87 files outside #175 means editing published XML by
hand — **POL-038**. Inside #175 it is a **one-line edit** to
`source_records.json`'s `metadata.copyright` plus a regenerate. That asymmetry
is itself an argument for landing the generator.

### "Where is NW showing up?" — nowhere in `@dialect`. Three places, all prose.

Checked every attribute of all 87 files. **`@dialect` in the PR head is already
`unknown` ×85 + `Southern` ×2, zero `Northern`** — the ruling is satisfied as
written; nothing to change.

`NW` / north-west survives only as descriptive text:

1. **`source_records.json`** (the PR's new ledger) — `"source_dialect_label":
   "North Western"` ×46. A record of what the accession form said; the
   generator never reads it into `@dialect`.
2. **One `@source` string, unchanged from `main`** — `Whitehorn_2010.10_02a_2`:
   *"Starting with a few oddments both in German and northwest Paiwan, a woman
   tells a story."* Archive-supplied description, not a dialect claim.
3. The PR README, once, explaining the decision.

The four spellings I reported (`(NW)`, `(? NW)`, `(north-west)`,
`(north-west dialect)`) are on the **scanned forms only** — they appear in no
text file in the repo.

### CORRECTION to my own phrasing

I wrote that the four unroll items were *"every one of them asserting provenance
the artifacts don't carry."* That over-generalized. Accurately, they are three
different faults:

- **Invented provenance** (2): the README's *"The World Oral Literature Project
  granted FormosanBank permission to use the Whitehorn collections under
  CC BY-NC 4.0"* — `audio_permissions.json` records the basis as the Basecamp
  corpus card, and the pre-port README said only that the recordings were
  *contributed by* Whitehorn *to* WOLP; and the citation/BibTeX retitling to
  *The Whitehorn Collections*, which appears nowhere but this PR while all 87
  archive-supplied `@source` strings say *"Whitehorn Paiwan collection"*.
  (A third, minor: the README's *"Following the corpus maintainer decision"* was
  written 2026-08-23 with no such decision on record. It became true 2026-09-07.)
- **Unsupported conclusion** (1): gb#71 deletes the standing Corpus Note
  (*"Whitehorn sometimes specifies dialects, but not using the modern dialect
  distinctions. This will need to be standardized if possible"*) and replaces it
  with *"the recordings do not support a blanket Northern assignment"* without
  showing what established that. Now settled by ruling — so **replace the note
  with the ruling**, don't delete it.
- **Provenance loss, not invention** (2): the ledger collapses the four form
  spellings to `"North Western"`, and records `Whitehorn_2010.5_01b` — whose
  form reads `Chinese & Paiwan (NW)`, *"Words and Hymn in Chinese and Paiwan"* —
  as plain `"North Western"`, dropping that the source unit is mixed-language.

⏳ The last two are **optional and low-stakes**: they touch `source_dialect_label`,
which nothing reads. If the archival label is not wanted at all now that
"northwest" is ruled non-canonical, deleting the field is equally coherent —
maintainer's preference.

### "What is the ledger?"

`Corpora/Whitehorn_Collection/CodeAndDocs/source_records.json` — new in #175,
1,782 lines, the single data file the whole corpus is generated from:

- `metadata` — `corpus`, **`copyright`**, `citation`, `bibtex_citation`
  (one set, applied to all 87 TEXTs).
- `source_files` — 71 entries, one per accession-form PDF: `path`, `sha256`,
  `pages`, `status` (`included`/`excluded`), `record_ids`, `disposition`.
- `records` — 87 entries: `output`, `id`, `language`, `dialect`,
  `source_dialect_label`, `source`, `recording_date`, `audio_url`, `audio_file`,
  `source_file`.

`generate_xml.py` hashes every PDF against it, cross-checks source↔record
coverage both ways, then emits `XML/` from it. So it is both the corpus's data
of record and the only POL-038-legal place to change a published value.

## 2026-09-07 — CI fix (snapshot out of `XML/`) + a measured Wakelin orthography proposal

### 🐛 Why `xml-validation` failed on the Wakelin PR — a latent workflow bug

**Not a data problem.** One finding: new HARD `V121` at
`pre_correction_snapshot/XML/Yami/Kalaku1.xml` `W=S13W1`.

`xml-validation` selects files with `Corpora/**/XML/**/*.xml`, and **git's
default glob lets `*` cross `/`**, so it also matched the POL-035 snapshot — 10
files picked up where 5 were intended. The step's own comment says it "excludes
files outside the canonical XML/ subdir", so this was a bug, not a policy.

It surfaced because the snapshot is *supposed* to hold what the published XML
must not: repairing `Kalaku1/S13W1` to `katu-nem/namen-rana` put a slash in a
snapshot W FORM, which is what the alternation ruling requires, and V121 flags
slashes in W/M FORMs.

**Fix (maintainer's, and the better one): move the snapshot out of an `XML/`
path** — `pre_correction_snapshot/XML/Yami/` → `pre_correction_snapshot/Yami/`.
No shared-code change, no override, and it aligns WakelinTexts with the majority
convention (Safolu, Virginia_Fey, Glosbe, Wikipedias all have no `XML/` level).
Committed to the branch (11 commits now). Verified: the workflow's own pathspec
now returns the 5 canonical files and the HARD comparison passes on all of them.

⏳ **SEALS33 has the same `pre_correction_snapshot/XML/` layout and the same
latent exposure** — untouched, worth a follow-up. The alternative fix, if anyone
prefers it, is a pathspec exclusion in the workflow, verified here to drop
exactly the 8 snapshot files and no canonical file:
`':(exclude)Corpora/*/CodeAndDocs/**'`.

### Wakelin orthography: a proposal with numbers

`claudeplans/2026-09-07-wakelin-orthography-proposal/` — `README.md`,
`Yami.tsv`, `Yami_Wakelin_113.tsv`, `measure.py`. **Nothing applied to the
corpus.** Reference: all `tao` corpora except Wakelin = 12,831 types / 135,435
tokens.

**Result: 49.1% of morph types and 78.6% of morph tokens** become attested
modern forms, from a 45.9% token baseline. Measured per rule; the unit is the
**morph**, because Wakelin hyphenates clitics modern Yami writes separately
(whole-word scoring gives 48.6% for orthographically irrelevant reasons).

- **`u` → `o` is the load-bearing rule** (+28 points). Three independent
  supports: Wakelin uses `o` in only 4 word types; the article's own errata
  correct `o`→`u` twice (F16, F17); and the gloss matches are the commonest
  words in the language (`su`/`so` 斜格, `ku`/`ko` 1.S.GEN, `tau`/`tao` 人).
- `ch`→`c`, `ǥ`→`h`, `?`→∅ all confirmed by glosses.
- ⚠️ **Two rules that work cannot be written in a flat conversion table**:
  `Cw`→`Co` (`kwan`→`koan` 說, 746×) and `Cy`→`Ci` are **positional**. A blanket
  `y`→`i` *loses* 7 points.
- 🔴 **`ř` cannot be resolved, and the reason is the reference data.** Plain `r`
  → `r` is clean (gloss-confirmed on `rana` 已經, `sira`, `araw` 天, `ciring` 話,
  `ngaran` 名字). But `ř`'s three gloss-confirmed hits disagree — `ařima`→`alima`
  五 vs `vařit`→`vazit` 藤 — and **modern Yami in FormosanBank does not itself
  distinguish `l`~`z`~`r`~`y` consistently**: 20–34 co-attested minimal pairs per
  combination, thousands of tokens (`sira`~`siya`, `rana`~`yana`, `ala`~`aza`~`aya`).
  No single-letter mapping can be validated against a target that varies that much.

**Recommendation: do not turn the tables on.** `ř` would be silently guessed;
the two load-bearing glide rules are inexpressible in the table format; and
78.6% is not yet POL-002's claim that the text *has been* transliterated.
⏳ To close it: settle `ř` from Rau & Dong's phonology, solve the `e`
correspondence (`pengsu`~`pongso`), decide whether `?` survives as `'`, and
re-measure against Rau & Dong alone so the target is one orthography.

## 2026-09-07 — #175: is anything in it worth having? Yes — the ledger. The rest is thin.

Maintainer asked whether #175 mostly introduces errors we then unroll. Checked;
**it does not** — it is the odd one out in this batch. Ledger below.

### Unlike #174 and #181, no published-XML data error survives the rulings

#181 applied the 1958 errata backwards across 67 forms; #174 downgraded rights
and flattened a real standard tier. #175 changes exactly three attributes and
**two of the three are things we affirmatively want**:

| change | files | verdict |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `@dialect` `Northern` → `unknown` | 46 | ✅ **ruled correct 2026-09-07** |
| `@copyright` → `CC BY-NC 4.0` | 87 | ✅ correct (POL-042 spelling) |
| `@citation` + `@BibTeX_citation` retitled | 87 | ❌ unevidenced — see below |

`@id`, `@xml:lang`, `@source`, `@audio`, `AUDIO/@file` and child counts are
**byte-identical** across all 87. There is no language data in this corpus to
damage.

### The one thing that is genuinely hard to get any other way

`generate_xml.py` + `source_records.json`. Whitehorn is one of only **three
corpora in the bank with no build code at all** (the others being
MontgomeryTexts — which #174 is the fix for — and Paiwan_Stories), and its
`main` README says so in as many words: *"The XMLs were compiled by hand, so
aren't entirely reproducible."*

Consequence worth stating plainly: **under POL-038 there is currently no
legitimate path to change this corpus at all**, including the copyright
normalization we want. #175 is what creates one. Verified by running it —
71 SHA-256-pinned sources, `--check` clean, full regenerate byte-identical,
stdlib only, no network, no private repo (POL-048 satisfied outright). It also
gives the excluded `Whitehorn_Paiwan_03A_01` a written disposition; today that
record is just an empty XML silently deleted in `2288d4f`.

### But the two attribute sweeps are worth less than they look

- **The dialect fix is 46 attributes.** Wanted, but trivially separable.
- **The copyright fix is a slice of a bank-wide backlog.** Measured across all
  14,565 published TEXTs: **67 conform to `rights_vocabulary.csv` today** — 66
  `public domain` plus a single `CC BY-NC 4.0`. The rest: `CC BY-SA` 13,239,
  `CC-BY-NC-SA` 436, `CC BY-NC` 323, `CC-BY` 260, `CC-BY-NC` 196 (87 of them
  Whitehorn's), `CC NC-BY` 20, `CC-BY-NC-ND` 9. So POL-042 conformance is a
  **~14,500-TEXT sweep** that has to happen bank-wide regardless, and taking it
  one corpus at a time costs one deliberate `rights-comparison` override each.
  ⏳ Worth doing as a single shared-code PR rather than 30 corpus PRs.

### What we unroll is small, and all of one kind

One invented README sentence (the WOLP "grant"), one invented citation title,
one deleted GitBook note, two ledger-fidelity nits. Every one is the same
failure mode: **asserting provenance the artifacts do not carry.**

On the citation specifically there is now *positive counter-evidence*, not just
absence: all 87 `@source` strings — archive-supplied, and untouched by the PR —
read *"Whitehorn Paiwan collection, record …"*, including the Amis, Atayal and
Seediq records. So the archive's own name for it is the old title, and
*"The Whitehorn Collections"* appears nowhere but this PR. **Revert the citation
and BibTeX to `main`'s wording** unless the Cambridge landing pages say otherwise.

### Recommendation

Take it, with (a) citation + BibTeX reverted, (b) the rights prose replaced by
the POL-044 block, (c) gb#71's Corpus Note replaced rather than deleted, and
(d) the ledger keeping the four NW spellings verbatim. If the batch is being
thinned instead, **the generator and ledger are the part to keep** — the two
attribute sweeps can be redone in minutes by anyone, and the copyright half
arguably belongs in the bank-wide sweep anyway.

## 2026-09-07 (close-out) — Wakelin: no open data questions left

`corpus/wakelin-policy-conformance` **9 commits**; GitBook
`docs/wakelin-policy-conformance` **5 commits**. Both unpushed.
**1,071 passed / 53 skipped**, idempotent, **14 HARD** (28 on `main`).

- **`Kalaku1/S6` → two sentences**, `ngaran-amn` and `namen-em`, both glossed
  `name-we`. The second replaces the whole word, so it inherits **no**
  morphemes. 11 variant / 8 split. **`Kwaway/S2` confirmed a spelling variant.**
  **No `review: true` calls remain.**
- **The 14 HARD V121 are ACCEPTED, not deferred.** `V121` assumes a parenthesis
  marks optional material (POL-026 → two sentences). The article's own key says
  `( )` is *"in data, probable discrepancy"* — **an uncertainty marker on the
  transcription**, so expanding it would manufacture readings the transcriber
  never proposed. Now stated outright in README + GitBook. CI compares HARD
  counts against the base and this branch takes them 28 → 14, so nothing needs
  suppressing. `Kangkang/S18`'s `kan(u)` remains the one paren that really is an
  alternation.
- **`rights_delta` override approved** for `CC-BY-NC-ND` → `CC BY-NC-ND 4.0`.
- `Sunagu` `source` attribute is `"Yami text. Sunagu"` (was "…Kalaku").

### 🐛 The lesson worth keeping: an invariant caught five live bugs

Added a build invariant — **every morpheme must occur in the word that holds
it** — because the S6 split is exactly the shape that breaks it. It immediately
found **five real bugs already committed from the ř batch**: my sentence-scoped
string replacement updated each *word* but not the *morpheme* inside it, because
the morpheme text is a substring (`arwa` is not `y-arwa`). Affected
`Kalaku2/S4W6M2`, `Kwaway/S23W2M1`, `Kwaway/S48W1M2` + `S48bW1M2`,
`Sunagu/S23W1M1`. **A whole-word find-and-replace over a segmented corpus
silently misses the M tier**; the build now fails instead of publishing it.
This pairs with the earlier derive-and-assert fix for branch sentence FORMs —
both are the same failure mode, a hand-edit that updates one tier of three.

### ⏳ All that is left

Push both branches, open the PRs, take the rights override, and close **#181**
and **GitBook #77**. No data or policy questions remain open on this corpus.

## 2026-09-07 — PR #174 rulings: close it and start clean

**Maintainer rulings (2026-09-07), all on the #174 review below:**

1. ⛔ **Heading deletion OVERRULED.** The three printed titles "are translated
   text and certainly linguistic data." They stay as `S1`. Corroborated by the
   scan: p.18 prints `O-LEMAK AKO ANINI` over a word-aligned gloss line
   `Day  I  Now` — the same two-line format as every numbered example.
2. ✅ **`mi-salama` → `mi-salrama` confirmed; make the correction directly.**
3. ⛔ **`f̆` → `f̂` DECLINED.** *"The original text really does look like an f
   with a breve. I agree that status is uncertain. But I don't think we change
   it without additional evidence."* Main's U+0306 stands. My caron reading is
   recorded below as an observation, not a change.
4. ⛔ **No `reproduce.sh` for this corpus** — "there is nothing for it to do."
   Montgomery is hand-maintained; the README states the POL-047/048 deviation
   explicitly rather than shipping a build script that only re-emits a ledger.
5. ⏳ **Slash alternatives in W glosses — question raised, answer below.**

### Answer to 5: slashed W-level glosses

Montgomery has **5**, all lexical W TRANSL, all printed that way in the source:
`good/holy` (S4W8), `noon/lunch` (S16W7), `trip/walk` (S18W9), `whole/all`
(S3W3), `and/with` (S5W8). Verified against pp.18–19 of the scan.

**How they are handled today: they are not.** They sit inline and surface as
**V122 SOFT** (`text.py`: parens or `/` anywhere in FORM or TRANSL). **V121
HARD covers only W/M FORM**, not TRANSL, so nothing blocks them.

**No policy covers this case.** POL-025 governs alternative *sentence*
translations (multiple TRANSL, all but one `ver="alt"`). POL-027 governs
alternatives in the *example text* (one S per option) — its target is a
Formosan sentence that genuinely varies, which is why it splits S blocks.
Neither fits a single fixed Amis word with two English equivalents.

Repo-wide this is small and confined:

| YeddaPalemeqBlog | 46 |
| Li-Conjunction-Thao | 6 |
| WakelinTexts | 6 |
| **MontgomeryTexts** | **5** |
| Nowbucyang-Truku-Thesis | 1 |
| ePark | 1 |
| **total** | **147 across 7 corpora** |

Proposed: POL-025's mechanism one tier down — two `TRANSL` on the W, the
second `ver="alt"` — because the Amis word does not vary and splitting S
blocks (POL-027) would be wrong. Awaiting the ruling.

## 2026-09-07 (later) — three maintainer challenges; TWO OF MINE WERE WRONG

### 1. ⛔ "Why are we dropping PHON? Don't we have the tables?" — RIGHT. PHON REINSTATED.

We do have both, and the tier regenerates clean. My no-PHON rationale
over-claimed and is withdrawn. Regenerating today gives **788 elements, 0 `*`**,
POL-013 `[o|u]` notation, hyphens stripped. Same SOFT total as the no-PHON
build (187): deleting it bought nothing.

**And it surfaced a real bug.** `Orthographies/Montgomery/Amis.tsv` gave the
letter `l` the IPA value **`d`** — the *letter* it maps to in Ortho113, sitting
in the column that wants that letter's *sound*. Ortho113's `d` is /ɬ~ɮ/, so the
same word came out **/dafak/ from the original tier and /ɬafak/ from the
standard**, differing in **50 of 394** elements. That is the incoherence the
2026-08-13 sweep referred and never resolved.

Akiw's own example settles it: `tamlaw` → `tamdaw` "people", pronounced
/tamɬaw/, so Montgomery's `l` writes the lateral fricative. Row now `[ɬ|ɮ]`.
Result: **0 of 394 pairs differ**, and `validate_conversion_table` resolves all
five rows. The profile's own `d` row is inert — the original tier has no `d`.

788 PHON, 568 change, **none deleted**: 482 tilde→`[x|y]` (the whole of issue
**#103**'s PHON complaint, so that half is now genuinely closed, not sidestepped),
145 lose hyphens, 50 take the profile fix.

### 2. Hyphens — no misunderstanding; my wording was bad

The stated policy is exactly what the branch produces. Measured on the build:

| tier | with hyphen |
| --- | --- |
| S original | 31 of 40 |
| S standard | **0** |
| W original | 57 of 354 |
| W standard | 57 of 354 |
| PHON | **0** |

The "hyphen problem" was never about policy: `standardize.py` **could not
produce that state** for this corpus, because C012 is gated on
`element.find(".//M")` and there is no M tier. Regenerating without the fix
would have left 28 hyphens in S standard. `--segmented-without-m-tier` is what
makes the shared tool implement the policy here. It stays opt-in because an
S-level hyphen is not always segmentation (15,855 S across 12 corpora would be
caught by a blanket widening — Wikipedias proper nouns, Siraya's deliberate
hyphens).

### 3. ⛔ "Southern Amis" — WRONG, RETRACTED

`validate_conversion_table` compares, per row, the source grapheme's IPA in the
input profile against the target grapheme's IPA in Ortho113, per dialect
column. "Resolves" = they match. Only `l`→`d` varied, and only because
Ortho113's `d` is /d/ under Southern and /ɬ~ɮ/ elsewhere.

That was never evidence about the text, and I read the "Confirmed
equivalences" list while skating past the **Coverage** section in the same
report. **Ortho113 marks `f` and `o` `NA` for Southern** — Southern Amis writes
`u`, not `o`, and has no `f` — and Montgomery's text is full of both
(`farotso?`, `foti?`, `toki`, `roma?`). Southern is *ruled out*, not suggested.
With the profile fixed the row resolves under Xiuguluan, Coastal and Hengchun
anyway. `dialect` stays `unknown`, now for the right reason. Corrected in the
README and on the GitBook page.

## 2026-09-07 (later still) — V135 made orthography-aware; a generated rule catalogue

Two maintainer asks off the back of Montgomery's 2 V135 findings.

### V135 — `?` is a letter where the orthography says so

Hardcoded punctuation set `.,!?;:` + full-width. Three profiled transcriptions
write the glottal stop `?` — **Ferrell Paiwan, Montgomery Amis, Tsuchida
Pazeh** — so `roma?` "home" read as ending in a question mark.

Now subtracts the tier's own letters, **per tier**: the original tier may be in
any profiled source orthography for the language, the standard tier is Ortho113
by definition (POL-002). New `_orthography_letters()` beside the existing
`_orthography_allowed_chars()` that V116 already uses — same job, but V116 keeps
only non-ASCII and the characters at issue here are ASCII.

**Blast radius measured before changing anything: V135 fires exactly TWICE in
the whole repo**, and both are Montgomery's glottal. So the fix removes the
rule's only two live findings, both false, and touches nothing else. Three
tests: glottal silent, real mismatch in the same language still fires, a
language with no `?` profile still treats it as punctuation.

### A list of the rules — `QC/validation/RULES.md`, generated

There was none, so a finding like `V135 trailing_punct_mismatch` sent the
reader grepping. `QC/validation/rules_catalogue.py` builds it from the `RULES`
lists that actually run — id, mnemonic, severity, scope, one-line description,
grouped by validator. `--check` exits 1 when stale;
`tests/validators/test_rules_catalogue.py` runs it, so a new rule fails CI
until the catalogue is regenerated. Linked from `QC/README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
**83 rules.**

### 🔍 It found a bug on its first run: V070 is claimed by two rules

`hard.v070_phon_placement` (validate_xml) and `gloss.v070_gloss_code_as_FORM`
(validate_glosses). A shared id makes a finding ambiguous in the findings CSV.
The generator does **not** deduplicate — it lists both, prints a warning, and
the catalogue carries a callout. ⏳ Renumbering one is a maintainer call;
nothing renamed.

### GitBook page — `qc-pipeline/rule-catalogue.md` (`ccbb02f`)

Maintainer asked for a page describing and linking `RULES.md`. There was none
because there was no `RULES.md`. New page, in `SUMMARY.md` **above** the
individual validator pages since it indexes them.

The part worth writing down is the relationship: the per-validator pages carry
the reasoning and the CLI, and **their rule tables are hand-written and
illustrative** (`validate-text.md` lists ~10 of text.py's 35). The catalogue is
complete by construction, so where they disagree it wins. Also documents the
V070 collision and the generated-file contract.

Two cross-references: the QC Pipeline overview points at it from the
Finding/Severity section where a reader first meets a rule id, and
`repository-contracts/generated-files.md` notes it as the one generated file
outside `statistics/` — and the only one whose staleness is a red check rather
than a silent overwrite.

⚠️ Its `blob/main` link to `RULES.md` 404s until the FormosanBank PR merges —
the same convention every other page here uses, and another reason to merge
FormosanBank first.

## 2026-09-07 — 🔴 CI RED on the Montgomery PR: a latent workflow bug, now fixed

`xml-validation / Validate XML files changed by this PR` failed. **Not the
data — the workflow's file selection.**

    git diff ... -- 'Corpora/**/XML/**/*.xml'

In a **default git pathspec `*` matches `/` too**, so that never meant "under
`Corpora/<name>/XML/`". It matched any `.xml` beneath a directory named `XML`
anywhere under `Corpora/` — including
`Corpora/<name>/CodeAndDocs/pre_correction_snapshot/XML/`. CI validated the
POL-035 snapshots **as published data**:

    HARD — 1 total:
      1 x rule_id='V081', location="TEXT[@id='Montgomery_Amis_Day_I_Now']"

`V081 text_id_unique_across_published_corpora` — the snapshot's TEXT id
duplicates the published file it is the baseline *for*. An added file has an
empty baseline, so every HARD finding is new and blocks.

**Latent, not new: `SEALS33` and `WakelinTexts` already ship a snapshot at that
path on `main`.** Nothing failed only because no PR had *added* one. Montgomery
is the first, and any future snapshot corpus would have hit it.

**Fix (`2c838c131`):** `:(glob)` magic — under it `*` stops at `/` and `**`
does not — in **both** `xml-validation.yaml` and `audio-validation.yaml`
(identical line, identical bug). Both workflows' own comments already claimed
this behaviour ("Excludes files outside the canonical `XML/` subdir"); the
implementation never matched.

This only teaches the workflows what the counting code already knows:
`corpus_counts.corpus_xml_dirs` globs `XML` at any depth *and* excludes any
path containing `CodeAndDocs`. Same rule, same reason — which is why the
statistics never double-counted the snapshot.

**Verified by reproducing the CI step locally**, per-file with
`compare_findings` against the base, all three validators: **9/9 "No new HARD
findings", would exit 0.** `tests/validators/test_ci_changed_xml_pathspec.py`
pins the pattern in both workflows *and* the behaviour, the last test against a
scratch git repo so a rewrite that keeps the string but changes the meaning
still fails.

### 🔴 The bigger one the maintainer caught: corpus METRICS counted snapshots

I first wrote this off as "the informational baseline job". **Wrong — and the
maintainer's instinct was right.** `corpus_metrics.py`, which writes
`corpus_size_history.csv` and the growth graph, had **two of its own file
selectors** and both counted snapshots:

    find_xml_files()        any *.xml with an "XML" path segment
    XML_HISTORY_PATHSPEC    ":(glob)Corpora/**/XML/**/*.xml" — `**` crosses
                            directories even under :(glob)

**11 files, 2,374 tokens** — WakelinTexts 6, MontgomeryTexts 3, SEALS33 2.
Wakelin's and SEALS33's landed on `main` in **August 2026**, so this predates
the Montgomery snapshot entirely.

**What was NOT affected** (checked, not assumed): the per-corpus CSVs are
clean — `get_corpus_stats.py` routes through `corpus_counts`, whose
`collect_records` has skipped `CodeAndDocs` since 2026-08-11 with the reason in
its docstring ("counting a snapshot would double a corpus's apparent size").
The **HEAD row** of the history CSV is clean too, because CI passes
`--stats-dir` and builds the row from those CSVs — its latest row matches the
CSV totals **exactly**: 8,268,883 tokens / 14,565 files / 492,772 sentences,
zero difference.

**What WAS exposed:** the git-blob side of `--history-extend` — the seed state
and the per-commit change stream, which feed the **intermediate rows of a
multi-commit push** — plus `--history-rebuild` and plain XML mode. A commit
touching only a snapshot also read as an XML-changing commit and earned a row.
There are matching ±2 file-count wobbles in the history around 2026-08-11/12,
exactly when SEALS33's and Wakelin's snapshots landed.

**Fix (`b03266109`):** one rule, two forms —
`corpus_counts.is_published_xml(path)` for path walking (now used by
`corpus_xml_dirs` *and* `corpus_metrics.find_xml_files`, so they cannot
diverge), and `XML_HISTORY_PATHSPECS` for git, adding
`':(exclude,glob)Corpora/**/CodeAndDocs/**'`. Both keep the nesting allowance.
Verified: the filesystem walk and the git pathspec now select the same
**14,565** files, equal to what `corpus_counts` sees.
`tests/utilities/test_published_xml_predicate.py` covers the predicate, both
walks, and that they agree on this repository.

⏳ **Still not fixed, genuinely informational:** the `validate-baseline` job
runs `validate_xml.py by_path --path Corpora`, so its *findings* count (not
word count) includes snapshots. Non-blocking; excluding `CodeAndDocs` there
would change `by_path` semantics for everyone, which deserves its own call.

## 2026-09-07 — Wakelin: three more rulings implemented; one proposal declined on evidence

`corpus/wakelin-policy-conformance` now **4 commits** (`/workspace/wt-wakelin`);
GitBook `docs/wakelin-policy-conformance` **2 commits**. Both unpushed.
Full suite **1,071 passed / 53 skipped**; build idempotent; no new HARD findings.

### Implemented

1. **Alternates stop at the W — never on the S.** Previously the alternate
   reading propagated to the sentence FORM. Two reasons to stop: a
   whole-sentence alternate for a one-morpheme spelling difference is noise,
   and where one sentence has two independent alternations (`Kalaku1/S17`, the
   `nem ~ namen` pronoun twice) each S-level alternate could show only one of
   them, reading as a claim that the other did not vary. `Kalaku1/S13` now
   comes out exactly as described: S `katu-nem-rana …`, W `katu-nem-rana` +
   `katu-namen-rana`, M `nem` + `namen`. S4, S7, S12, S17 same shape.
2. **`unan` is the "unanalyzed" marker, not a gloss** — a TRANSL whose whole
   text is `unan` is no longer published, at any level. Composite glosses
   containing it are untouched.
3. **A word whose morphemes do not line up with its gloss keeps no M** — the
   W-level gloss stands alone. Unit counting is paren-aware
   (`unan-(one-after-another)-us-completely` = 4, not 6), and a gloss carrying
   the source's own slash across the whole word (`Kwaway/S25W1`) counts as
   aligned if either side matches — that one rescue keeps four morphemes and
   their POL-025 alternative glosses.
   ⏳ **The review list the maintainer asked for**: `CodeAndDocs/
   gloss_alignment_review.tsv`, **52 W**, regenerated by the build. Two
   dominant patterns: the `-em`/`-m` narration suffix the article says outright
   is left untranslated (~40), and single morphemes glossed with a hyphenated
   English phrase (`kakwa` 'long-time-ago', 13).

Splitting also now carries each branch's own gloss where the source recorded a
second reading as `TRANSL[@ver="alt"]`; an alt gloss elsewhere in the sentence
is a genuine POL-025 second reading and is left alone.

Totals: 178 S, 882 W, **1134 → 1007 M**, **2203 → 1764 TRANSL**, 18 alternate
FORM. `V064`/`V065` now fire as SOFT wherever the article gave no gloss — the
intended consequence, documented in README and GitBook.

### ⛔ DECLINED with evidence — the `Kalaku1/S11` gloss swap

Proposed: reverse the last two glosses and split the word as `a-ni-padi` /
`machyura-rana`. **Not applied.** Recorded in `source_discrepancies.md` §C2.

- **Word-box coordinates from p.14**: `unan-many-still/again-them` sits at
  x=265.7, directly under `dy-aru-pa-sira` at x=265.5;
  `unan-past(unctn)-…accompany-completely` starts at x=428.9 under
  `a-ni-padi/machyura-rana` at x=356.0.
- **The corpus's own morpheme glosses**: `rana`→'completely' **39×**,
  `ni`→'past(unctn)' **22×**, `sira`→'they/them' **6×**, `aru`→'many',
  `pa`→'still/again'. The swap would make `rana` mean 'them'.
- **Free translation**: "Many, many other foreigners accompanied us."
- The proposed split also fails the **maintainer's own count test**: 3 and 2
  morphemes against a 4-unit gloss, versus 4 and 4 for the current reading.

The sentence's one real defect *is* fixed by rule 3: `dewdew-em` glossed
`foreigners` had a morpheme `em` also glossed 'foreigners'; the M tier goes.

### ⏳ Still open

The six source discrepancies from the 2026-09-06 report, the 16 HARD V121
optional-material parens (a POL-026 question), the `Kalaku1/S13W1`
`snapshot_repairs` entry, the two `review: true` alternation calls, the
`rights_delta` override at merge, and closing #181 / GitBook #77.

## 2026-09-06 — WakelinTexts reworked on `corpus/wakelin-policy-conformance`. #181 not used.

Branch `corpus/wakelin-policy-conformance` off `origin/main` `5749419a5`, worktree
`/workspace/wt-wakelin`, **3 commits, unpushed**. GitBook companion
`docs/wakelin-policy-conformance` in `/workspace/wt-gitbook-wakelin`, **1 commit,
unpushed**. Nothing was taken from PR #181.

### How #181 regressed the errata — the mechanism, corrected

Earlier I wrote that #181 "applies the errata backwards". That described the
effect; the maintainer asked for the mechanism, and it is different. **The
snapshot is untouched** — all six files are byte-identical between `main` and
the PR. The errata corrections live *in* the snapshot, and `main`'s
`make_xml.sh` restores from it. #181 instead **stopped using the snapshot** and
built from `source_records.json`, a new hand-keyed ledger transcribed from the
raw printed pages, which never had the errata applied. Same 59-sentence
regression, by abandoned baseline rather than reverse edit — and nothing in the
PR compares the new ledger against the old one, which is why it went unseen.

### The four rulings, and what they cost #181

1. **The Kwaway S36/S40 duplicate is real** — it is printed twice.
2. **The slash alternatives are TRANSCRIBER UNCERTAINTY** and do not become
   separate S blocks by default. This **rejects #181's headline feature** (18
   new `v2`/`v3` sentences) and, more broadly, means **POL-027 does not apply to
   transcriber uncertainty**. ⏳ Worth a POLICIES note: the two are
   indistinguishable by punctuation, and issues **#80** and **#139** both read
   these slashes as POL-027 violations.
3. **`Original.pdf` was already committed** — the reproducibility credit I gave
   #181 was wrong. Worse: **nothing in #181 reads the PDF.** Its scripts never
   open it; `reproduce.sh` and `test_corpus.py` only hash it.
4. **No standard tier**, and none in the snapshot either.

**Verdict on #181: nothing salvageable.** All 72 of its changed S FORMs are 59
errata reversals + 13 slash removals; zero genuine corrections. Its "restores
printed Kwaway S40" is false — `main` already has S36 *and* S40; what it does is
attach S40's translation to S36 as an `alt`. M-tier coverage (issue #80) is
untouched: W-with-no-M goes 428 → 427 on shared sentences.

### What the new branch does

- **Snapshot is now the source of record** (supersedes f64dc5c0a's "never
  edited", POL-050): standard tier dropped from it (2,120 FORMs), errata A30
  `buken`→`puken` applied, `Kalaku3/S8W8` unfused — one W had held the 3-word
  string `mangday su aep`, the corpus's only multi-word W. `Kwaway/S48b` removed
  from the snapshot because it pre-materialized one branch of an alternation.
- **`alternative_decisions.json`** — all 18 alternations classified by hand,
  **11 variant / 7 split**, with the printed string and a reason for each
  (POL-039). ⏳ Two marked `review: true`: `Kalaku1/S6` (recorded alternate looks
  truncated) and `Kwaway/S2` (single-vowel `a/u`, kept as a variant though the
  readings share no letters).
- **`generate_xml.py` + `generate_xml.sh`** (POL-047 naming; `make_xml.sh` and
  `drop_derived_tiers.py` deleted). Alternate FORMs propagate up to the
  containing W and S, so **no published FORM keeps a slash**. Splits drop only
  *unmatched* parens, so the corpus's own `(unctn)` gloss marker survives.
- **Ids:** first branch keeps the printed number, rest take `b`, `c`. POL-037

## 2026-09-06 — RULINGS on #181 Wakelin: close it. Nothing in it is salvageable.

Four maintainer rulings, and re-measurement against them. **Verdict: #181 has no
mergeable content.** Every change it makes to shared sentences is a regression;
everything it adds is either rejected by a ruling or already on `main`.

### The rulings

1. **The Kwaway S36/S40 duplicate is real** — it is in the printed source and
   stays. (#181 does not delete it, but see the S36 defect below.)
2. **🔴 The slash alternatives are TRANSCRIBER UNCERTAINTY, not source-offered
   alternatives — they do NOT become separate S blocks.** This overturns my
   read of them as POL-027 material and **rejects #181's headline feature**, the
   18 new `v2`/`v3` sentences. `main`'s scheme is the correct one: the slash
   stays in the S-level FORM as printed, and the uncertain word carries
   `FORM[@kindOf="original"]` + `FORM[@kindOf="alternate"]` at W or M level.
   ⚠️ Consequence: **POL-027 does not apply to transcriber uncertainty.** Worth
   a POLICIES note — the two are indistinguishable by punctuation alone, and
   issues #80 and #139 both read these slashes as POL-027 violations.
3. **`Original.pdf` was already committed on `main`** — I gave #181 undue credit
   for reproducibility. Corrected below.
4. **No standard tier for this corpus**: it is not Ortho113 and we do not know
   how to convert it. Confirms merged `f64dc5c0a`; #181 reverts it.

### What #181 actually does to the six published files

All 72 changed S-level original FORMs classified, none left over:

| n | change | verdict |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 59 | **errata reversal** (p.22 `for X read Y` undone) | regression |
| 13 | slash / alternate removal feeding the new S blocks | rejected by ruling 2 |
| **0** | genuine textual correction | — |

And on the 172 shared sentences: **16 TRANSL sets change** — 3 gloss errata
reversals (A3, D7), 1 dropped free-translation addendum (F20), **3 lost
`ver="alt"` readings** (POL-025), 2 paren-parse artifacts (`from Imurud)`),
1 wrong addition (below); **3 W and 7 M removed; nothing added.**

### Claimed gains that do not survive checking

- **"Restores printed Kwaway sentence 40" — false.** `main` already has S36
  *and* S40, with their distinct translations. What #181 actually does is attach
  S40's translation to **S36 as a `ver="alt"`**, conflating the two records
  ruling 1 says are independent. A defect, not a restoration.
- **Reproducibility credit withdrawn.** `Original.pdf` is already on `main`
  (ruling 3), and **nothing in #181 reads it** — `build_corpus.py`,
  `expand_alternatives.py` and `validate_corpus.py` never open it;
  `reproduce.sh` and `test_corpus.py` only **hash** it. The corpus is built
  entirely from `source_records.json`, a hand-keyed 31,480-line ledger from the
  private repo. So the pin proves the PDF is unchanged while nothing checks the
  ledger *against* it — which is precisely how 59 reversed errata and the
  invented `named` got through undetected. It remains a tier-3
  "ledger, not source" corpus, exactly as the 2026-09-03 audit classified it.
- **M-tier coverage (issue #80's V144) is not addressed.** On shared sentences
  W-with-no-M goes **428 → 427**: one W gains analysis, one loses it. The
  headline +75 W / +86 M is entirely the duplicated new sentences.
- **Standard tier**: 2,299 FORMs, 100% byte-identical to their originals —
  rejected by ruling 4.
- **Rights**: `CC BY-NC-ND` → `All rights reserved; …` fails the merged
  `rights_delta.py` gate (verified, exit 1) and POL-043.

### ⏳ Recommendation: close #181; open a small issue instead

Nothing needs to be extracted from the branch. The genuinely open work on `main`
is short, independent of it, and expressible as a worklist:

1. **17 S-level FORMs carry raw slashes; none has an S-level alternate FORM.**
   Under ruling 2 that is fine where the uncertain word has a W/M `alternate`
   sibling — 13 do. **Four do not**: `Kangkang/S33` (`simuskem/tanu-di-muskem`),
   `Kalaku4/S2` (`(imurud nu tau)/(tau d-imurud)`), `Kwaway/S48`
   (`pi-tulang-an-a/(tulang u ragaw)`), `Kalaku3/S8`.
2. **`Kalaku3/S8W8` is the corpus's only fused W** — one W holding the 3-word
   string `mangday su aep`. #181 spotted this; the observation is worth keeping
   even though its fix (a new sentence) is rejected.
3. **`Kwaway/S48b` is a separate S for what ruling 2 calls uncertainty** — it
   should be an alternate on S48. It is published and ID-stable, so folding it
   is a POL-037 / POL-051 call, not a cleanup.
4. **Errata A30 was never applied**: `Kangkang/S30` still reads
   `buken a s-ina-ku-imu`; A34 was applied on the same page, so this is a
   straggler. (`main`'s only errata gap — it is right on the other 28 checked.)
5. GitBook **#77** carries the same rights downgrade and the same standard-tier
   claim; close it with the PR.

### Verified by running it

- **Reproduction is real and idempotent.** Extracted the PR's corpus into a

  28,419 s folded into `pwn/unknown` 34 / 16,043 s → 80 / 44,462 s. Paiwan total
  unchanged (82 files, 44,969 s). Necessary, since `audio_durations.csv` is keyed
  on `(corpus, language, dialect)` and would otherwise go stale.

### RIGHTS — the change is correct, and it is the *pre-existing* position

Maintainer, 2026-09-05: *"the rights are as they were previously described
before this port."* That is exactly what the PR encodes.

`CC-BY-NC` → **`CC BY-NC 4.0`**, the exact `rights_vocabulary.csv` string.
`main`'s unversioned spelling is **not** in the vocabulary; POL-042's
"unversioned → 4.0" makes this pure normalization. Two places already published
4.0: `audio_permissions.json` (`whitehorn-cambridge`) and the GitBook page's
`## Copyright`. `validate_hf_audio.license_family()` folds both spellings, which
is why HF parity passed on either side. Nothing is weakened, so **POL-043 is not
in play** — unlike #165/#167/#174/#179/#181.

Ran the merged gate: `QC/validation/rights_delta.py` **exits 1**
(`Whitehorn_Collection: 'CC-BY-NC' -> 'CC BY-NC 4.0'`). Expected — the designed
friction, needing the deliberate maintainer override, same as #174/#181.

⚠️ **But the README invents a grantor.** It states *"The World Oral Literature
Project granted FormosanBank permission to use the Whitehorn collections under
CC BY-NC 4.0."* Nothing in the repo says that: `audio_permissions.json` records
the basis as *"publication approval is recorded on the corresponding Basecamp
corpus card"*, and the pre-port README said only that the recordings were
*contributed by* Whitehorn *to* WOLP. gb#71 makes no such claim. Since the
rights are as previously described, the licence line stays and the **provenance
sentence should be replaced by the POL-044 block** naming the real grantor and
date, `evidence: ask maintainer`.

### ⏳ THE open call: 46 × Paiwan `Northern` → `unknown`

Read the accession forms directly (image-only scans, rendered at 150–220 dpi).
The ledger is **faithful** where I checked it: `Whitehorn_Paiwan_01A_04` prints
*"Paiwan (southern dialect)"* → `Southern`; `Whitehorn_Paiwan_02B_01` prints
plain *"Paiwan"* → `null` → `unknown`. So the 34 already-`unknown` records are
right and the 2 `Southern` are right.

The 46 are the judgement call. The forms **do** say north-west, in four
spellings: `Paiwan (NW)`, `Paiwan (? NW)`, `Paiwan (north-west)`,
`Paiwan (north-west dialect)`. So this is not "no information" — it is
information that does not match `dialects.csv`'s Paiwan set (Northern, Central,
Southern, Eastern). `main` mapped it NW→Northern; the PR retreats to `unknown`
and keeps `North Western` in the ledger only.

The PR's README says *"Following the corpus maintainer decision"* — **I can find
no such ruling** in `claudeplans/`, POLICIES.md or the log. It also asserts
*"review showed that the recordings cannot all be mapped to Northern"* without
showing the review. And gb#71 **deletes the standing Corpus Note** that flags
this exact problem — *"Whitehorn sometimes specifies dialects, but not using the
modern dialect distinctions. This will need to be standardized if possible"* —
while answering it with `unknown` rather than standardizing. Removing the note
without resolving it is the wrong direction.

**Maintainer's call:** NW ⊂ Northern (keep `main`'s mapping), or `unknown`
(take the PR)? If `unknown`, gb#71 should keep the note, reworded.

### Ledger fidelity: 3 nits, one interesting

- `source_dialect_label` is **normalized, not verbatim** — all four spellings
  above collapse to `"North Western"`, and `(? NW)` loses Whitehorn's own
  uncertainty marker.
- **`Whitehorn_2010.5_01b` reads `Chinese & Paiwan (NW)`**, described as *"Words
  and Hymn in Chinese and Paiwan"*, and the ledger records only `North Western`.
  The two published records off that form (`_2` the Paiwan hymn 17.19–17.50,

  and it is the one form whose access field reads **"BBC Radio 3 broadcast"**

## 2026-09-05 — PR #168 TangRecordingsOfTaroko reviewed; audio downsampling needs a ruling

Head `fc6137929` (unchanged since 2026-08-23), forked at `3a3c47c22`, now
**80 commits behind** `origin/main` (`5749419a5`). Paired GitBook PR **gb#64**
(`ea38481`). **No open issue mentions Tang** — the only GitHub hit for "Tang"
is this PR. Review only; nothing pushed, no fix branch cut.

16 files: **zero XML diff**, a rewritten `CodeAndDocs/`, and 3 shared-tree
files (`audio_sources.json`, two `statistics/` CSVs). Merges onto current
`origin/main` with **no conflicts** (`git merge-tree`, verified).

### Verified by running it, not by reading

- **Reproduction is real.** Extracted the PR's `CodeAndDocs/` into a scratch
  tree, ran `make_xml.py`: **all 30 files byte-identical** to published XML,
  from committed evidence alone — the manifest plus the four RO-Crate JSONs.
  **No audio and no network needed.** POL-048 satisfied outright.
- **It fixes a generator that could never have worked.** `main`'s `make_xml.py`
  reads `CodeAndDocs/Audio/Truku` and writes `CodeAndDocs/XML/Truku` — neither
  path exists (both live at the corpus root) — and required all 13.6 GB of
  audio present first. POL-038 was quietly violated on `main`.
- **The 4 deleted `Audio/*-ro-crate-metadata.json` are byte-identical
  duplicates** of `CodeAndDocs/Metadata/*` — all four SHA-256 compared. Real
  dedup, zero content loss, and disclosed in the PR body (POL-051 met).
- **No shared-code change smuggled in** (POL-049 clean). `post_download`
  already exists in `QC/utilities/download_audio.py` and is already used by
  NTU_Paiwan_ASR; the `audio_sources.json` edit is confined to the Tang entry
  and does not change the pinned HF revision (`6efaa2356…`, same as `main`).
- **Manifest arithmetic checks out.** 30 files / 4 PARADISEC items;
  `frames ÷ rate == duration` for all 60 values; totals **76,976.624 s =
  21.382396 h**, matching README, gb#64 and both statistics CSVs.
- Its 5 tests pass; `verify_sources.py` passes offline.
- **Deleting `upload_hf_datasets.sh`** in favour of shared
  `QC/utilities/upload_to_hf.py` is POL-046 conformant; Tang was the last
  corpus carrying a bespoke uploader. No dangling references left.

### ⏳ 1. NEEDS A RULING — the audio every user gets changes: 44.1 kHz stereo → 16 kHz mono

This is the substantive change and the PR does not frame it as one. A new
`post_download` hook runs `prepare_audio.py --rebuild` after every download, so
`download_audio_data.sh` now hands users **2.46 GB of 16 kHz mono instead of
13.59 GB of 44.1 kHz stereo** — an 82% reduction. For an **untranscribed**
corpus the audio *is* the corpus.

The PR calls this "the approved 16 kHz mono output". **I can find no approval.**
Nothing in `POLICIES.md`, `AUDIO-PERMISSIONS.md`, `QC/README.md` or any
validator establishes a published audio format; the only 16 kHz in the repo is
`validate_audio_quality.py:314`, which resamples **transiently in memory** for
the acoustic model and stores nothing. Tang would be the first corpus whose
downloader alters audio fidelity (NTU_Paiwan_ASR's `post_download` segments,
it does not resample).

If 16 kHz mono is wanted it belongs in POLICIES as a bank-wide format, not in
one corpus's download hook. If it is not wanted, drop `post_download` and keep
the manifest — the source/prepared hash pinning is valuable either way.

### ⏳ 2. Hazard created by (1): the shared uploader would destroy the pinned source

After `download_audio_data.sh`, `Audio/Truku/` holds **prepared** files, not
source. `QC/utilities/upload_to_hf.py` uploads new/changed files from `Audio/`.
Running it on Tang pushes 16 kHz mono over `FormosanBank/TangRecordingsOfTaroko`,
invalidating all 30 `source_sha256` and breaking `verify_sources.py --live`
permanently. Tang has no `.hf_dataset.yaml` (so the tool prompts), but this
needs at minimum a loud README warning.

Not a regression, but noted: `move_audio_files` skips only same-size files, so
prepared ≠ source size means every run re-installs the source and re-converts
all 30. Self-healing and idempotent; never cheap.

### ⏳ 3. RIGHTS — substance preserved; but `CC BY-NC` is out of vocabulary post-#194

**Maintainer (2026-09-05): "the rights are as they were previously described
before this port."** Checked against that:

- **XML untouched** — all 30 files still `copyright="CC BY-NC"`, ids and
  citations unchanged (POL-037 clean).
- README goes from *"collected by Prof. Apay Tang, a member of the Truku tribe
  and a prominent preservationist and revitalizationist… Prof. Tang graciously
  agreed"* → *"The published source license is CC BY-NC 4.0. Prof. Apay Tang
  gave FormosanBank permission."* Same rights; but **Prof. Tang's community
  standing is dropped from both the README and gb#64**. Recommend restoring
  the maintainer's own sentence.
- The "4.0" is read from `audio_manifest.json`'s `source.license` — which is
  **FormosanBank's own HF repo field**, not the grantor. Correct under POL-042
  ("where a value names no version it is 4.0"), circular as evidence.

**New since PR #194 merged (`5749419a5`):** `rights_vocabulary.csv` contains
only `CC BY-NC 4.0` — bare `CC BY-NC` is **not in the vocabulary**, so Tang's
published XML violates POL-042 on today's `main`. It is not alone: **22 of ~27
corpora are out of vocabulary** (measured with `_rights.corpus_license` against
the shared checkout). So this is a bank-wide normalization backlog, not a Tang
defect — but this PR regenerates the XML anyway, so `CC BY-NC` → `CC BY-NC 4.0`
costs one string in `make_xml.py`, and **PR #174 was ruled the same way the
same day**. Consistency argues for doing it here; it forfeits the PR's
"zero XML diff" property and turns `rights-comparison.yaml` red, which is the
designed friction, not a defect.

**What #194 did *not* ship:** `V160`/`V161` are absent from
`QC/validation/rules/hard.py` and `tests/corpora/test_rights_documentation.py`
does not exist. Only the delta gate is live, so nothing today catches an
out-of-vocabulary value or a missing POL-044 block.

### Smaller findings

- **POL-044 block missing.** No `## Rights` section with `**License:**` /
  `**Rights source:** Prof. Apay Tang, <date>; evidence: ask maintainer`. Post-dates
  the PR; cheap to add and currently unenforced.
- **POL-047 naming.** Entry point is `reproduce.sh`, should be
  `generate_xml.sh`. Absent steps 3–5 are legitimate (no text tiers) but the

- **POL-052.** This is the rebuild moment. Add `CodeAndDocs/provenance.json`,

  replace the README's inline SHA (`3a3c47c220…`, now 80 commits stale) with a

- **gb#64 Copyright** reads `CC BY-NC 4.0` while the XML reads `CC BY-NC`.
  POL-044 wants them equal; `manage_corpus_pages.py` does not lint the Copyright
  section, so nothing catches it. Resolved for free by normalizing the XML.
- **CI is stale.** 4 checks, all green, run 2026-08-23 against a base 80 commits
  old; `xml-validation`/`audio-validation` never ran (path filters, no XML
  change). Merges clean, so a rebase and re-run is cheap.
- Nit: rename `test_citation_matches_josh_decision` to describe the rule.

README + gb#70 must say the publisher's CC-BY-ND is **interpreted
liberally** — the old README's own words — with the POL-044 block:
`**License:** CC BY-NC-ND 4.0` / `**Rights source:** …; evidence: ask
maintainer`. gb#70's Copyright section currently drops the licence entirely.

### 2. PHON — RULED: none. The PR is right.

All **788** PHON elements deleted (372 + 222 + 194). Confirms the maintainer's
call; also closes **GitHub issue #103** ("MontgomeryTexts: regenerate PHON and

### 3. ⛔ STANDARD TIER — the PR is wrong. It is NOT a copy of original.

The PR flattens the standard tier to `standardize.py --copy`, on the stated
premise that "no source-specific standardization profile is approved."
**That premise is false**, three ways:

- `Orthographies/ConversionTables/Amis_Montgomery_113.tsv` exists on main —
  5 rows: `ts→c`, `?→'`, `l→d`, `r→l`, `ř→r`.

  prints it in full. gb#70 *keeps Akiw's table on the page* while calling the
  conversion unapproved — self-contradictory.

Measured on main: **185 of 391 S+W FORMs (47%) differ** from original —
**38 of 40 S-level FORMs, 147 of 354 W**. Every S-level standard FORM
differs. So the "identical, therefore drop it" precedent (Latham
`be579c6b0`, Wakelin `f64dc5c0a`) does **not** apply here.

**It regenerates from the shared tool today.** Ran on the PR's own XML:

    python QC/utilities/standardize.py \
      --tsv_path Orthographies/ConversionTables/Amis_Montgomery_113.tsv \
      --corpora_path Corpora/MontgomeryTexts/XML

→ **357 of 388 standard FORMs byte-identical** to the published tier.
The 31-form residue is fully accounted for:

- **28 = the known C012 M-guard bug** (S-level segmentation hyphens survive
  because `standardize.py` gates hyphen-stripping on `element.find(".//M")`
  and this corpus has zero M). Escalated 2026-08-13, still unfixed; the
  identical shape hit Nowbucyang. Per POL-046 the fix is the shared guard,
  not a corpus script.
- **3 = the two original-tier disputes below**, propagating through.

### 4. "Lost alternative FORMs" — that was #181, not #174

Verified by count: MontgomeryTexts has **0** `kindOf="alternate"` FORMs on

respected (S1 retired, S2–S18 not renumbered), but "heading, therefore not

### 5. Two original-tier reversals, both checked against the scan at 1200 dpi

`Original.pdf` pages 2–5 are image-only (no text layer) — the PR's G020
explanation is accurate. Rendered and read directly.

- **`mi-salama` → `mi-salrama` (Silo S5): the PR is RIGHT.** Page 4, Silo

  *"The status of f̂ (which is rare) is uncertain."* One occurrence, 2 FORMs.
  Needs the maintainer's call before anyone changes it a third time.

## 2026-09-05 — RULING: strip accents on VOWELS only. Implemented; exception lists gone.

Maintainer proposal: *"what if we only consider accents on vowels."* Evaluated
over every published FORM, then implemented — `c88f7a40a` on
`fix/accent-keep-from-standard-orthography`. **1,050 passed / 7 skipped.**

**Answering the two questions directly.**

*Does it leave anything in place we actually want stripped?* **No.** Every
acute, macron or breve **on a vowel** still folds — `túturu`→`tuturu`,
`āyí`→`ayi`, `dourŭk`→`douruk`. That is the entire prosody case.

*Does it keep a great deal the rule never intended to touch?* **Yes — 488
consonant diacritics**, all of which we were wrong to strip:

| letter | corpus | n | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ḡ` `Ḡ` | Campbell-Favorlang, Siraya_Gospels | 273 | a 17th-century Favorlang letter |
| `ć` `ś` `ń` `ğ` `Ś` | Wikipedias | 213 | Slavic/Turkish proper nouns — `Tomislav Nikolić` now survives |
| `ř` `f̆` | MontgomeryTexts | 2 | transcription letters |

`y` and `w` are deliberately **not** vowels here: every orthography in the bank
maps them to the glides /j/ and /w/, so `ý` is a consonant carrying a diacritic.

**This retires the exception-list problem entirely.** `ḡ` is a consonant, so the
vowel rule protects it structurally — which is the second independent reason
`ALWAYS_KEEP` was unnecessary (`5264168dc`).

### ⛔ Still declining caron + grave, even restricted to vowels

Re-measured under the vowels-only rule: adding them destroys **197 real letters
and names** — 41 Siraya `à è ì ò ù`, 2 Favorlang `ò`, ~154 Romance proper nouns
in Wikipedias — to normalize **35** genuine pinyin tone-3 vowels. Mandarin
loanwords in Formosan text (`āyí`, `yípó`) are a closed set of *words*; a
character-class rule cannot target them.

### Siraya `--copy` — DECLINED, with a concrete cost

### 4. ⛔ Breve/macron are NOT primarily pinyin, and adding grave would damage data

Sampled every occurrence. **Macron** is partly pinyin (`āyí` in Yedda/ePark
Mandarin kin terms) but substantially 17th-century orthography — Favorlang
`paḡa`, `Tsinnummaḡach`; Siraya. **Breve is essentially never pinyin**: Turkish
`ğ`, Romanian `ă`, and phonetic transcription (`f̆`, `ř` in MontgomeryTexts,
`raoyăk`/`dourŭk` in Glosbe).

Also: **pinyin tone 3 is the caron U+030C, not the breve U+0306.** Currently
stripped: acute (T2) + macron (T1) + breve. Not stripped: caron (T3, 279) and
grave (T4, 235).

Measured what adding **grave + caron** would do — 514 FORMs, and the letters at
risk are the wrong ones:

| letter | corpus | n |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `š` `č` `ž` `Š` `Č` | Wikipedias | 350 |
| `à` `è` `ì` `ò` `ù` | Wikipedias | 288 |
| `à` | **Siraya_Gospels** | 70 |
| `ř` | **MontgomeryTexts** | 64 |
| `ò` | **Campbell-Favorlang** (`róòs`) | 3 |
| `ǎ` (actual pinyin T3) | Wikipedias | 26 |

So it would mangle ~640 Slavic/Romance proper nouns and destroy real letters in
three historical orthographies, to normalize ~26 genuine pinyin vowels.
**Not implemented.**

⏳ The problem you are actually pointing at is *Mandarin loanwords written in
pinyin inside Formosan text* (`āyí`, `yípó`) — a small closed set of words, not
