## 2026-09-05 — What `--remove_accents` actually strips, measured

Maintainer asked. Only **three** combining marks are ever removed, and only from
**Latin** base letters: U+0301 acute, U+0304 macron, U+0306 breve. Anything else
— combining tilde, Atayal's dot-below `ṟ`, cedilla — passes through, and
non-Latin scripts are never touched (Greek `ί ό ά έ ή`, Cyrillic `й у́ о́` all
survive). Exemptions: the language's standard-orthography accented letters
(now Rukai `é` only, per dialect) and `ALWAYS_KEEP` `ǣ ḡ`.

Counted over every original FORM in the bank: `é` 5,308 kept / 1,016 removed
(Rukai vs everywhere else) · `á` 2,207 · `í` 1,258 · `ē` 799 · `ó ú ā ō ī ū`
~1,870 · breves `ă ŭ ŏ ĕ` 202 · Kanakanavu `ʉ́` 11 → `ʉ` · `ḡ` 271 and `ǣ` 118
kept.

⏳ **Two things in that inventory worth a ruling, both pre-existing:**
- `ć` 51, `ğ` 19, `ś` 10, `ń` 1 are **foreign proper nouns in Wikipedias** —
  `Tomislav Nikolić`, a Belarus article. They fold to `c g s n`, so the standard
  tier spells the name `Nikolic`. Is stripping a diacritic off a foreign name
  intended?
- `ý` 4 and `ğ` 1 are in **Siraya_Gospels**, 17th-century Dutch-era orthography —
  and Siraya is exactly the language with a blank `standards.csv` entry, so
  nothing protects them. If `ǣ` warranted `ALWAYS_KEEP`, `ý` may too.

### Why `ǣ`/`ḡ` are still needed (also asked)

Because their languages have **blank `standards.csv` entries**, so
`standard_orthography_accents()` has nothing to read. Not decorative:
**Siraya_Gospels has a standard tier of 1,951 FORMs, 105 carrying `ǣ`** — without
the guard the next `standardize.py` run folds them into the corpus's 5,234 plain
`æ` and destroys the contrast. Campbell-Favorlang has only an original tier, so
its `ḡ` is protected pre-emptively. Proper retirement is a `standards.csv` entry
plus table for both, as `_accents.py`'s own comment says.

### Yedda's "validator" (also asked)

FormosanBank's own QC tooling, pinned. `rebuild_xml.sh` demands `VALIDATOR_ROOT`
— a **separate, clean** FormosanBank checkout at exactly `7c2e0b692` — and runs
`clean_xml.py`, `standardize.py` and `add_phonology.py` from it, aborting on any
other commit or a dirty tree. That commit is "Merge PR #185
fix/strip-macron-with-attested-keep" (2026-09-04); `main` is **47 commits**
past it. So Yedda is reproducible against a frozen toolchain and **cannot
receive any shared QC fix until `EXPECTED_VALIDATOR_COMMIT` is bumped** — a
deliberate design with a standing maintenance cost.

## 2026-09-05 — RULING + FIX: accent keep set comes from the STANDARD orthography

**Maintainer ruling:** *"When I said we should check whether it is attested in

as represented in Orthographies … We should definitely not be using
unique_characters.txt, which is used for orthography detection."*

**1,049 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed.**

New `_accents.standard_orthography_accents(language)` is the single source:
`standards.csv` names the scheme, that scheme's `<Language>.tsv` `letter` column
names the letters. `standardize._attested_accents` wraps it;
`add_phonology` keeps the accented letters of whichever profile it is applying
(the standard table for the standard tier, the `--orthography` table for the
original). The `unique_characters.txt` derivation is gone from both.

Resulting keep sets: **Rukai `é` only.** Puyuma, Yami, Thao, Kanakanavu, Amis
and the rest are empty. `ALWAYS_KEEP` (`ǣ`, `ḡ`) is unchanged and still needed —
Siraya and Babuza-Favorlang have blank `standards.csv` entries.

**A kept letter is now always a mappable one**, so folding can no longer be why
a PHON tier stars. Measured: **2,100 PHON change, 1,414 lose a star** —
RauDong (Yami) 1,098, ePark (Puyuma) 278, ePark (Rukai) 24, ILRDF_Dicts (Thao)
14 — and **501 standard-tier FORMs** fold an accent they had been keeping

**Bonus precision:** `Ortho113/Rukai.tsv` marks `é` **NA** for Wutai, Eastern,
Dawu, Dona and Wanshan, mapping it only for Maolin and `default`. The keep set
is now per dialect, so `é` folds in the five dialects that do not have the
letter — the old rule kept it for all of Rukai.

**Honest limit, checked:** 1,807 accent-bearing FORMs still star. Those stars

accent removed and getting identical output. They come from loanword letters
and proper nouns (`b` in Puyuma `bungka`, `o` in `Kalēngko`), which is the

## 2026-09-05 — The Yami "reference orthography" is a generated character dump

Maintainer asked which Yami reference orthography has accented letters. Answer:
**`QC/validation/reference/Yami/default/unique_characters.txt`** — the only one
(Yami has a single `default` dir). It ends `… y z á é í ó`.

**But it is not an orthography.** These files are *generated* by
`QC/orthography/orthography_extract.py`, which writes every distinct character
observed in the reference text. The Yami file also contains
`! " ' ( ) , - . / 0 1 2 3 4 5 9 : ; ?`; Puyuma's also contains `– … ！`. So
"in the inventory" means **this character occurs in the reference material**,
not "this language's orthography designates it a letter."

That is the root of the accent question. `_attested_accents()` in
`standardize.py` and `_reference_accented_letters()` in `add_phonology.py` both
read these files and treat presence as attestation — a rule that **cannot
distinguish an orthographic letter from a prosodic diacritic that merely
appears in the text**. Puyuma's `ē` is probably a real letter; Yami's
`á é í ó` are plausibly the very stress marks `_accents.py` cites as prosody in
its own docstring (`máduk`, `dálix`). Rukai is the clean case: `é` is both in
the inventory **and** mapped in `Orthographies/Ortho113/Rukai.tsv`.

⏳ **Open for you:** whether Yami `á é í ó` should be kept or folded. It decides
whether 1,098 RauDong forms keep their accents on regeneration, and whether the
star count roughly doubles.

that already exists for exactly this kind of cross-corpus pipeline gap — as

`docs/add-phonology-refresh`). It records the symptom, the 2,076 per-corpus
counts, the fact that the inventories are generated character dumps, and an
explicit warning that **regenerating RauDong or Li-Conjunction-Thao restores
those letters to the standard tier and roughly doubles RauDong's stars — an
expected diff, not a regression.** That is the note the PR-by-PR sweep will hit.

## 2026-09-05 — CORRECTION: `--remove_accents` DOES keep attested accents

**Maintainer was right, I was wrong.** I claimed `standardize.py
--remove_accents` strips every accent from the standard tier with no keep set.
That stopped being true on **2026-09-04**, in `37834a610` "Strip the combining
macron, protected by attested-letter keep sets" — whose commit message says in
so many words: *"strip_accents already took a keep set for exactly this, but
standardize.py never passed one … Two changes fix that."*

**My test was the bug.** I called `apply_standard(element, [])` directly,
reproducing the pre-fix call. The real signature is now
`apply_standard(s_element, standard, keep=frozenset())`, and `main()` derives
`keep_accents` per file via `_attested_accents(lang_code, dialect)` — reading
`QC/validation/reference/<Language>/[<dialect>|default]/unique_characters.txt`,
unioned with `_accents.ALWAYS_KEEP` — then passes it in **both** modes
(lines 429 and 512). Verified end-to-end instead of by unit call:

    Puyuma  'kēmay túturu āyí'  ->  'kēmay tuturu ayi'    (ē kept, acutes folded)
    Paiwan  'āyí yípó'          ->  'ayi yipo'            (macron not attested)
    Yami    'máduk dálix'       ->  'máduk dálix'         (á attested -> kept)

So the "three different keep policies" table in the entry below is wrong.
`standardize.py` and `add_phonology.py` now use **the same source** — the
language's reference orthography. Two small differences remain, neither a
defect: standardize scopes to the file's dialect while add_phonology unions all
dialects, and add_phonology additionally keeps the accented letters in its own
profile table. The Rukai `é` hazard I flagged does not exist.

### 🔴 What this does create: a pending change in two corpora's standard tiers

`37834a610` notes "corpora are not regenerated here." Measured today:

| Corpus | Language | attested accents in original | in standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RauDong | Yami `á é í ó` | 1,098 | **0** |
| Li-Conjunction-Thao | Thao `í` | 20 | **0** |
| ePark | Puyuma `é ē` | 455 | 455 |
| Presidential_Apologies | Puyuma | 27 | 27 |
| ILRDF_Dicts | Thao | 7 | 7 |

RauDong's and Li-Conjunction-Thao's standard tiers were built before the fix, so
their attested letters were stripped. **Regenerating either now restores them**
— correct in itself — and because `Orthographies/Ortho113/{Yami,Thao}.tsv` have
no rows for those letters, the standard PHON will then star too. RauDong's
1,098 stars would roughly double.

⏳ **Question this raises for you:** `_accents.py`'s own docstring gives Yami
`máduk`/`dálix` as the example of *prosodic* stress that should be removed — but
Yami's reference orthography lists `á é í ó`, so the keep set now protects
exactly those. Either the reference inventory is over-broad for Yami, or the
docstring example is stale. Worth deciding before RauDong is regenerated,
because that decision determines whether 1,098 forms keep their accents.

## 2026-09-05 — Accent-keep policy is inconsistent across four callers; null-PHON provenance

Answers to three maintainer questions, all checked by running the code.
Page updated on `docs/add-phonology-refresh` (`90322ec`).

### ⚠️ "We only keep accents in standard if they are in the standard orthography" — NO

`standardize.py --remove_accents` strips **every** accent from the standard
tier. There is no keep set in that mode: it calls `apply_standard(element, [])`
with an empty mapping list, so nothing is protected. Verified directly —
`é → e`, `ē → e`, `túturu → tuturu`. In TSV mode the protected set is the
diacritic-bearing letters **the conversion table lists**, which is not the same
thing as the standard orthography either.

So `strip_accents` now has **four callers and three different keep policies**:

| Caller | Keep set |
| --- | --- |
| `standardize.py` (TSV mode) | letters the conversion table lists explicitly |
| `standardize.py --remove_accents` | **nothing** |
| `orthography_detector.py` | letters attested in the language's orthographies |
| `add_phonology.py` (2026-09-04) | profile table + reference orthography |

⏳ **Latent hazard:** a Rukai corpus running `--remove_accents` would merge its
orthographic `é` into `e` in the standard tier. No corpus does today (the ten
that use the flag are Amis/Kanakanavu/Paiwan/Yami/Truku-side), but the
`_accents.py` docstring tells callers to pass a keep set and this one passes
none. Worth aligning `--remove_accents` with the reference-orthography keep set.

**"We leave them in original" — YES.** `apply_standard` only touches
`FORM[@kindOf='standard']`; POL-001 keeps the original tier untouched, and
`add_phonology` folds a working copy of the text, never the `FORM`.

**"Puyuma stars because é isn't in Ortho113 for Puyuma" — YES, exactly.** The
reference orthography attests it, so step 3 declines to fold; the Ortho113 table
has no row, so step 6 stars it.

### Which tier stars — the split is explained by `--remove_accents`

| Corpus | Language | original | standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RauDong | Yami | 1,098 | 0 |
| Li-Conjunction-Thao | Thao | 20 | 0 |
| ePark | Puyuma | 455 | 455 |
| Presidential_Apologies | Puyuma | 27 | 27 |
| ILRDF_Dicts | Thao | 7 | 7 |

RauDong and Li-Conjunction-Thao run `--remove_accents`, so their standard tier
has no accents left to star. The other three keep accents on both tiers.

### Null PHON `∅` vs `""` — provenance, and why it is not a free swap

- **Decided** in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-null-morpheme-handling-design.md`
  §5, implemented by `dd913c014` (2026-08-09), recorded as **POL-012**.
- **By whom:** the spec commit `5635af3be` and the implementation are both
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5`, committed under the maintainer's identity —
  a design-spec decision, **not an explicit human ruling**.
- **Stated rationale:** "PHON is never empty (empty tiers trip validators); a
  visible `∅` states 'this morpheme is silent'."
- **The rationale holds:** `V073_phon_non_empty` is **HARD** — an empty or
  whitespace-only PHON is a data error, with an existing carve-out only for
  `<UNCLEAR/>`. ⏳ So switching to `""` is a two-part change: a V073 carve-out
  for null morphemes plus the `phonologize` return. Maintainer's call; nothing
  blocks it technically.

### The page was stale in four ways — only one of them mine

The documented pipeline was 3 steps; the code runs 6.

1. **Mine.** No step for the stress-accent fold (`dc8edacb8`).
2. **`08d1eac99`.** The page opened with "It **always** processes the standard
   tier (using the `Orthographies/Ortho113` tables)". The scheme comes from
   `standards.csv` per language, and **a blank entry means standard PHON is
   deliberately skipped** — 16 of 18 name Ortho113; **Siraya and
   Babuza-Favorlang are blank**, so "always" was already false in published data.
3. **`dd913c014`.** Null handling undocumented: a whole-null FORM gets PHON `∅`;
   a null unit inside a form is dropped before mapping.
4. **`9fcae3125`.** The ordered `<Language>.rules.tsv` sidecars undocumented —
   applied after the mappings, dialect-scoped (blank = universal, named =
   that dialect, `default` = fallback). Four exist: Bunun, Seediq, Thao, Yami.

whitespace" becomes `*`, implying punctuation survives. Unmapped punctuation is
**dropped**; only unmapped *letters* star.

### 🔴 New finding: "kept" ≠ "mapped" — 2,076 stars in published PHON

Verifying my own draft caught it. I had written that the keep set is how
"Rukai é, Puyuma ē and Yami á survive". Ran it: `phonologize("ē", Puyuma)`
returns **`*`**, not `e`. The keep set only prevents *folding*; a kept letter
still needs a row in the orthography table, and only Rukai's `é` has one.

| Language | Attested, kept, but unmapped | Published PHON with `*` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yami | `á é í ó` | RauDong 1,098 |
| Puyuma | `é ē` | ePark 910, Presidential_Apologies 54 |
| Thao | `í` | ILRDF_Dicts 14 |
| | | **2,076** |

**Pre-existing, not a regression** — those letters starred before the accent
change too (they were unmapped then and are unmapped now). But my keep set
*locks in* the starring: without it they would fold to a base vowel that does
map. Keeping them is the linguistically right call — folding would merge two
distinct letters — so ⏳ **the fix is a row per letter in
`Orthographies/Ortho113/{Puyuma,Yami,Thao}.tsv`, not a code change.** Documented
on the page as a known gap meanwhile, so a reader does not chase it as a new
orthography problem.

⏳ Note this is a *different* worklist from the 9,355 stale tiers: those are
accents that will now fold on the next rebuild; these are accents that will
still star until the tables gain rows.

## 2026-09-05 — Pipeline standardization audit: there is no standard

Maintainer asked what the standard processing pipeline *is*, sketching
`refresh_source.sh` → `generate_xml.sh` (generate → clean → manual corrections
→ standardize → add_phonology). Audited all 27 corpus dirs on `origin/main`
(`ee1120120`) plus the newest state of every open PR touching `Corpora/`
(#148–#181) — **33 corpora**. Full report:
[claudeplans/2026-09-05-pipeline-standardization-audit.md](2026-09-05-pipeline-standardization-audit.md).

**Answer: no standard exists and nothing asserts one.** `POLICIES.md` has no
policy on the entry point, its name, or its step order; `QC/README.md` and the
`run-qc-pipeline` skill describe *QC* order for *dev repos*, not a published
corpus's `CodeAndDocs/`; CI never runs any corpus's build script. Result:
**8 entry-point conventions** (`make_xml.sh` 16, `reproduce.sh` 11,
`run_qc_pipeline.sh` 2, `Makefile` 1, `make.sh` 1, none 2) and **12 distinct
orderings** of the four shared steps. The plurality is `CLEAN>STD>PHON` (11),
or `ME>CLEAN>STD>PHON` counting manual edits (15) — i.e. the sketched shape is
already the modal practice; the gap is naming plus six real decisions.

The sketch maps well, with three forced adjustments: (1) `apply_manual_edits.py`
belongs **after** `clean_xml`, not before; (2) an explicit **baseline step 1**
(snapshot restore or scratch-dir staging) is needed or `generate_xml.sh` cannot
be idempotent; (3) validators stay **out** of the build. `refresh_source.py`
already exists under that exact name in #179 (ILRDF) and is the best template.

⏳ **The `apply_manual_edits` placement is genuinely contradictory — two merged
rulings disagree.** 2026-08-12 (Wikipedias) wired it *before* `clean_xml`
"per QC/README's documented order"; 2026-09-04 (HPS, maintainer ruling) wired it
*after* the cleaner and before standardize/add_phonology. Both are on `main`.
Five corpora do it one way (Wikipedias, SEALS33, #153, #180, Song), two the
other (HPS, #148), and NTU runs it dead last after 23 repair steps. The HPS
reasoning is right; `CLAUDE.md`, `QC/README.md` and Wikipedias' `make_xml.sh`
need to follow it. **Needs a ruling to close.**

⏳ **New findings not in the 2026-09-03 content audit:**
- **#180 silently downgrades Glosbe's standardization** — `main` runs four
  per-language transliterations (Amis Ortho94→113, Atayal Church→113, Truku,
  Saisiyat); #180 replaces all of them with a bare `standardize --copy`, deletes
  `make_xml.sh` and deletes the POL-035 snapshot. Glosbe's standard tier stops
  being a transliteration.
- **#158 removes `clean_xml` from Latham** — `main`'s `make_xml.sh` runs it;
  #158's does not, and no reference to it survives anywhere in the corpus.
- **NTU_Paiwan_ASR has no build script**, and #161 modifies 1,400+ of its XML
  files. Nothing committed reproduces them (POL-038).
- **#157 is the only open PR patching `QC/utilities/standardize.py`** — it adds
  `--single-pass`, which #157's own `make_xml.sh` uses and which does not exist
  on `main`. Merge-order dependency.
- **#174/#181 use a unique flag idiom** (`--corpora_path <corpus> --corpus XML
  --ortho-path <abs>`) for what all 23 other corpora write as
  `--corpora_path <XML dir>`.
- **`add_phonology --orthography` is used three ways** — name (18), filesystem
  path (#149, #151), omitted entirely (#153, #163, #179, #180).
- **#173 RauDong mutates published `XML/` in place with no baseline** — no
  snapshot, no staging dir.
- **Pinned-external-checkout builds are spreading** — #179/#180 require
  `FORMOSANBANK_AUTHORITY` at commit `3a3c47c22` (already 5+ commits stale),
  #180 also a private reference repo, #153/#154 `FORMOSANBANK_QC_ROOT`, and
  merged #178 `VALIDATOR_ROOT`. Contradicts the 2026-09-03 "rebuild from a
  FormosanBank checkout alone" ruling.

⏳ **Proposed, awaiting go-ahead:** a POL-042 fixing
`CodeAndDocs/generate_xml.sh` as the sole entry point with the ordered steps
above, plus a CI job that runs every `generate_xml.sh` in a clean clone and
asserts `git status` is empty. Nothing checks any of this today.

## 2026-09-04 — Song README/GitBook completeness audit: 2 wrong claims, 9 gaps

Audited both documents against what the pipeline actually does and against what
a linguist would need. Branch `work/song-standardize-on-main` `160fe6d9e`;
GitBook `docs/song-processing-notes` `710a064`. Both unpushed. Every number
below re-verified against the published XML.

### Two claims were wrong

- **"Two sentences … carry no analysis" — it is 49.** 699 S, 650 with W/M. The
  other 49: **47 are Appendix 1's punctuation table (pp. 187-191)**, which is a
  punctuation table rather than a glossed text, and 2 are body examples the book
  leaves unglossed (5-2 p.80, footnote 27 p.118). `UNANALYZED_SOURCE_IDS` lists
  only those 2, which is what the README had been reading. These 49 are exactly
  main's new V148 findings.
- **Step 8 still advertised the `takananga` standard-tier correction**, which
  moved to `manual_edits.xml` at step 5. Step 8 also overstated itself: of its
  128 decisions it **rewrites exactly one sentence** (the p.190 song); the other
  127 are verified, not applied.

Also structural: my earlier "Recorded per-record corrections" insert had been
placed *inside* the Notes bullet list, swallowing five bullets (partial
glossing, exclusions, repeats, unanalyzed words, rights). Moved below them.

### Nine gaps a linguist would have hit

Added to the README, and in lighter form to GitBook:

1. **The standard tier is near-identical to the original.** Ortho113 *is* the
   source orthography, so nothing is transliterated — across the whole corpus
   the two tiers differ only by folded stress accents and by one song sentence.
   Nobody should read "standard" here as evidence of a spelling change.
2. **Everything is Mandarin; there is no English.** All 10,090 TRANSL are `zho`.
3. **Glosses are the book's Chinese category labels** (`主事焦點`, `受事焦點`,
   `完成貌`, `非實現`, `重疊`, `主格`, `狀態改變`), **not Leipzig**. The 377
   glosses containing Latin text are proper names.
4. **Segmentation lives on W/M, never on S** — S FORMs are running text on both
   tiers; W/M keep `-`, `=`, `<…>` on **both** tiers (733 W with `-`, 484 with
   `=`, 117 with `<…>`).
5. **POL-014 infix notation**, with the worked example (`t<um>a-túturu` → `t-a`
   · `-um-` · `túturu`) — so an internal `-` in an M FORM is an infix gap, not
   an unsplit word.
6. **POL-015 clitic notation**, with the inventory: all 21 clitics are
   enclitics, every clitic M carries a **leading** `=`, no M carries a trailing
   one, and the gloss carries the marker too.
7. **PHON pipe notation** (POL-013): `[r|ɾ]` in 4,922 PHON elements means
   "either of these", not a literal bracket.
8. **No audio; no `alternate` FORMs.**
9. **The 49 unanalyzed sentences and the 4 unglossed M** stated with their
   validator ids, so a user meeting a V148/V064 row knows it is expected.

### QC section rewritten with measured numbers

Replaced the prose summary (which claimed "the XML validator has no finding")
with a per-validator table plus a reproduce-it command. Current state, all
measured on the branch: **no HARD finding anywhere**, `validate_port_readiness`
0 HARD / 0 WARN, and SOFT = `validate_xml` 49 (V148) · `validate_text` 6
(V122 4, V133 2) · `validate_glosses` 384 (V060 377, V061 3, V064 4) ·
`validate_duplicate_sentences` 63 groups. Each class is explained in place —
notably V060, where a host+clitic is one W but two whitespace-free words, so the
counts differ by design.

### 4 — what the add_phonology rewrite actually is

Three additions to `QC/utilities/add_phonology.py`, ~40 lines:

1. `_reference_accented_letters(language)` — cached; unions the accented
   letters in `QC/validation/reference/<Language>/*/unique_characters.txt`.
2. `PhonologyProfile.accented_letters` — that set unioned with the accented
   letters of the profile's own `letter` column, computed once in
   `load_profile`.
3. In `phonologize`, immediately before `apply_phonology_mappings`:
   `if _has_strip_mark(text): text = strip_accents(text, keep=profile.accented_letters)`.
   The guard matters: `strip_accents` NFC-composes whatever it touches, so an
   unrelated decomposed cluster (`a` + combining tilde) would otherwise stop
   matching its profile row and become `*`.

Nothing else changed — no mapping, no rule engine, no output format.

**Tests** (`tests/utilities/test_add_phonology.py`, 41 pass):
- `test_unknown_characters_star_marks_survive_punctuation_dropped` — rewritten.
  Was: a combining acute rides through, precomposed `á` → `*`. Now: both
  spellings fold to the base letter, and a **non**-stress combining mark (tilde)
  still rides through. Its fixture language moved Yami → Kanakanavu, because
  Yami's reference orthography attests `á` and the test is about starring.
- `test_profile_attested_accented_letter_is_not_folded` — new. A profile that
  lists `é` maps it to its own IPA; plain `e` is unaffected.
- `test_reference_orthography_accents_are_kept` — new. Puyuma keeps `é`, Yami
  keeps `á`, Kanakanavu keeps nothing, an unknown language returns empty.

Song's own `test_interlinear_regressions.py` (21 pass) covers the rest end to
end: the p.69 repair and its PHON, marker-freedom, and that no standard or
alternate FORM carries an accent while original FORMs do.

commits** on `origin/pr-160` (`2c8502f14`, `dbca2227a`); GitBook
`docs/song-processing-notes` is at `1d4ef5f`. Both unpushed.

### 4 — yes, we did rewrite add_phonology; it had never been done before

`git log` on `QC/utilities/add_phonology.py` shows **no accent handling in any
prior commit** — the null-morpheme, punctuation-dropping, dialect-rules and
standards.csv commits never touched accents. The rewrite is this session's work
and it is on the branch. The open item was never "should we do it" but the
**9,360 PHON tiers in 9 other corpora** whose committed output the rewrite makes
stale. Still unregenerated, still your call.

### 4c — DONE, and the maintainer's route is strictly better

**The book itself prints `takanaga`** — verified by rendering reader p.69 from
`raw_data/source.pdf` (a scan; no text layer, so the page image is the only
authority). Example 4-9's sentence line reads `rorovana ia, upeni takananga
kasu kumakʉnʉ?` and its own aligned analysis one line below reads
`takanaga=kasu`. So it is a **typesetting slip in the source**, not an OCR or
scraping artifact — the README's previous "the printed analysis line's OCR
reads takanaga" was simply wrong and is fixed.

Repairing the **original** (per your ruling) is better than the standard-only
patch on its own merits: the bare `g` is not an Ortho113 letter, so it had no
phonological mapping and surfaced as `*` in the **original PHON**. Song now has
**0 starred characters in PHON (was 2 — both this word)**.

Implemented as `CodeAndDocs/manual_edits.xml` (one record), applied by the
shared `apply_manual_edits.py` at build step 5; the standard tier and both PHON
tiers regenerate from it. `normalize_standard_forms.py` loses
`ANALYSIS_TIER_CORRECTIONS` and `normalize_analysis_tiers` entirely. The
extraction ledgers still record exactly what the page prints, and the p.69
regression test now pins the repair instead of the slip.

⏳ One thing to be aware of, not a blocker: POL-001 says the source's spelling
must be preserved, and this *is* the source's spelling — a one-off contradicted
by the same example two lines up. Worth a POLICIES line that a source's
self-contradiction is repairable in the original via `manual_edits`.

### 4d/4e — reader p.190 is a punctuation table; it answers both

Rendered the page. It is **Appendix 1, 族語標點符號及範例** (indigenous-language
punctuation marks and examples), and both sentences come from it:

- **Row 8 — 破折號 (em dash).** The book gives the halfwidth Kanakanavu spelling
  as **`--`** and the fullwidth Chinese equivalent as `―`. It is punctuation,
  not segmentation: the examples gloss `sumasima'ʉ--nguai …` as
  `不要跟Pani一起玩―就是那位酒鬼的兒子Pani。`. **We do not preserve `--`**:
  `build_xml.py` renders it as a single `-` in the **original** tier (the
  2026-08-07 reviewer decision), so the standard tier inherits it unchanged and
  the two decision rows (`S0469`, `S0472`) are **text-identity no-ops that only
  attach a `notes` string**. My earlier table row claiming the original keeps a
  double hyphen was wrong.
  ⏳ Worth revisiting: collapsing a defined em dash to `-` makes it
  indistinguishable from a segmentation hyphen — which is exactly why those two
  sentences are the corpus's only V133 findings. `—` (or the book's own `―`)
  would keep POL-011 satisfied without the ambiguity. Note `--` is *not* in
  POL-011's list (that lists single characters U+2010…U+2015 etc.), so this is a
  Song build decision, not a policy one.
- **Row 10 — 連結號.** Kanakanavu `-`, Chinese equivalent 無 (none), defined as
  *用於歌曲中，分解歌詞配合樂譜需求* — "used in songs, to break lyrics to fit the
  musical score." The example is `S0477`, a crab-catching song. So the hyphens
  are a musical notation, and the original tier rightly keeps them.
  Why the standard tier cannot just delete them: the printed
  `ti-sa-'ʉku-'a-pa-sʉ` would collapse to one word `tisa'ʉku'apasʉ`, where the
  attested reading is three (`tisa'ʉ ku 'apasʉ`). The e-reader text layer has
  also lost spaces around the line breaks (`'ara-vang'aa'ara-`). The boundaries
  therefore come from an independent attestation of the same song, pinned by
  commit + SHA-256 in `standard_surface_review.md`.

**Net: `S0477` is now the only standard-only edit in the corpus** — one
sentence, source-guarded, with external evidence.

(verified element-by-element); **1,024 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed** on the

### Settled by the maintainer

1. **Clitic `=`** — **verified corpus-local, not assumed.** Both functions are
   defined only in `Corpora/Song-Kanakanavu-Grammar/CodeAndDocs/scripts/
   extract_interlinear.py`; a repo-wide grep finds **zero references outside
   that corpus directory** (10 call sites in the script, 3 in Song's own

   `normalize_standard_forms`), and nothing imports them. No shared QC

   Q&A records, glued dictionary forms, sentence→word). So the unconditional
   enclitic rule is confined to Song, where it is correct: 530 leading-`=` M,

   to the original tier before the standard tier exists, and (b) the list being
   in README + GitBook. (a) **verified**: both override tables run at extraction
   (step 3), four steps before `standardize.py`. (b) **done** — see below.
6. **4 gloss-less M** — approved: keep the parsing, no invented glosses.

### 4 + 4b — DONE, and `add_shared_phonology.py` is gone

`standardize.py --remove_accents` replaces `--copy`; the shared
`add_phonology.py` replaces the wrapper; **both local scripts deleted**
(`fold_standard_stress.py`, `add_shared_phonology.py`).

The wrapper could **not** simply be dropped: run plain `add_phonology.py` on
Song's accented originals and **659 PHON change, 661 gain a `*`** (vs 2 in the
published file) — no profile maps a stressed vowel, so POL-003's "unmapped
letters surface as `*`" fires on every acute. Fix applied in the shared tool:
`phonologize` folds stress accents before mapping, keeping any accented letter
the language's **own** Ortho113 profile attests (Rukai `é`, via
`_accents.accented_letters` → `strip_accents(keep=…)`). With that, plain
`add_phonology.py` reproduces the published PHON **exactly** (0 of 20,160
differ).

Two things this exposed, both handled:
- `strip_accents` NFC-composes what it touches, so an unrelated *decomposed*
  cluster (`a` + combining tilde) would stop matching its profile row and turn
  into `*`. The fold is therefore **guarded** on `_has_strip_mark(text)`.
- `tests/utilities/test_add_phonology.py` asserted the **old** contract
  ("a combining acute rides through rather than being starred"; precomposed
  `á` → `*`). Updated, plus a new test pinning the Rukai `é` behavior.

**`keep` had to be widened past the Ortho113 profile.** Mid-session, main
gained `37834a610` "Strip the combining macron, protected by attested-letter
keep sets" — `_accents.ACCENTS_TO_STRIP` now includes the combining macron.
That is **not** in `origin/pr-160`, so this branch was re-verified against
main's copy. With profile-only `keep`, the change would have folded **Puyuma's
orthographic `ē` (1,488 FORMs) into `e`** — no `Orthographies/` table lists it;
only `QC/validation/reference/Puyuma/*/unique_characters.txt` does. `keep` is
therefore the union of the Ortho113 profile's accented letters **and** the
language's reference orthography (new `_reference_accented_letters`, cached).
Result: Puyuma keeps `é ē`, Yami keeps `á é í ó`, Thao keeps `í`, Rukai keeps
`é`; Kanakanavu, Amis, Seediq, Bunun, Truku, Kavalan, Tsou, Sakizaya keep
nothing. Song reproduces byte-identically under **both** versions of
`_accents.py`. This also moved one existing test off the "Yami" fixture — Yami
attests `á`, so its acute is orthographic and must not fold.

⏳ **Ruling needed — this is a bank-wide change, not a Song cleanup.** Measured
by running the new `phonologize` over every published accent-bearing FORM that
has a PHON: **9,360 PHON tiers across 9 corpora would change**, and 1,315 stay
put because the accent is attested as orthographic.

| Corpus | Language | PHON changed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ePark | Rukai | 5,956 |
| RauDong | Yami | 870 |
| NTUFormosanCorpus | Kanakanavu | 759 |
| ePark | Puyuma | 721 |
| Wikipedias | Sakizaya / Amis / Seediq / Atayal / Paiwan | 363 / 172 / 157 / 125 / 110 |
| Glosbe | Seediq / Atayal | 34 / 12 |
| NTUFormosanCorpus | Sakizaya | 23 |
| Li-Conjunction-Thao | Thao | 20 |
| ILRDF_Dicts | Thao / Amis | 14 / 8 |
| YeddaPalemeqBlog | Paiwan | 10 |
| MontgomeryTexts | Amis | 4 |
| ePark | Paiwan | 2 |

**Nothing was regenerated** — the branch changes the code, not those corpora.
The alternative — adding `á é í ó ú` rows to
`Orthographies/Ortho113/Kanakanavu.tsv` — was rejected: the profile is the
language's orthographic inventory, and á is not a Kanakanavu letter, so it
would also tell `orthography_detector`/`validate_orthography` that á is
legitimate.

Side effect, an improvement: the wrapper owned the final write, and its
2-space indent made Song's two files **the only two in the bank** with that
serialization (13,650 files use `<?xml version="1.0" ?>` + 4-space). They now
match the majority.

### 4c — manual_edits CANNOT do this. Structural, by design.

`manual_edits_common.strip_s()` **deletes every `FORM[@kindOf="standard"]` and
every `PHON` (S, W and M)** before storing or comparing a record. POL-002 states
the intent: "an edit made *only* to a standard FORM or PHON is invisible to
capture and futile anyway." So a `manual_edits.xml` cannot express any of these
edits — not the text, not the `@notes`.

What is actually left to host, after the accent work removed the rest —
**three standard-only edits, and each meets your "really good reason" test**
because POL-001 forbids fixing the original:

| Record | original must keep | standard must be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `S0012` W4 + M | `takanaga=kasu` — what p.69's analysis line prints | `takananga=kasu` (Ortho113 has no bare `g`) |
| `S0477` | the lyric-division hyphens as printed (p.190) | `mati'ara'aravang 'aa 'aravang vatu 'aravang vatu! tisa'ʉ ku 'apasʉ.` — word boundaries **independently attested**, not derivable by deleting hyphens |
| `S0469`, `S0472` | the double-hyphen break punctuation | same text, single dash — **text-identity writes**; only a `@notes` is added |

Routes considered and rejected:
- **Edit the original instead** → POL-001 violation in all three.
- **A conversion table row `g` → `ng`** → `standardize.apply_standard` does
  sequential `str.replace`, so it would also turn the corpus's 1,418 existing
  `ng` into `nng`. (Bare `g` outside `ng` occurs exactly 3× — the 2 `takanaga`
  plus one capitalized `Ng`.)
- **C012** → cannot produce S0477: removing the hyphens from
  `ti-sa-'ʉku-'a-pa-sʉ` yields one word, `tisa'ʉku'apasʉ`; the source-attested
  reading is three (`tisa'ʉ ku 'apasʉ`).

⏳ **Your call.** Either (a) a POL-002 carve-out for a declared, source-guarded
decision table, or (b) the `standardize.py --decisions <tsv>` input proposed in
the POL-002 entry below, which would move all four corpora's patchers inside
`standardize.py`. Separately: the **125 dictionary decisions write nothing** —
they are pure verification and belong in `CodeAndDocs/tests/`, not in a build
step that runs after `standardize.py`.

### 5 — `takananga` confirmed, and documented

Not in doubt: **`takananga` occurs 22×** in the corpus — including the S-level
FORM of this very sentence, `rorovana ia, upeni takananga kasu kumakʉnʉ?` —
while `takanaga` occurs **exactly twice**, both inside that one word's analysis
line. The book contradicts itself within a single example.

### Documentation (items 3 + 5) — DONE

- **README** gains a **"Recorded per-record corrections"** section: one table for
  the original-tier extraction overrides (all five `MORPHEME_OVERRIDES` entries
  with reader page, what the source prints, and what is recorded) and one for
  the three standard-only edits, plus a note that the 125 dictionary decisions
  only verify. Pipeline steps 3, 7 and 9 rewritten to match the new flow.
- **GitBook** page gains `## **Corpus Processing**` + `## **Corpus Notes**`
  (the `RauDong.md` convention — which carries the same accent note), linking to
  the README section and `standard_surface_review.md`.
  `manage_corpus_pages.py check` OK; 26/27 GitBook tests pass —
  `test_policies_sync` fails **on clean `origin/main` too** (the known
  policies.md drift, [[gitbook-policies-sync-gap]]).

## 2026-09-04 — #160 Song: accents CAN move into standardize.py (tested); nulls already shared

Answers three maintainer questions on `normalize_standard_forms.py` /
`fold_standard_stress.py`, and corrects the account of them in the
"standard-tier edits outside standardize.py" entry below.

**Baseline established:** `make_xml.sh` rebuilds both Song XMLs
**byte-identically** to main in 7.5 s (scratch copy, `FORMOSANBANK_PATH`
= this checkout). Every claim below is from that harness, not from reading.

### 1. Accents → `standardize.py --remove_accents`: YES, works. Tested.

Swapping step 6 `--copy` → `--remove_accents`, deleting
`fold_standard_stress.py`, and folding the decision outputs at the four
places they are compared/written in `normalize_standard_forms.py`
produces **byte-identical XML**. The four places (each fails loudly, in
this order, if missed):

1. `normalize_dictionary` compares `standard.text == output` — 14 decision
   rows / 19 entries have accented outputs. First failure:
   `dictionary-0070 standard drifted ... 'ikamu'; expected 'íkamu'`.
2. `assert_marker_free`'s `allowed` whitelist is built from raw (accented)
   outputs; the folded standard no longer matches (`S0469 retains analysis
   marker`).
3. `apply_decision` writes `standard.text = output_forms[0]` — S0469's
   output carries `napá'ici`, so a naive swap silently re-accents one
   sentence.
4. `normalize_analysis_tiers` compares/writes the two W/M corrections
   (accent-free today, but same shape).

Fix is `strip_accents(...)` at those four call sites (+1 import). Leave
the `alternate` outputs unfolded — see 4.

**Blocker to note:** `add_shared_phonology.py` does `from
fold_standard_stress import fold_stress`, so the file cannot simply be
deleted; repoint it at `QC.utilities._accents.strip_accents`.

`strip_accents` ≡ the private `ACCENT_MAP` on this corpus, verified
exhaustively: the **only** combining mark anywhere in Song's FORM+PHON is
COMBINING ACUTE (811 occurrences). The earlier (2026-08-12) conclusion
that the swap "cannot" be done was wrong on its stated reason — the 15
accented decision rows key on the **original** tier, which standardize
never touches.

Side effects of `--remove_accents` beyond accents, both verified no-ops on
Song: `remove_null_units` (0 nulls, see 2) and C012 (the 3 hyphen-bearing
S have **no M tier**, so C012 does not fire — the two break dashes are safe).

### 2/3. ∅ and Ø: both mechanisms already exist in main, and Song bypasses one

- **Removing nulls from the standard tier** — `standardize.remove_null_units()`,
  POL-012. It is **skipped in `--copy` mode by design** ("`--copy` keeps them;
  V120 SOFT"). Song runs `--copy`, so Song opts out. The swap in 1 opts it
  back in — a second reason to make it.
- **Unifying ø/Ø/∅ → ∅** — `clean_xml.normalize_null_morphemes()` (POL-012),
  on every tier including original, already **step 5 of Song's own
  `make_xml.sh`**. So `\u00d8` in `DICTIONARY_MARKER_RE`/`GRAMMAR_RESIDUE_RE`
  is unreachable for the null case by the time those run.
- Both are moot on today's data: **`∅`, `Ø`, `ø`, `+`, `{`, `}` occur zero
  times** anywhere in Song. Minor defect if kept: the two regexes list `Ø`
  (U+00D8) but not `ø` (U+00F8) or `⌀`, which G006 treats as the commoner
  variants — the guard misses what it is most likely to see.

### 4. The `alternate` half of `fold_standard_stress` — agreed, drop it

Dead **and** unreachable today: 0 `alternate` FORMs exist, and the only
code path that creates one (`apply_decision`, outputs 2..n) is reached
solely from `normalize_grammar`, which asserts exactly one output. If it
ever did fire it would strip stress from a source-facing tier with no
policy behind it.

### Correction to the entry below ("C012 under-fires", #160 bullet)

`normalize_standard_forms.py` does **not** "remove the residue by hand
(128 decisions)". Verified by instrumented run:

- **Dictionary (125 of the 128): zero writes.** `normalize_dictionary` only
  *asserts* — originals apparatus-free, 870 entries, 26 duplicate ids absent,
  11 bound ids absent, 228 split-variant entries matching their reviewed
  output. The residue is never in the dictionary standard tier because
  `build_xml.py` emitted one clean surface per entry *before* `--copy` ran.
- **The 26 duplicate drops and 11 bound exclusions happen in `build_xml.py`**,
  which imports `DUPLICATE_VARIANT_ENTRY_IDS` from `normalize_standard_forms`
  and cross-checks it against its own computation.
- **Actual text mutations: three.** S0477 (lyric relayout) and the two W/M
  `takanaga`→`takananga` corrections. S0469/S0472 are text-**identity**
  writes that only add `@notes`.
- Decision classes: 100 slash variants (POL-027), 12 semicolon lexemes (no
  POL — local extension), 11 bound exclusions (no POL), 2 break dashes
  (POL-011), 1 optional word `'akia (na)` (POL-026), 1 mixed lexical
  variant, 1 lyric layout.

### Two gaps against main that survive either way

- **POL-022 dedup is invisible.** `validate_duplicate_sentences` greps
  CodeAndDocs for `remove_duplicate_sentences|dedup`; Song's private id list
  says neither, so its **63 within-file duplicate groups stay SOFT** instead
  of HARD. Song *is* a reference resource that dedups — it just does not say so.
- **`assert_marker_free` is a build-time HARD copy of V120/V121/V122/V129/V133.**
  Residual SOFT after the run is exactly **6**: V133×2 (the reviewed break
  dashes) and V122×4 (S0456, a genuine parenthetical clause mirrored in the
  Chinese TRANSL — not POL-026 optional material; correctly whitelisted).

### PR #160 vs main — what is NEW, what is LOST

`origin/pr-160` = `fac70df27`; merge-base with main = `3a3c47c22`, and **main
has not touched Song since**, so the Song comparison below is exactly
PR-vs-main. The PR is 12 commits behind main, but merging loses none of that
(the large `git diff main..pr-160` is direction artifact, not content).
The PR's own footprint is 15 files: the Song corpus plus one shared QC rule.

**Nothing is removed.** 0 ids present in main and absent in the PR. S = 699,
W = 3,477, `TEXT` attributes, every S/W/M attribute, and all ids unchanged
(POL-037 safe). **Token delta 0** (5,256 Kanakanavu, both). The **dictionary
XML is byte-identical**. All change is in the grammar file's M tier.

**NEW — POL-014/POL-015 morpheme-tier conformance (the whole point of the PR):**
- **996 clitic-boundary moves — the `=` moves OFF the host ONTO the clitic**,
  staying on the same side of the same boundary. `te=musu`: main `te=` + `musu`
  → PR `te` + `=musu`. 466 host M lose a trailing `=`, 530 clitic M gain a
  leading `=`; 1,232 M glosses follow (`告知=` `狀態改變=` → `告知` `=狀態改變`).
  POL-015 says the **clitic** FORM retains the marker, so the PR is conformant
  and main had it on the wrong element. Verified: PR160 has 530 leading-`=` M
  and **0 trailing**; main had 0 and 530. All 21 distinct clitic forms are
  genuine enclitics (`=cu` 118, `=ku` 67, `=maku` 45, `=in` 45, `=kasu` 42 …)
  and **0 M `=` placements disagree with their W surface**.
  ⚠️ The new `split_morphemes`/`split_clitics` do this **unconditionally** —
  every `=` starts the next morpheme. Right for Song (no proclitics), but the
  splitter assumes it rather than reading position; a future proclitic corpus
  reusing this code would be silently wrong.
- **239 infix re-analyses, covering ALL 117 W with inline `<>`** (0 left
  unchanged) — not just the Ca-reduplication cases. Main's **gloss pairing was
  already correct** (`um`↔`<主事焦點>`, `ra`↔`Ca重疊-`); what it violated were
  the three things POL-014 names explicitly:
  1. infix M emitted **first**, out of surface order;
  2. root written **rejoined without the gap hyphen** (`ra`, `ta`, `tituru`) —
     POL-014: "writing the root *rejoined* with no hyphen (`ta`)" is the
     deviation;
  3. infix written bare `um` instead of `-um-`.
  `r<um>a-ravisi`: main `um`/`ra`/`ravisi` → PR `r-a`/`-um-`/`ravisi`, glosses
  unchanged and now in surface order. Plain infixes too: `t<in>ituru` →
  `t-ituru`/`-in-`. The 239 PHON pairs regenerate to match; **no PHON changed
  without its FORM changing**.
- **+14 M from a NEW hardcoded `MORPHEME_OVERRIDES` table** in
  `extract_interlinear.py` — 5 hand-authored entries (S0318 `t<in>i-taini`,
  S0422 `m-ukʉrʉ`, S0609 `ka-cangcangarʉ-a`, S0636 `pa-arivivini-ʉn`, S0678
  `t<um>a-túturu`), each pinning the expected W FORM + W TRANSL + M list, on
  five page images where the printed form and gloss lines do not align 1:1.
  3+2+3+3+3 = 14 M, 4 of them deliberately gloss-less. **Not parser-derived.**
  This is a *second* override table in that file (`ANALYSIS_OVERRIDES` already
  existed) — worth weighing against POL-039 (no data tables hidden in code).
- **2 TRANSL relocations, POL-024-conforming and NOT lossy** — I checked the
  attributes: `我有錢。（=我的錢存在）` moves out of the primary TRANSL text
  into `TRANSL/@notes`, which is what POL-024 prescribes for an analytic
  paraphrase. New `docs/mt_quality_review.md` records both, plus two
  `extreme_fertility` findings deliberately retained as dictionary definitions.
- **1 shared QC change:** `gloss_scrape.G003` stops flagging an internal `-`
  in an M FORM when that M is an **exact** POL-014 gap root derived from its
  parent W's inline infix (`t<um>a` licenses `t-a`). Narrowly scoped —
  unrelated internal dashes still flag. Plus `make_xml.sh` gains
  `apply_manual_edits.py` (checked no-op), `rm -f XML/cleaner_warnings.csv`
  (POL-033 — main's build leaves that file in `XML/`, neither committed nor
  gitignored, so a rebuild dirties the tree), and a repinned reference commit.
- `normalize_standard_forms.py`: **1 line, and it is not clitic logic** — the
  entry is the `g`→`ng` spelling repair for `takanaga`/`takananga` (reader p69
  prints the sentence and its analysis differently), and the tuple is a
  *lookup key matched against M FORM text*. The clitic resegmentation changed
  that text (`takanaga=` → `takanaga`), so the key had to follow. The `=`
  handling itself lives entirely in `extract_interlinear.py`. `fold_standard_stress.py` and
  `standard_surface_decisions.tsv` are **unchanged**.

**LOST — one thing, and it is a trade, not a deletion:**
- **4 M now carry no gloss** (main: 0) — `m-ukʉrʉ` M01/M02, `pa-arivivini-ʉn`
  M03 `ʉn`, `t<um>a-túturu` M01 `t-a`. These are *newly added* morphemes on
  words that previously had no M tier, and **all three parent W keep their
  word-level TRANSL** (`拿著`, `使動-跟隨在後`, `<主事焦點>-告知`), so no gloss
  content is lost — the words are simply now segmented past what the source
  glosses. In the shared validators: **V061 8 → 3, V064 0 → 4** (net −1 SOFT;
  `validate_text` unchanged at 6 SOFT).
- ⏳ This reverses, for these words, the sweep's recorded call that "V144
  (7 W) deliberately not actioned — the book prints a single gloss for those
  complex words." Segmenting past the source's gloss line is defensible, but
  it is a reversal and should be ruled on, not absorbed.

⏳ **For you:** approve the accent swap (4 call sites + 1 import + delete
`fold_standard_stress.py` + repoint `add_shared_phonology.py`), and say
whether it lands on #160 or as a follow-up. It leaves the published XML
byte-identical and removes one of the four POL-002 offenders below.

## 2026-09-04 — CONFIRMED: Yedda has never had morpheme glosses

Maintainer asked for confirmation before documenting it. **Confirmed, three
independent ways:**
1. **Every version that has ever existed has zero `M/TRANSL`** — all nine
   commits touching the XML on `main` back to `0c0231d5d` "Yedda's blog now
   added", plus both PR branches.
2. **Both frozen scrape snapshots have zero** (#148 `raw_xml/`, #178
   `data/source_snapshot/`).
3. **The scraper cannot emit one.** `analyze_blog_structure.py` creates
   `TRANSL` under `s_elem` and `w_elem` only; `M` is created under `w_elem` and
   never given a `TRANSL` child. No code path exists.

So the absence is a property of the blog, not a processing gap. Corroborated by
`glossed_words = 0` against `segmented_words = 4,475` in the published stats.

**Why this matters — it reframes V064 and V062.** The blog *segments* (marking
infixes inline in angle brackets, `s<em>eljec-an` — that notation in the FORM is
the sole basis of the M tier) but *glosses only words*, in prose. Hence:
- V064's 6,492 findings are not recoverable data; supplying them is original
  linguistic work, additive under POL-036.
- V062's 274 findings are a **notation** difference, not missing data — e.g.
  `S288_1W3` says "-em- is actor voice (AV) case marker, and -in- is undergoer
  voice" in prose rather than `<AV>`.
- Corrects a wrong assumption I nearly shipped in the #82 draft: infixes are
  identified from the **FORM's** angle brackets, **not** from any M-level gloss.
  There are no M-level glosses to identify anything from.

Documented in both the README (opening description + "Reading the tiers") and
the GitBook page (Overview + Glossing + Morpheme sections), tied to the two
statistics a reader can see. FormosanBank `518a3636d`, GitBook `7e781a5`.

## 2026-09-04 — Macron stripping (repo-wide) + apply_standard_surface retired

**Maintainer ruling (2026-09-04):** *"Lets add stripping the macron
repo-wide."* Done, but **not as a one-line change** — see below.

### ⚠️ The naive version would have destroyed data

Adding U+0304 to `ACCENTS_TO_STRIP` alone would conflate a real letter with its
bare base in **three** languages, each contrastive in its own corpus:

| lang | letter | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `pyu` Puyuma | `ē` | 744 in the standard tier; **`QC/validation/reference/Puyuma/` attests it** in all 5 dialect inventories |
| `fos` Siraya | `ǣ` | 236 in Siraya_Gospels beside 5,234 plain `æ` |
| `bzg` Favorlang | `ḡ` | 263 in Campbell-Favorlang beside 1,013 plain `g`, +16 in Siraya |

Exactly the phoneme-conflation class the sweep spent months fixing (tj/c, z/r,
ř/r). The other ~617 macrons — szy 245, ami 154, trv 99, tay 58, pwn 61 — are
loanword/prosodic notation in languages attesting no macron letter, and are
what we actually want stripped.

**Root cause of the hazard:** `strip_accents` has always taken a `keep` set,
but **`standardize.py` never passed one** — `--remove_accents` calls
`apply_standard(element, [])`, an empty mapping, so nothing was protected.
`orthography_detector.py` did pass one. That asymmetry was latent.

### What shipped — branch `fix/strip-macron-with-attested-keep` (`37834a610`)

- `_accents.py`: macron added to `ACCENTS_TO_STRIP`; new `ALWAYS_KEEP =
  {ǣ, ḡ}` unioned into `keep` on every call, for languages with **no reference
  orthography directory at all** (fos and bzg have none). Remove an entry when
  its language gains one.
- `standardize.py`: derives a keep set per file from
  `QC/validation/reference/<Language>/[<dialect>|default]/unique_characters.txt`
  and passes it through `apply_standard` → `strip_accents`, in **both** the
  table-driven and `--remove_accents` modes.
- Verified end-to-end on real corpora: **Puyuma ē 92/92 kept, Siraya ǣ 10/10
  kept, Paiwan ā 3/3 stripped.** Full suite **1046 passed, 7 skipped**. One
  existing test asserting `ō` survives was moved to the stripped table.
- ⏳ **Corpora are NOT regenerated** by this PR; standard tiers pick it up on
  the next `standardize.py` run. Yedda's `āyi` becomes `ayi` only after this
  merges *and* Yedda is rebuilt.
- ⏳ Follow-up worth considering: Favorlang and Siraya have **no reference
  orthography at all**, so nothing validates their letter inventories. That is
  why `ALWAYS_KEEP` had to exist.

### apply_standard_surface.py retired (Yedda, `e4c2fe6ac`)

**Maintainer question:** *"Would we lose anything replacing it with #148's
manual_edits?"* **Answer: manual_edits cannot express this at all.**
`manual_edits_common.strip()` deletes every `FORM[@kindOf='standard']` and every
`PHON` from a recorded `<S>` before storing it (POL-002/POL-030) — a record
would capture nothing. Nor is upstream blog drift the issue: the build reads a
frozen snapshot, so both mechanisms are equally immune.

Resolved the underlying goal instead — *nothing edits the standard tier after
`standardize.py`*: C012 already produces the `S652653654_2` standard surface by
rule, so the script had nothing left to do but attach a note. The note moved to
that sentence's **original** FORM, written by `build_xml.py` before any derived
tier exists, asserted and fail-closed. The pipeline now runs nothing after
`standardize.py` except `add_phonology`. Test asserts the note is on the
original and that **no standard FORM carries one**. XML unchanged apart from
that attribute; gate 0 HARD / 0 WARN, 9,918 accepted.

## 2026-09-03 — Yedda #148 vs #178: three-way XML diff

Maintainer asked for a catalogue of how the two open Yedda PRs' XML differs
from each other and from `main`, with causes. Full report: artifact
`a27dbb4a-2b04-4111-a416-b4edd26104c7`. Method: all three blobs of
`Corpora/YeddaPalemeqBlog/XML/Paiwan/Paiwan_Yedda_Blog.xml` parsed into
normalized per-S/W/M records and compared field by field, plus the three
validators run against each. `main`'s blob is identical at both PRs' merge
bases, so the comparison is clean.

**Five repairs both PRs make character-identically** (settled either way):
(1) PHON regenerated with `tj` de-conflated from `c` — 662 S, 1,510 W, ~900 M;
(2) PHON no longer carries punctuation, hyphens or infix angle brackets
(both re-run current `add_phonology.py`); (3) the three source-alternative
splits actually applied — **`main`'s S535 is broken**: both halves read
`tjangtjang`, `_1`'s FORM still prints the raw `tjangtjang / siyak`, and the
`tjangtjang` W element is missing from a sentence whose own FORM asserts it;
(4) three double-infix words split correctly, clearing `main`'s only HARD
findings (3×V067, plus 3×V061); (5) `S535_1.wav` withdrawn (666→665 AUDIO,
4227.6→4217.7 s) and `audio_url` dropped on the six split records.

**Three real disagreements:**
- ⏳ **M tier.** #148's `fix_m_tier.py` (the 2026-08-12 per-sentence ruling)
  strips the M element from 1,165 words in unparsed sentences: M 7,654→6,492,
  `segmented_words` 5,641→**4,475**. #178 keeps them (7,657) and reports them
  as 7,657 SOFT V064 source limitations. **`fix_m_tier.py` is NOT a no-op over
  #178's output** — it is the piece of #148 worth salvaging if #178 lands
  first, and it is independent of the manual-edits machinery.
- ⏳ **Translations.** Only #178 has the 24 sentence + 41 word repairs from the
  2026-08-23 live re-fetch: 9 wholly missing S translations restored (S with no
  TRANSL 9→**0**; `eng_transl_count` 5,863→5,877 = every sentence translated),
  15 truncated ones completed, and word glosses pulled back out of five free
  translations. **Both frozen intermediates carry the same 5,501 TRANSL**, so
  #148 has no path to this content — merging #148 alone leaves 9 sentences
  untranslated.
- ⏳ **Accents.** #148 runs `standardize.py --remove_accents`; #178 runs
  `--copy`. Only #148 flattens two quoted Mandarin kin terms in the standard
  tier, and only half-way: `yípó`→`yipo` but `āyí`→`āyi`, because
  `_accents.py::ACCENTS_TO_STRIP` holds only the combining acute and breve.
  Its docstring calls accents "prosodic noise" — pinyin tone marks are lexical.
  Worth a ruling on whether the standard tier should flatten a quoted
  non-Formosan word at all.

Also: #178 writes 11 `FORM/@notes` + 76 `TRANSL/@notes` of provenance and one
reviewed standard-tier segmentation removal (`S652653654_2`, via its own
`apply_standard_surface.py`); #148 writes none. Both PRs emit
`<?xml version="1.0" ?>` where `main` emits `encoding='UTF-8'`. #178's
validator totals reproduce its `QC_STATUS.md` exactly (8,680 gloss SOFT,
2,419 text SOFT). #148's lower SOFT counts are arithmetic, not quality.

**Maintainer:** *"Yes, let's not depend on a previous commit."* Done —

**What the baseline is actually for** (asked, and worth recording): only two
things are not derivable from the DOCX —
- **Morpheme ids.** 36,815 inherited verbatim from the published corpus; 123
  more derived by suffixing when one published `M` splits into several source
  units (`M0` → `M0a/b/c`, e.g. `078S4W19M0c`). POL-037 forbids renumbering.
  **S and W ids are computed from the source** (`{story}S{ordinal}`,
  `{sentence}W{position}`) and the baseline only *asserts* none disappeared.
- **Four `TEXT` attributes** — `id`, `citation`, `BibTeX_citation`, `dialect`.
The published W FORM is never read, so the skeleton needed is small.

**Now committed as data:**
- `data/baseline_text_metadata.tsv` — 100 rows (52 KB)
- `data/baseline_morphemes.tsv` — 36,705 rows, document order (1.8 MB)

`rebuild_xml.py` gains `load_baseline()` and loses `--baseline`;
`make_xml.sh` **no longer invokes git at all**. `scripts/export_baseline.py`
regenerates the tables from an XML tree so they stay auditable against the
corpus they came from (not part of the build). `provenance.json` reverts to
pure documentation.

🐛 **Subtlety worth remembering:** an empty cell means the attribute was
**absent**, not present-and-empty. Story 098 carries no `source` attribute at
all, which `text_metadata_corrections.tsv` records as `<missing>`; the loader
must omit empty values rather than set `""`, or 098 fails its metadata witness
(`story 098: baseline metadata differs from review`). Hit this on the first run.

**Verified the actual claim, not just the build:** copied the tree to a
directory with **no `.git` whatsoever** and `make_xml.sh --check` exits 0.

⏳ **Generalisable:** every other RE-PORT PR that reconciles against a baseline
has the same latent tie to a reachable commit. Worth the same treatment.

`rebuild_xml.py --baseline` at `$BANK/Corpora/HundredPaiwanStories/XML` — the
**live** tree, which on this branch is the corpus's own rebuilt output. The

## 2026-09-04 — RULING: correct the ORIGINAL tier, never repair the standard

**Maintainer:** *"We really shouldn't be editing the standard forms... the
remaining edits should be applied to original prior to running standardize.py...
without changing the final content of the standard tiers."* **Feasible, and
implemented** — `2bf541f44` (FormosanBank) + `551f1c0` (GitBook).

New `CodeAndDocs/scripts/apply_manual_corrections.py` (modelled on
NTUFormosanCorpus's) removes the source's `(?)` uncertain-reading annotation
from the **S-level original FORM before `standardize.py`/`add_phonology.py`
run**, recording what it removed in that FORM's `notes` attribute. Each of the
11 is witness-gated against `original_form` in the decision table and fails on
drift; idempotent; the build asserts 11/11.

- **Constraint met:** standard **FORM** content is byte-identical.
- 🐛 **It also fixed a real defect.** `?` is the **glottal letter** in Ferrell's
  orthography, so a `(?)` left in the original standardizes to a glottal stop
  the language does not have. The old post-hoc repair fixed the standard *FORM*
  and **never the PHON** — the published phonology carried invented consonants
  (`qəpuqəpuiʔ`, `aʔ`, `sinʦəvuŋanʔ`). Correcting the original fixes both tiers:
  **9 standard PHON and 9 original PHON elements lose a spurious `ʔ`**
  (PaiwanCh2_091 alone: 10 → 2).
- `V122` **8,050 → 8,028**, exactly the 22 parens; no sentence FORM carries a
  parenthesis any more, so `EXPECTED_V122_TIERS` loses its `S.FORM.original` key.
- `normalize_sentence_standards.py` now corrects **nothing** (`corrected_forms=0`)
  — it runs after `standardize.py` purely to verify all 16 decisions hold.
- README/GitBook rewritten: both mechanisms act on the original tier; neither
  edits a generated tier.
- ⚠️ **A README edit was silently lost earlier** (a `p.write_text()` was never
  reached after an assertion failed mid-block), leaving the README contradicting
  itself about `manual_edits.xml`. Caught and fixed in the same commit.

## 2026-09-04 — RULING: hyphens out of the standard tier (#167)

**Maintainer ruling:** *"I actually want those hyphens removed from standard.
Hyphens aren't part of the standard orthography."* Implemented in
`4284801a8` (FormosanBank) and `cdfcbef` (GitBook).

Context from the other instance's review: `normalize_sentence_standards.py`
repaired the standard tier after `standardize.py`, because C012 was wrong for
this corpus — Ferrell §1.6 has three interlinear levels and the plain-text
first line (→ S FORM) legitimately carries hyphens, which C012 stripped.
Keeping them in the **original** tier is right; putting them back into the
**standard** tier is not.

- **Measured first:** all 153 of the table's form corrections were *exactly*
  "adds hyphen and nothing else". So dropping hyphen restoration removes the
  script's entire form-correcting role for those rows.
- **Table 166 → 16 rows**, all parenthetical: 11 remove parenthesised
  uncertainty, 5 publish a parenthesised optional token as two complete
  sentences. (The 150 pure-hyphen rows are gone; the 3 hybrids keep only their
  parenthesis half.) The 16 do 11 real form changes; the other 5 are validation
  of the variant sentences.
- **Guard inverted:** the script used to *require* rows that add a hyphen; it
  now *rejects* any row whose corrected standard form contains one.
- **Findings:** `V133 dash_in_S_standard_FORM` **153 → 0**. `G010` stays 153 —
  it reports the *original* tier, which is correct. `review_qc_findings.py` now
  derives the expected G010 set **from the XML** (the decision table no longer
  records those hyphens) and asserts no standard FORM has regained one.
- Standard tier: 153 hyphenated sentences → **0**. Original tier: still 153.
- 52 XML files changed, 169 lines, all standard-tier hyphens. `--check` 0.

**Documented in README + GitBook, as instructed:** why the decision table is
used *rather than* `capture_manual_edits.py`/`manual_edits.xml` (each row
carries source form, blanket output, corrected form, decision and evidence, and
the build re-derives it rather than replaying a diff), what each of the 16 rows
does, and a **link to the table itself** so readers can check every decision.

is the only `RIGHTS.md` in any open PR, on main, or anywhere in history.

**Documented by nothing.** No reference in `CLAUDE.md`, `POLICIES.md`, the
`port-corpus-in` skill, `README.template.md`, or `corpus_page.template.md`.

**Not the first ad-hoc rights file.** Main already carries
`Corpora/Nowbucyang-Truku-Thesis/CodeAndDocs/data/processed/rights_and_permission_notes.md`
— different name, different path, overlapping job, also undocumented, and a
*different format*: a key-list (`rights_status: full_rights_obtained`,
`machine_translation: prohibited`) versus ILRDF's prose. Two files, two schemas,
no shared structure. This is fragmenting, not converging.

**Documented homes it does not join:** `TEXT/@copyright`; README
`{{LICENSE}}`; GitBook `{{COPYRIGHT}}`; root `LICENSE.md`,
`AI-USE-ADDENDUM.md`, `AUDIO-PERMISSIONS.md` + `audio_permissions.json`.

**The gap is real: POLICIES.md has no rights entry at all.** No POL-0xx covers
corpus licensing or permission evidence — which is exactly why the five rights
downgrades in this batch had nothing to check against.

**The content is good, though.** ILRDF's file records the source's own
statement, the finding, the authorization date, and the source URL + review
date — precisely the evidence a later reviewer needs in order to check rather
than re-infer.

documented per-corpus rights record rather than letting each corpus invent one
— fixed path, fixed fields (grantor, date, scope, evidence location, source
statement + review date), referenced from the README template and the port
skill, and covered by the proposed POLICIES.md rights entry.

found ... The prior `CC-BY-NC` XML label was therefore removed"), so it needs

## 2026-09-05 — Hash IDs: only #179, and they are stable against the wrong axis

**Scope: #179 ILRDF alone.** Scanned S ids in all 20 corpora with open RE-PORT
PRs: 8,848/8,848 hash-like in ILRDF, **0** everywhere else (Safolu `S00001`,
NTU `ap3_S_1`, HPS `001S1`, Siraya `verse1`, Glosbe `Amis_1`, …).

**How the id is chosen** — `CodeAndDocs/ilrdf_source.py:104`:

    def sentence_id(language: str, original: str) -> str:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(original.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
        return f"{language}_{digest}"

Content-addressed: the id **is** a truncated SHA-256 of the sentence's own
original FORM. 167,821 S, all ids distinct, no collisions within or across
files. A guard at line ~385 raises on a true 64-bit collision (two *different*
originals hashing alike; probability ~1e-9 at this scale).

**Advantage, and it is real.** ILRDF is an API-scraped dictionary. Sequential
ids shift wholesale whenever upstream inserts or reorders an entry, so
`Amis_5313` was never actually stable either. Content-addressing is immune to
reordering, needs no counter state, and reproduces exactly on a clean rebuild.
It also self-enforces the POL-022 dedup a dictionary wants — `extract_sentences`
merges into `grouped: dict[str, Sentence]` keyed by the text, so "same headword,
two entries" cannot exist.

**Cost: it is stability against the wrong axis.** POL-037 guarantees a published
id keeps pointing at the same record. A content hash guarantees the opposite —
the id survives only while the text never changes. Every OCR fix, POL-001
restoration or punctuation normalization retires an id and mints a new one. For
a corpus whose purpose is progressive source-fidelity correction, that is
backwards. The one-time cost is already paid: all 98,837 published ids are gone,
and the README says only "generates deterministic sentence IDs from the source
form" — no rationale, no acknowledgement of the break.

**⏳ Yes, it breaks `manual_edits`.** `apply_manual_edits.py:23` builds
`{s.get("id"): s}` and matches records **by S id**. POL-030/POL-002 send hand
edits to the *original* tier — the exact tier the id is derived from. So a
recorded edit changes the text, the next generator run mints a different id, and
the record targets an id that no longer exists: an orphaned no-op, kept with a
warning, silently stopping. If it *does* apply, the published id is then the
hash of text it no longer matches. Maximally incompatible with POL-030. ILRDF
has no `manual_edits.xml` today, so nothing is broken now — but the mechanism is
foreclosed for that corpus.

**⏳ Recommendation.** The API snapshots already carry stable GUIDs at every
level — `word.id`, `explanationItem.id`, and `sentenceItem.id` (e.g.
`20a69646-e70a-f011-bd65-00155db40116`). Deriving the id from the source's own
key gives reorder-immunity *without* hostaging the id to corrections. Trade-off
to decide: GUIDs are 1:1 with sentenceItems, so the text-keyed merge would have
to become an explicit dedup step instead of a side effect of the id function.

## 2026-09-09 (night) — POL-028 variant rework: four stacked PRs ready

All four built, each independently mergeable, **in this order**:

| # | Branch | Commit |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | `schema/form-ver-alt` | `b6fb98488` |
| 2 | `qa/standardize-derives-variants` | `f212c78d2` |
| 3 | `corpus/migrate-alternate-ver` | `c9f87c277` |
| 4 | `corpus/wakelin-resolve-parens-both-tiers` | `38c230407` |

### What forced a schema change

Your two rulings — "exactly one non-alternate of the same tier (kindOf), and
there can be multiple alternates" and "alternates can occur for both original
and standard tiers" — are not expressible in the current XSD. `kindOf` is an
enum where `alternate` sits *beside* `original`/`standard`, so a variant
carries no tier: a node with two variants cannot say which base each varies
from, and nothing can transliterate a variant because nothing knows its tier.

A variant is now `ver="alt"` on a FORM whose `kindOf` names the tier — the
shape TRANSL has used since POL-025, sharing one allowlist (V084 for TRANSL,
new V156 for FORM). V149 rewritten, V150 pairs within a tier, V157 (SOFT) is
the migration worklist. `alternate` stays valid but deprecated: retiring it in
PR 1 would make 116 published FORMs schema-invalid until PR 3, which would
stop each PR being independently mergeable.

**Two things you asked about needed no schema work at all:** `FORM/@notes` and
`TRANSL/@notes` both already exist and are documented — `TRANSL/@notes` even
says "a literal reading kept out of the translation text itself". You flagged
the TRANSL move as possibly needing a spec update; it doesn't.

### Two supersessions cited (POL-050)

POL-028's own "not `ver`", and `694bbc903`'s "standard tier only… the original
tier keeps all of this notation untouched".

### Results

- **V121 14 → 0** — WakelinTexts leaves the HARD list. The bank's
  corpora-with-HARD-findings goes 5 → 4, and → 3 once PR #170 lands
  Virginia_Fey.
- **V157 116 → 8.** Utrecht 82 → 0, Wakelin 26 → 0. Latham's 8 stay:
  its `make_xml.sh` rebuilds from the POL-035 snapshot and never runs
  `build_lexical_xml.py`, and POL-028 already records that 6 of its 8 are
  competing lexemes awaiting POL-027 remediation. Migrating data about to be
  deleted is work twice.
- Wakelin's `(unctn)` → `@notes`: 1 word, 101 TRANSLs, 1 deleted where the
  sentence repeated the word's marker. One gloss whose whole text is the
  marker (`Kalaku1 S2`) is left alone and reported — emptying a TRANSL is
  invalid and picking a replacement is your call.
- Wakelin's 7 parenthesis variants were **the only ones in the bank spelled in
  the standard orthography**, because they were created after standardize ran.
  Moving the step fixed that; all 26 are now original-spelled with derived
  standard counterparts.

### Caught in flight

- **V015** ("duplicate kindOf is forbidden") counted every FORM, so migrating
  Utrecht turned 81 nodes into false HARD findings. It now counts *base*
  FORMs, exactly as V085 lets same-language TRANSLs coexist when all but one
  carries `ver`. Folded into PR 1 and the stack rebased.
- Wakelin's `generate_xml.py` **reads** the POL-035 snapshot (legacy spelling,
  frozen) and **writes** the published XML (current spelling). I conflated the
  two and broke the build; readers now accept both, the writer emits one.
- **V150 4 → 8 SOFT** on Wakelin: the same four pairs, each reported once per
  tier now that the variant exists in both. Not a regression.

### Verified, not asserted

`standardize.py`'s change is inert for existing data: running main's version
and the branch's over the same input gives byte-identical output for Wakelin,
Utrecht, Latham and SEALS33. Utrecht's migration is spelling-only — 1143 FORMs
before and after, every text byte-identical, 82 attribute changes all
`(alternate, None) -> (original, alt)`. Wakelin's build is idempotent. Element
census: nothing removed anywhere, so no POL-051 disclosure is owed.

unauthenticated-HF job is out of the picture.

### POL-054 — waiving a HARD finding

Per-corpus `CodeAndDocs/qc_waivers.tsv`: `rule_id`, `file` (relative to the
corpus `XML/`), `location`, `reason`. A match reclassifies HARD → **WAIVED** —
still in the CSV, still in the summary, no longer failing. Applied in
`_report.py`, so all three finding-based validators get it with no
per-validator wiring, which is what let SEALS33's `check_hard_findings.py` go.

**Your two rulings, both in:** no count column; waivable rules restricted to
judgement rules — `WAIVABLE_RULES`, today just `{V129}` (V142, the other
judgement rule, is SOFT and needs no waiver).

**Your third ruling reversed the anti-drift rule**, correctly: the version I
built failed the build when a finding was *fixed*, taxing the action we want.
Now asymmetric — an unwaived HARD finding fails; a spent waiver passes
silently and is tidied on request with `waivers.py prune`. Landed as its own
commit rather than an amend, because #215 was already open (POL-050 shape).

Accepted residual risk, written into the entry: a spent waiver would silently
cover a *different* finding arriving later at the same key.

**Merging #215 blocks nothing** — verified, not assumed. WakelinTexts (14 HARD
findings, no waiver file) produces a byte-identical findings CSV and the same
exit code on both branches. Waivers are opt-in, only ever move a finding out
of HARD, and the PR gate (`compare_findings.py`) is relative, so the same rows
leave both sides of its subtraction.

**`compare_findings.py`, for the record** (you asked): used in exactly one
place — `xml-validation.yaml`'s `validate-changed-files` job, `pull_request`
only, path-filtered to `Corpora/**.xml` / `QC/validation/**`, and further
scoped to added-or-modified `Corpora/*/XML/**/*.xml`. The push/scheduled job
runs `--no-exit-on-hard` and never fails. Its fingerprint omits `message` (the
hunter-audit hole) and it is purely relative, so a pre-existing HARD finding
is invisible forever — which is the gap POL-054 fills.

### ⏳ Ordering: merge #215 before the GitBook sync

POL-054 changes `POLICIES.md`, and gitbook `tests.yaml` byte-compares its
synced copy against FormosanBank main. Prepared on GitBook branch
`docs/sync-pol-054` (`2cc0675`, off gitbook main): `sync_upstream_docs.py`
output, +62 lines, nothing else moves. Verified both ways — 4 passed against a
checkout with POL-054, 1 failed against main without it. **Merge #215 first.**

### ⏳ Still yours: how a V129 waiver should work

Three shapes, in ascending cost:
1. **Corpus-owned guard, status quo.** `check_hard_findings.py` pins the exact
   permitted HARD set. Cheap, but every corpus invents its own, and a
   bank-wide `validate_text` run still exits 1.
2. **Teach V129 the distinction.** A sentence-initial or token-initial `*` is a
   grammaticality judgement (POL-016, exclude); `*-` before a segment is a
   reconstruction label (allow, or SOFT). One rule change, no per-corpus state,
   and it generalizes to the next comparative paper we ingest.
3. **A POL entry plus a registry.** Explicit waivers keyed by
   (corpus, rule, location) with a reason, checked by CI.
My recommendation is **2**, with a POL entry recording that `*` in a published
FORM means reconstruction because POL-016 already removed the other reading.
Note the standardize fix I just made rests on exactly that premise, so the two
belong together.

## 2026-09-04 — ⏳ TO FIX: standard-tier edits outside standardize.py (#178, #161)

**Maintainer ruling (2026-09-04):** *"There shouldn't be editing the standard
tier unless there is really good reason to edit standard **without** editing
original."* Wants to review these two personally.

Consistent with the same day's **#167 hyphen ruling** above (hyphens out of the
standard tier; `4284801a8`). Both cases below are the *legitimate* divergence —
the standard tier is supposed to lose segmentation the original keeps — but
both are implemented in the wrong place: a one-off script *after*
`standardize.py`, which a standalone standardize run silently destroys.

### #178 YeddaPalemeqBlog — `CodeAndDocs/scripts/apply_standard_surface.py`
`rebuild_xml.sh` L55, immediately after `standardize.py` (L53). One sentence,
hard-coded, no record file:

    S652653654_2
      original: pai, maya manu seman-neka-aravac tua zuma.
      standard: pai, maya manu semannekaaravac tua zuma.
      notes:    "Source segmentation is removed only in the standard tier."

Asserts expected original+standard text first, fails loudly on drift. (Already
noted in the "Yedda follow-ups" entry above as part of #178's override set.)

### #161 NTUFormosanCorpus — `CodeAndDocs/scripts/repair_unsegmented_standard_clitic.py`
`make.sh` L182, after a *second* `standardize.py` at L177. One sentence:

    Sentences/Bunun/Bunun.xml  60_S_16   (xml:lang="bnn")
      source:   mansia Tainancia hai na=unau unku tu asang.
      standard: mansia Tainancia hai naunau unku tu asang.

Its docstring names the cause: "The shared standardizer intentionally runs C012
only when a sentence has an M tier. NTU Bunun 60_S_16 has source-aligned W
tiers but no recoverable M tiers, so its S-level standard FORM otherwise
retains a clitic `=` marker and triggers V126." It imports and calls the shared
`QC.utilities.standardize._process_standard_hyphens` for that one sentence.

### The pattern: C012 under-fires
After the #167 ruling, every remaining case points the same way — C012 is
*correct* about what the standard tier should contain, and simply fails to fire:

- **#161** — trigger requires an M tier; this sentence has W but no M.
- **#178** — same shape, one sentence.
- **#160 Song** — `standardize.py --copy` on a dictionary, so C012 never fires
  at all; `normalize_standard_forms.py` removes the residue by hand
  (128 decisions), and `fold_standard_stress.py` folds acute accents in
  `standard` **and `alternate`** FORMs because `--copy` never calls
  `strip_accents`. ⏳ The `alternate`-tier half deserves a separate look — that
  tier is source-facing and no policy says stress marks come off it.
- **#167** is now the counter-example that confirms the rule, not an exception.

**Proposed fix:** widen C012's trigger in `standardize.py` (W-tier presence, or
any S-level segmentation marker, rather than M-tier presence) and retire the
local patchers. Do **not** forbid original≠standard — that divergence is the
point of the standard tier. Forbid it living outside `standardize.py`.

**Companion check worth adding:** a validator or port-readiness rule for
"S-level standard FORM differs from what a fresh `standardize.py` would
produce". That catches this whole class, including any future one-off patcher.

### Counter-example done right
**#170 `reconcile_source.py`** patches the *original* tier *before*
`standardize.py` (make_xml.sh step 2 of 8) and deletes stale standard FORMs so
they regenerate — exactly what POL-002 prescribes.

not accessible to others."* A published corpus must be rebuildable from a
FormosanBank checkout alone — the pinned `Formosan-*` dev-repo commit is
provenance metadata, never a build input, and must never be a dependency.

Audit of the 24 open RE-PORT PRs against that ruling (full report:
artifact `b22d647f-1d41-419a-a5e1-e0d7490d9ba0`).
Note: 30 `Formosan-*` dev repos ARE checked out under `/workspace/`, so
source-fidelity checks are available in this container (no Yedda repo though).
