- ✅ **#167 two stray `TRANSL[@kindOf="standard"]` — CAUSE FOUND + FIXED
  2026-09-03** (commit `3b3069b91`). They are `078S4W19` and its final `M`, and
  they are the **only** two such glosses in the whole bank: every other W/M
  TRANSL is `kindOf="original"` (this corpus, 61,492) or unset (everything
  else, 865,938). Cause: `rebuild_xml.py` used `kindOf` as an
  *editorial-provenance* flag — `kind_of="standard" if <gloss is the editorial
  "?"> else "original"` — at both the W and M call sites. But POL-036 reserves
  `TRANSL[@kindOf="standard"]` for a standardized gloss recorded **alongside**
  a `kindOf="original"` sibling; these two had no sibling, so selecting
  `TRANSL[@kindOf="original"]` to collect source glosses returned a silent hole
  at the one morpheme the corpus meant to flag as a gap — the opposite of the
  intent. Fix: emit `kindOf="original"` and let the existing `notes` attribute
  ("No source gloss was supplied for final -i.") plus the `?` carry the
  editorial marking. One file, two lines; `--check` 0; bank-wide count 2 → 0.
  Note for POL-036: its additive pattern (standard gloss beside original) is
  used **nowhere** in the bank — worth knowing before relying on it.
  ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (maintainer ruling): no `?` gloss.** *"We shouldn't
  have a `?` gloss, particularly one added during processing. What we should do
  instead is just not have a gloss for that morpheme. That will trigger an
  error, but we accept that error and document it."* Done in commit
  `dfa85c227`. `078S4W19M0c` now has **no TRANSL**; the W TRANSL carries the
  source string verbatim (`do<qal>-plant`) with the gap in its `notes`.
  **Decisive supporting fact:** this source writes `?` itself as a real gloss
  for morphemes it cannot identify — **337 times in the DOCX** — so the
  invented `?` was indistinguishable from the author's own.
  **Three accepted findings** follow, all pinned to that word:
  `V064` every_M_has_TRANSL (SOFT), `G002` M_count_matches_gloss_units (SOFT),
  `G001` marker_skeleton_parity (**HARD**). `make_xml.sh` no longer passes
  `--exit-on-hard` to the gloss-scrape audit (which documents itself as *not* a
  gate); the gate is now `review_qc_findings.verify_accepted_gloss_gap()`, which
  checks all three against the XML and fails on a fourth finding, a move, or any
  other morpheme losing its gloss. Generator invariant flipped from "zero
  unglossed morphemes" to "exactly one". Documented in the README with a table.
  🐛 **Latent bug found en route:** `review_qc_findings.py`'s V061 loop consumed
  every gloss row without filtering on `rule_id`, so the arrival of any second
  gloss rule would have crashed it. Fixed.
  ✅ **GitBook done 2026-09-04** — see the GitBook entry below.

  *(superseded — original note)* ⏳ **Open for you — where the `?` came from.** Checked the DOCX: sentence
  078S4's word 19 has morph `al=te-talem-i` (4 units) but gloss `qal=do-plant`
  (3 units), so the final `-i` is genuinely **unglossed in the source**. The `?`
  is *invented by the port* — an editorial placeholder from
  `word_alignment_overrides.tsv`'s `canonical_glosses` (`qal | do | plant | ?`).
  The TSV's `source_gloss` column records the true source string accurately.
  So my fix labels an editorial mark `kindOf="original"`, disclaimed by its
  `notes`. The alternative is to emit no TRANSL for that M, but all 36,938 HPS
  morphemes currently have one, so that would make it the corpus's only

- ✅ **Ferrell row removal is IPA-neutral — confirmed 2026-09-04.** Maintainer:
  *"the conversion table used to have Ḍ→dr because add_phonology.py had
  difficulty with capitals. We since made add_phonology.py more robust... I am
  concerned about how it affects the resulting IPA."* **Confirmed: zero IPA
  impact.** A/B over the full corpus with the current pipeline: **0 of 128,830
  PHON elements differ**; `Ḍ` yields `ɖ` either way, in both original and
  standard PHON. The only difference is 30 standard-FORM elements (the 4 proper
  names' capitals) and 0 original-FORM elements. Mechanism confirmed:
  `add_phonology.py:269` compares orthography letters with `.casefold()`, so the
  profile's single lowercase row `ḍ → ɖ` already covers `Ḍ`. The workaround is
  genuinely obsolete — its removal only affects standard-tier capitalization,
  which you said you're not concerned about.

  still lowercase (`Ḍiququ → driququ`). Only without it does derivation from

  finding there. (My 2026-09-03 note below compared main vs the PR, which

## 2026-08-13 — classifier fixed; the Saisiyat guard is LIFTED

**`work/classifier` `59a4212ab`**, suite **1033 passed**, no corpus XML
touched. All four defects fixed, each verified to reproduce before the fix:

1. `attested()` truncation at `'` → `attestation_candidates()` offers every
   reading of the word run, so both-edge-glottal words (`'oka'`, `'aehae'`)
   can finally veto.
2. Truncation at Saisiyat's length `:` → the run now spans an interior `:`
   (`kapayaka:i'` vetoes).
3. Opener attestation in rules 2/3 → rules 2–4 veto on either side. **Two
   further bugs surfaced while fixing this**: no rule required opener <
   closer (rule 3 was pairing `Sa'` with an `'okik` to its *right*), and
   Rule 1 accepted a closer-first sequence — both now require proper
   alternation.
4. `TRANSL_QUOTES` split into directional pairs (`《》〈〉‘’「」『』“”`) and
   symmetric (`"＂`); directional marks count only as **matched pairs**, so
   an English possessive `’` can no longer inflate `tq`.

**NTU's stray-`"` debris was handled, not deferred**: a wholly-wrapped
TRANSL is discounted, but still counts when the FORM is quoted edge to
edge — which preserved 3 genuine Glosbe whole-sentence corrections that a
naive discount destroyed.

**Replay, read-only, mirroring production** — `'`→`"` rewrites before →
after: **NTU 44 → 2**, **ePark 30+1 stranded → 8+1**, **ILRDF 6 → 0**.
Saisiyat rewrites across all three: **50 → 0**. Regression holds exactly:
Glosbe **169 → 169, byte-identical sentence for sentence** — and matching
the committed `quote_corrections.csv` (168 c031 + 1 c032), which also
proves the replay harness faithful; Safolu 0 → 0.

Nine survivors were inspected individually: ePark Rukai 50551/146942 and
ePark Amis 266 are correct quotations; ePark Bunun 205909 (`'tupatu'`) is
uncertain; **one real false positive remains** — NTU
`Amis_Nr-frog_cinhua_S_14`, `miceli'` — whose cause is *dictionary
coverage, not logic*: NTU writes Amis in the `u` orthography while
`reference/Amis/attestation.txt` is `o`-only (`faloco'` present, `falucu'`
absent). Carried forward as non-blocking.

**The process guard is struck** in the design spec and in
`claudeplans/phase-a-reviews/00-consolidated.md`, and NTU / ePark /
ILRDF_Dicts are now running.

## 2026-08-12 — validator model corrected (standard tier / glosses / M tier)

**Maintainer correction, and it invalidates my earlier reasoning.** The
V063 fix decided "does a standard tier exist" **per sentence**, justified
by treating a mixed file (some sentences with the tier, some without) as a
case to accommodate. That is wrong: *"If there is a standard tier, it
should appear in every sentence in an XML."* A partially-populated
standard tier is an **anomaly**, not a normal state — softening it hides
the very thing worth seeing.

**Corrections now in flight** on `fix/v063-soft-without-standard-tier`
(amending `6c8007708`):
1. **V063 tier-presence is decided PER FILE.** No standard tier anywhere
   in the file → SOFT. File *has* a standard tier → HARD as before for
   every sentence, *including* one that lacks standard FORMs (in a file
   that has the tier, a sentence missing it is a defect worth failing).
   The "mixed file → S1 HARD + S2 SOFT" test is rewritten to "both HARD".
2. **Gloss completeness is never fatal** — *"we can't have a hard rule
   against it"*. **V064** (every M has a TRANSL) and **V062** (infix M
   needs an angle-bracket gloss) both drop HARD → **SOFT**; V065 already
   was. They now read as one family: gloss presence and notation are
   *reported*, never fatal. V062's case is notation, not missing data —
   Yedda glosses infixes in prose ("bring, AV. The root is kacu 'bring'.")
   and POL-036 makes a standardized `<AV>` additive anyway.
   → **This also unblocks `work/b3-yedda`**: its 6 blocking fingerprints
   were V062/V064 HARD, which become SOFT.

⏳ **Still to design — the M-tier rule (V144).** The maintainer's model:
- Generally, if any W in a corpus has M children, they all should.
- **But the rule must be switchable off per corpus**, because segmentation
  is genuinely incomplete in some sources — whole sentences unsegmented,
  or some words within a sentence.
- Either way it should be **reviewed against the original** to be sure
  nothing was lost in processing.
- **Refinement worth implementing**: compare against W-level glosses — if
  *every* word in a sentence has a W TRANSL and only *some* of those words
  have Ms, the M-less ones are almost certainly an omission, so that case
  deserves a sharper flag than a sentence that is simply unglossed.
Open question for the maintainer: where the per-corpus switch lives. My
recommendation is the **POL-022 pattern** — the corpus declares it in its
own pipeline/CodeAndDocs rather than a central table — since that is how
"is this corpus duplicate-free?" is already expressed, and it keeps the
decision next to the evidence. A repo-root registry (POL-039 style) is the
alternative if you would rather see all opt-outs in one place.

## 2026-08-12 — Nowbucyang second-clean_xml removed; Song stress analysis

**Nowbucyang DONE — `sweep/b2-nowbucyang` `c52665d0e`.** The second
`clean_xml` pass is gone and the rerun output is **byte-identical** — it
was genuinely redundant. Why: `standardize.py`'s C012 strips `-`/`=` from
S-level standard FORMs for every sentence that has an M tier, and `trv`
is not a hyphen-is-a-letter orthography, so it applies unconditionally —
covering 269 sentences. The 9 W/M-less sentences C012 skips are covered
by the `manual_edits.xml` records from the previous ruling. 269 + 9 = 278,
no gap. Surviving markers: **none** (0 of `-`, `=`, `<`, `>` in standard
FORM and both PHON tiers; `<`/`>` occur nowhere in the corpus at all).
All deltas zero; idempotent. The duplicate pair `C01_E026A_0079_01` /
`C03_E034b` is now recorded as a **settled keep-both** decision.

**Song `fold_standard_stress.py` — CANNOT be replaced by
`standardize --remove_accents`, but its duplicated table can go.**
Evidence gathered:
- The *transformation* is equivalent: applying the shared
  `strip_accents` and the script's private `ACCENT_MAP` to all 10,080
  original FORMs gives **0 differences** (762 carry acute accents).
- But the *timing* is not interchangeable. `--remove_accents` strips at
  the moment it regenerates the standard tier from the original, i.e.
  **before** `normalize_standard_forms.py` applies the 128 reviewed
  decisions. **15 of those 128 decision rows key on accented text**
  (e.g. `expected_input` = `íkamu; kamu; mu; kamua`), and the script
  asserts the standard tier is unchanged before review
  ("Analysis-tier standard changed before review for {record_id}").
  Stripping earlier would fail those matches — loudly, which is at least
  the good kind of breakage.
- Second, smaller difference: `fold_standard_stress` also folds
  `kindOf="alternate"` FORMs, which `standardize.py` never touches (it
  has no mention of `alternate`). The published corpus currently has 0
  alternate FORMs, but `normalize_standard_forms.py` can *create* them,
  so that branch is latent rather than dead.
- Caveat if we ever do swap: `strip_accents` removes **all** Latin
  combining marks, whereas `ACCENT_MAP` removes only the five acutes.
  Identical on today's data; a future macron/circumflex in the source
  would be silently stripped by one and kept by the other.
→ Recommendation: keep the step, but delete its private `ACCENT_MAP` and
have it call the shared `QC.utilities._accents.strip_accents`. That
removes the duplicated table (the actual bespoke-code smell) without
moving the strip earlier in the pipeline. Awaiting your go-ahead.

## 2026-08-12 — V062 answered; id policy clarified; POL-041 added

**Item 2 — V062 examples (Yedda).** The 271 findings are *not* missing
information: Yedda glosses the infix's function in **prose** rather than
Leipzig angle-bracket notation, which is what V062 looks for. Examples:

| W | W FORM | Yedda's gloss | M tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| `S668_1W5` | `k<em>acu` | "bring, actor focus" | `k-acu`, `-em-` |
| `S660661662663_1W4` | `k<em>acu` | "bring, AV. The root is kacu 'bring'." | `k-acu`, `-em-` |
| `S660661662663_3W1` | `q<em>udjalj-anga` | "it is raining already, actor focus. The root is qudjalj 'rain'." | `q-udjalj`, `-em-`, `anga` |

Infix distribution across the 271: `-em-` 155, `-in-` 87, `-en-` 27,
`-ema-` 1, `-ar-` 1. Note the second example literally says "AV" — just
not as `<AV>`. Under POL-036 any fix is **additive** (a standardized
`<AV>` gloss added as a separate `TRANSL[@kindOf="standard"]`, never
overwriting Yedda's prose); it needs a linguist, so nothing was changed.

**Item 3 — POL-037 clarified (maintainer).** The rule is *not* "ids never
change" but "don't change them without a compelling reason, and if you do,
be careful what breaks". Tidiness is explicitly not compelling: **keeping
original numbering with gaps is preferred over renumbering**. My earlier
Yedda parallel-renumbering is being reverted accordingly — the id churn
drops to the theoretical minimum (only `S535_1`, where the word itself
changes from `siyak` to `tjangtjang`; the other three sentences keep their
published ids exactly).

**Item 8 — POL-041 added**: W/M-level `TRANSL` (gloss) content is
deliberately **not** cleaned. Those tiers are human-read, not MT input, so
the extra material a source packs into a gloss (etymology, root notes,
alternates, asides) is information to keep. Consequences recorded:
parens/slashes/prose in glosses are not defects, and gloss standardization
stays additive per POL-036. This also reclassifies the earlier
"`clean_xml` skips W/M TRANSL repo-wide" finding — **intended, not a bug**.

**Items 5 & 9 — accepted/done**: V065 (772) is the signature of a
*partly-glossed* corpus (some Ws simply have no gloss in the source) — a
property, not a defect; `beautifulsoup4` added to `requirements.txt`.

**Items 4, 6, 7, 10 — in flight** on `work/b3-yedda`: double-infix
extraction fix (V067 ×3, `d<em><in>udu` → root `d-udu` + `-em-` + `-in-`,

   `uvi?` 'potato') — almost certainly a glottal stop. Needs your
   confirmation. Consequence already acted on: **no phonology step was
   added.** A probe with `add_phonology --orthography Ortho113` produced
   4,240 PHON with zero `*` — i.e. it silently *deleted* every `?` and
   asserted `ʂ/ɕ/ə` — so generating PHON under Ortho113 would fabricate
   pronunciation. Documented; PHON deliberately absent.
3. **`Kalaku4.xml` is actually text F by Saman Sunagu, not Kalaku.** The id
   was kept per POL-037 (published ids are stable) and the mapping is
   documented in the README, but you may want a different resolution.

  prominent CLAUDE.md note + memory. There is no Truku Wikipedia; the trv
  wiki is the Seediq Wikipedia.
- **Paiwan orthography** — Ortho113 Paiwan HAS `'` (=ʔ); `q` is uvular.
  Per-corpus orthography (from each README) is the only valid basis; never
  a single table. Encoded in the skip rule.
- **Boilerplate phrase** (`cinkhulan sa knita' sa brbiru'`) — "sources
  cited" reading supported (`knita'` view/seen, `biru'` writing/book,
  `cinkhulan` ≈ Atayal *kinhulan* origin); vocabulary is Atayal-leaning
  (Seediq uses *patas*); stub-template boilerplate across ~181 articles.
  Ruling: `knita'`/`brbiru'` whitelisted in the Seediq normalization.
- **Q5, TRANSL quote charset** — `classify_quotes.TRANSL_QUOTES` covers
  `" “ ” ＂ 「」『』` but NOT `《》`/`〈〉`/`‘’`; since tq==0 suppresses
  conversion, `《…》`-quoting TRANSLs falsely confirm "no quotation"
  (missed corrections only). On the classifier fix worklist with the
  `attested()` truncation bugs (at `'` and at Saisiyat's length `:`).

## 2026-09-04 — authority.json investigation + reference-data docs

**Q: "what is authority.json?"** It is NOT a FormosanBank repo-level file and
not (yet) a convention. Findings after fetching all 174 refs including
`refs/pull/*/head`:

- Present on **4 of 26 corpora**, all in OPEN PRs: #162 Paiwan_Stories, #163
  Li-Conjunction-Thao, #167 HundredPaiwanStories, #171 Presidential_Apologies
  (plus their `publication/*-20260822` branches). Part of the #157–#181 re-port
  batch. Not on `main`.
- **⚠ All four have DIFFERENT, non-overlapping schemas. No field name is common
  to all four:**
  - #162: `{formosanbank_commit}` — one field, and *nothing reads it*
  - #163: `{formosanbank_commit, source_development_commit, xml_sha256}`
  - #167: 5 sections — `source` (docx sha256s), `public_baseline` (commit +
    XML tree hash), `tooling` (11 git blob SHAs), `port_remediation`, `rights`
  - #171: `{formosanbank: {commit, remote, objects}}`
- **No shared repo code reads any of them** — 0 mentions in `QC/` on every ref
  including main. Each is read only by its own corpus's `make_xml.sh` /
  `reproduce.sh` / `review_qc_findings.py`.

**Maintainer said "document as if it exists in general, we have PRs for every
corpus."** Premise is partly off: 4/26, and they do not agree. Documenting a
general spec would mean inventing one. **RAISED, AWAITING RULING** — the
recommendation is to treat this as a POL-039 case (four hardcoded copies of an
idea that have already diverged, which is exactly the ISO-map failure POL-039
was written for): pick #167's schema as canonical, write one loader + validator,
then document. Docs should follow the spec, not precede it.

Side finding, ties to the maintainer's open editor: #167's `port_remediation`
targets `Orthographies/ConversionTables/Paiwan_Ferrell_113.tsv` line 5
(`Ḍ→dr`) — the row "overrode the standardizer's case-variant derivation and
lowercased proper names", so `Ḍ` should derive case-preservingly to `Dr`.
**Published `main` still carries that row**; only the unmerged port drops it.
The dev-repo copy's rationale ("redundant") was retracted in 4b5dbef60.

**BUILT:** `repository-contracts/language-reference-data.md` (approved scope —
attestation.txt + .rules.tsv). GitBook branch now 4 commits.
- `attestation.txt`: 16 languages, ~4055 lines, GENERATED by
  `build_attestation_dict.py`, read by `clean_xml.py` + `classify_quotes.py`.

  Builder defaults to single-word S-FORMs because interior tokens carry

  missing columns / empty pattern / backslash in replacement. Optional

(in corpus-metrics CI trigger paths; every `tokens` value is currently `null`),
and the legal/meta set (`NOTICE-AI.md`, `LICENSE.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
`pyproject.toml`, `xml_template.dtd`).

### authority.json — does it earn its keep? (analysis 2026-09-04)

**Unique capability vs every other corpus:** pins shared FormosanBank tooling at
exact git blob SHAs, clones/checks out the pinned commit, verifies all 11 blobs,
then builds. Every other corpus's `make_xml.sh` (Glosbe, Wikipedias, SEALS33,
Campbell-Favorlang, Virginia_Fey, Nowbucyang, Li-Conjunction-Thao…) is a
documented idempotent script that calls the **current** shared tooling. So the
one thing it adds is: rebuild with tooling as of port time, not as of now.

**Evidence it buys nothing today:** all 8 checkable pinned blobs are byte-identical
to current `main`; the baseline commit is an ancestor of main. The pin is a
**no-op right now**. It only activates the day shared tooling changes — and on
that day its effect is to rebuild with *stale* tooling, the exact opposite of
what the #157–#181 re-port batch just did to 24 corpora. It fights the project's
own model (shared tooling improves; corpora get regenerated).

**What it is ACTUALLY doing** (the real finding): #167 carries a **private fork of
the shared conversion table** — `CodeAndDocs/data/Paiwan_Ferrell_113.tsv`, blob
ae0e827f, differing from `Orthographies/ConversionTables/Paiwan_Ferrell_113.tsv`
(9c19e4f4) by exactly one line: `5d4 < Ḍ<TAB>dr`. The `port_remediation` block
exists to legitimize that fork. So its live function is not reproducibility —
it is letting one corpus disagree with the shared repo and record why. Wrong
fix: if `Ḍ→dr` is wrong (rationale: it overrode case-variant derivation and
lowercased proper names), it belongs on main where every Paiwan corpus benefits.
A fork means the next Paiwan corpus hits the same bug.

**Other defects:** `source` duplicates `source_checksums.sha256` byte-for-byte,
and `make_xml.sh` uses the .sha256 file (not authority.json) for the actual
source check — one of five sections is already dead weight. No shared code reads
any of them. Four schemas across four PRs. The name describes nothing.

**RECOMMENDATION — fold it.** (1) Land the Ferrell fix on main; delete the private
table fork and `port_remediation`. (2) Keep `source_checksums.sha256` — standard
format, already works. (3) Keep one fact, the FormosanBank commit built against,
as a single line (#162/#163 already do essentially this). (4) Drop the tooling
blob pins. (5) Move `rights` prose to the README, where every other corpus records
rights. (6) Rename any survivor for what it holds (`provenance.json`).

**Fair counter:** blob pins are the right mechanism if the goal is to *prove* an
artifact's provenance for citation/archival, rather than to rebuild it. But that
is a different goal, and it would need to be a bank-wide contract with a loader
and validator (POL-039), not one corpus's ad-hoc JSON.

STATUS: awaiting maintainer ruling. Affects open PRs #162, #163, #167, #171.

### Findings that settled open questions

- **`=` is NOT a null marker.** 4 occurrences, all Thao, all the source's
  "same as" notation joining equivalent phrasings. PR #179 deletes the
  character and produces run-on two-sentence standard forms. v2 keeps the
  source's first variant. The TSV's `note` column was simply wrong.
- **C012 is already satisfied.** `_apply_standard_hyphens` returns early
  unless the sentence has an `<M>` tier (`standardize.py:170`); ILRDF has no
  W/M. Its 3,882 hyphens are proper names, Bunun/Thao letters and loans, not
  segmentation. Item 6 needs no code — only documentation.
- **GUIDs verified safe:** 211,595 sentence items, 0 missing an id; 210,502
  distinct GUIDs, 0 carrying two texts, 0 cross-language. `Sentence.source_ids`
  already collects them (`ilrdf_source.py:353`) and never reads them.
- **The TSV's apostrophe row fires 99,821 times** — it is the corpus's entire
  glottal-letter canonicalization (`ʼ` U+02BC → ASCII `'`), not cosmetic.
  Deleting the TSV requires dropping `restore-source`, which currently reverts
  clean_xml's work on the original tier.

  tier (PR #179 kept them). Matches every other corpus and repo policy, but is
  a visible change to published source text. **Needs sign-off.**
- Dictionary filename: `<Lang>_dictionary.xml` vs `dictionary.xml`.
- Entry id prefix `d` (`Amis_d20a69646e70af011`).

### 2026-09-05 (later) — ILRDF v2, alternatives ruling

**Ruling:** `=` gets "the usual alt treatment". Implemented as
`FORM[@kindOf="alternate"]`, **not** a second `TRANSL[@ver="alt"]` — the `=`
cases have ONE translation and TWO source wordings, so the varying tier is
FORM. `kindOf="alternate"` is in the XSD and already used in Latham-1862 and
WakelinTexts. **Flagged back to the maintainer in case a second TRANSL was
actually meant.**

**Ruling:** parens and slashes come INTO scope; at minimum retain what PR #63 did.

**Checked — paren/slash handling exists nowhere but PR #63.** `pr/53`–`pr/58`
(Hunter, 2026-07-29) are V131 zero-width-character removal, which is where the
stray `qc_mt_text_remediation_20260729.csv` came from. `work/ilrdf`: nothing.
PR #179: the grep hits were `.parent` false positives.

**Data.** 376 paren-bearing standard forms (320 all-Latin alternatives, 54
all-CJK annotation, 2 mixed); 2,410 slash-bearing (Atayal 967 / Paiwan 774 /
Sakizaya 539 = 96%). PR #63's algorithm in its real composition order resolves
2,734 of 2,737 cleanly; the 3 failures are unbalanced source parens, a bare CJK
`或`, and a trailing CJK note plus inline paren.

**G011 split-into-two-S rejected for this corpus.** It assumes one alternation
site. Full cartesian split of the 2,410 → **15,483 S**, worst single Atayal
sentence → **768 variants**. Policy instead: original verbatim; standard =
first reading; `alternate` FORM only where there is exactly one alternation
site (4 `=` + 1,488 binary slashes ≈ 1,492).

**New out-of-scope item:** 92 records carrying `1. … 2. …` — two-plus distinct
examples in one `S` (75 Atayal). Source-structure defect, not an alternatives
problem. Task 5 inventories all 92 by id; splitting is a follow-up PR.

Plan updated: `4dbf705b4` on `work/ilrdf-dicts-v2`. Appendix C explains PR #63's
normalizer function by function.

### 2026-09-05 (later still) — ILRDF v2, alternatives architecture + variant cap

**Ruling:** record splitting must happen EARLY and on the ORIGINAL tier, not as
a late patch on standard. Plan to be restructured: a split/alternatives step
runs right after generate, before clean_xml and standardize.

**Ruling:** exclude sentences with >3 cartesian variants from automatic
handling. **That is 870 of 2,410** (Atayal 536, Paiwan 219, Sakizaya 112,
Tsou 2, Yami 1). Kept: 1,540 — of which 1,488 are exactly 2 variants (these
get an `alternate` FORM) and 49 are exactly 3 (first reading only).

**CORRECTION to an earlier claim.** I said splitting the 92 numbered records
"retires ids". Wrong — that is true of PR #179's hash ids, not of GUID ids.
86 of the 92 are backed by one GUID, 5 by two, 1 by three; one half keeps the
parent id and the others need a *minted* id (e.g. `_2` suffix). None of the 92
have audio. 83 split mechanically into 2-3 parts; 7 have a stray leading `1.`;
2 start at `2.`/`3.`. Recommended folding the split INTO this PR.

**Measured: PR #63's slash handling is not sophisticated.** Its only
clause-vs-word signal is `(?<=[.!?])\s*/\s*`, which fires on **6** of 2,410
sentences. Clause alternation is actually written `) / (` in **13** — all
missed and shredded, because `TOKEN_ALT_RE` uses `\S`, absorbing parens.
No parallelism, token-width, or attestation test.

**RETRACTED (same day, maintainer challenge).** I claimed 2,388 of 2,410 slash
sentences have every alternation side exactly ONE token. That was **circular**:
the regex `[^\s/]+(?:\s*/\s*[^\s/]+)+` matches only non-whitespace runs, so it
cannot represent a multi-word side. "All sides one token" was true by
construction, not by observation. See the honest re-measurement below.

**Prior art located, both reusable:**
- `Corpora/Glosbe/CodeAndDocs/scripts/glosbe_pipeline.py:2310`
  `target_gloss_variants` — splits on `; , /`, strips parens, enumerates a
  variant SET; `target_ildrf_reference_status:2340` adds the good discriminator:
  try the whole string, else require EVERY part to independently validate.
- `Corpora/Safolu-Amis-Dictionary/CodeAndDocs/build_formosanbank_xml.py:57-100`
  `strip_leading_annotation` + `recover_form_from_translation` — splits Latin
  from CJK at the first CJK char and repairs a `（…）` annotation that STRADDLES
  the split. That repair fixes 2 of PR #63's 3 residue failures.

**OPEN:** (a) does ">3 excluded" apply to first-reading resolution too (leaving
870 sentences with `/` in standard), or only to alternate enumeration?
(b) for word-level alternation, does the original tier keep the raw slashed
string, or become the first reading with the source string preserved in
`FORM/@notes`?

### 2026-09-05 — honest re-measurement of slash alternation (replaces the retracted claim)

Method that can actually see a multi-word alternant: does a slash touch a
bracket (`) /` or `/ (`)? Plus orthographic similarity of the tokens flanking
each slash.

**Provable phrase alternation: 25 sentences.** 21 of the 25 fall in the
>3-variant bucket, so the maintainer's cap removes most genuinely ambiguous
material. 4 sit in the kept (<=3) bucket and need review.

**3,769 slash-adjacent token pairs:**
| similarity | pairs | reading |
|---|---:|---|
| >=.80 | 2,177 (57.8%) | spelling variants — `swa / swaʼ`, `su / suʼ` |
| >=.50 | 996 (26.4%) | morphological variants — `pnqas / pinqasan` |
| <.50 | 596 (15.8%) | unrelated — `hatomi^ / foliki^`, and bracket boundaries misread as word pairs |

**Inspected the seven largest by hand.** `Atayal_faae0f9178f020a8` (768) IS
eight single-word sites. `Atayal_d947d6a434b9db1f` (768) is NOT — it carries
`(kana su / suʼ kusa kya) / (kana su / suʼ uci kyaʼ )`, a bracketed PHRASE
alternation with nested word alternations, plus `smayuʼ / smayu / (kbkaʼ
smʼang)` alternating a single word against a bracketed two-word phrase.

**Conclusion:** the sentence-vs-word problem is real in this corpus, not
marginal. I under-called it with a broken instrument.

### Two further rulings

**Split ids:** convention is a letter suffix — `S_59_a`, `S_59_b`. For ILRDF
that is `Atayal_605c631ca81eecac_a` / `_b`. No corpus currently uses this shape
at S level (the precedent is M-level, `M0` -> `M0a/b/c`).

**Zero-source-drift auditing DROPPED.** Maintainer: reproducibility is checked
by diffing a rebuild against the published tree; a refresh after upstream
change SHOULD change text. The real invariant is id stability — ids never
silently change, but may be deleted (suppression) or added (new items, splits).
Replaced with a committed ledger `source_data/published_ids.csv`
(id, source_guids, status, note) and an audit that fails on: an active id
missing, an XML id absent from the ledger, or a ledger id whose source_guids
changed. This dissolves the chain that forced `restore-source` -> which forced
`standardization.tsv`. Generalizable to a POL later; NOT generalized in this PR.

### 2026-09-05 — ILRDF v2 alternatives: FINAL architecture (maintainer ruling)

**Different options → different `S` blocks.** `FORM kindOf="alternate"` NOT
used. Checked its only repo uses: Latham-1862 (8, a word list where each S is
one lexical item) and WakelinTexts (17, all at **W** level). Neither is a
sentence-level precedent.

**Splitting happens on the ORIGINAL tier, early** (right after generate, before
clean_xml/standardize). The raw `hatomi^/foliki^` string is therefore NOT
published; each split S carries one clean reading with the source string in
`FORM/@notes`. Split ids take a letter suffix (`..._a`, `_b`).

**Cascade (staged — Stage A sentence-level, Stage B word-level):**
A1 numbered `1. … 2. …` · A2 slash after `.!?` · A3 bracketed phrase `(A)/(B)`
B4 one site, two options · B5 one site, N mutually-similar options (>=.5)
B6 ANYTHING ELSE → **delete** (more than one site, or N-way dissimilar)

Plus the Safolu straddle-repair for bracketed annotations crossing a split
point (`build_formosanbank_xml.py:57-100`) — fixes 2 of PR #63's 3 residues.

**MEASURED over the PR #179 XML:**
| | n | |
|---|---:|---|
| Stage A numbered | 12 | → 38 S |
| Stage A sentence-final | 6 | → 12 S |
| Stage A bracketed phrase | 1 | → 4 S |
| Stage B word-level | 1,497 | → 3,014 S |
| **SPLIT** | **1,516** | **→ 3,068 S** |
| deleted: >1 site | 862 | |
| deleted: N-way dissimilar | 32 | |
| **DELETE** | **894** | |

S per surviving sentence: 2 (×1,478), 3 (×31), 4 (×4), 1 (×3). **Max 4.**

**MAINTAINER'S PREDICTION CONFIRMED — no hard variant cap needed.** 866 of the
894 deletions (96.9%) are exactly the >3-cartesian-variant sentences; only 4
survivors exceed 3. The cap is redundant with the more-than-one-site rule and
is NOT implemented. The earlier ">3 excluded = 870" ruling is superseded.

**README/GitBook figures (maintainer required these be published):**
1,516 sentences split → 3,068 records · 1,315 spelling/morphological variant
sites · 195 distinct-word sites · 523 sites with an option attested nowhere
else · 894 records deleted as uninterpretable.

**Attestation (Glosbe test) is a REVIEW COLUMN, never a gate** — my earlier
note wrongly implied the maintainer had asked for it as a gate; they had not. `hatomi^ / foliki^`
is structurally unambiguous but `hatomi^` appears nowhere else; 99.2% of
ordinary tokens are attested, so the 523 flagged sites are a review list, not
a defect list. Deleting on rarity would discard good data.

Plan commits: `9e21ce6c4` (id ledger), `c5d5a7f2e` (split cascade).

### 2026-09-05 — ACCENTS_TO_STRIP gap (maintainer ruling: grave/caron SHOULD strip)

**Maintainer:** `è ē ǔ` should be deleted by `standardize --remove_accents`.

**Merged `origin/main` into `work/ilrdf-dicts-v2`** (61 commits, merge
`ef175f532`). Note for anyone repeating this: the worktree filesystem is
**case-insensitive** (Docker Desktop bind mount) and main renames
`Corpora/YeddaPalemeqBlog/readme.md` -> `README.md`. Git's `ort` strategy
aborts on that case-only rename. Workaround: `rm` the lowercase file and clean
the partially-checked-out untracked trees, then merge. Only that one path
clashes repo-wide.

**Post-merge, `ē` is already fixed.** Current main's `ACCENTS_TO_STRIP` is
{acute, **macron**, breve} -- macron was added since Aug 12. With the
per-language keep set: Amis `ē` x5 now strips (Amis attests none), Puyuma
`ē` x2 is kept (attested), Thao `í` x8 kept (attested). Correct behaviour.

**Remaining gap: COMBINING GRAVE ACCENT and COMBINING CARON.** Repo-wide
survey of every standard tier:

| mark | total | where |
|---|---:|---|
| grave | 218 | Wikipedias 176, Siraya_Gospels 41, ILRDF 1 |
| caron | 215 | Wikipedias 214, ILRDF 1 |

**No language whose corpora carry them attests a grave or caron letter**
(Amis, Atayal, Paiwan, Sakizaya, Seediq, Siraya all: NONE), so the keep-set
mechanism would strip all 433.

**The judgment call, which is why this needs its own PR:** the Wikipedias
occurrences are quoted foreign proper nouns -- `š ž č Š Č` (Czech/Slavic),
`à è ì ò ù` (Romance), `ầ` (Vietnamese). Stripping turns `Škoda` into
`Skoda`. That may be right (the standard tier is meant to be Formosan
orthography) or wrong (it mangles a proper noun), but it is a decision about
Wikipedias and Siraya_Gospels, not about ILRDF -- whose stake is 2 characters.

**Recommended: separate PR off main** changing `QC/utilities/_accents.py`,
with Wikipedias and Siraya_Gospels regenerated and reviewed on their own
terms. Per the ILRDF plan's global constraint, a repo-wide tooling change must
not ride along in a corpus PR. The 2 Paiwan characters in ILRDF stay until
that lands.

**Also surveyed and deliberately NOT proposed for stripping:** macron-below
(3,228, almost all ePark -- likely a real orthographic letter), circumflex
(878, Siraya 506), diaeresis (995, Siraya 434). These look orthographic, not
prosodic. Anyone extending ACCENTS_TO_STRIP should check them first.

resolved, 2 dropped** (the attached-bracket append idiom `uculru(wa)`).

## 2026-09-10 — PR #227 merged; two follow-ups opened (ver-blind lookups, NTU alternates)

**#227 `fix/standard-base-variants` merged** as `62b42b118`. It taught
`create_standard` to pick a tier's base by `ver is None` rather than by
document order. Verified before merge: `main` and the branch produce
**byte-identical** output on the real WakelinTexts and Utrecht XML, and
**0 nodes** in the bank have a base that is not first — so nothing needed
regenerating. Four failure modes were reproduced on `main`, of which
**case A (standard base silently derived from a variant) passes every
validator clean** — that was the argument for merging rather than relying
on V149.

### Two maintainer rulings, 2026-09-10

**RULING 1 — a tier with variants but no base has NO base (strict).**
The shared FORM selector returns `None`/`""` rather than falling back to a
variant. V149 (HARD) already owns that shape; validators skip the node,
and `corpus_counts` counts 0 *and* emits its existing "no countable FORM"
warning so the omission stays visible. Rejected alternative: fall back to
a variant (today's accidental behaviour), which would have every
downstream rule silently reasoning about a secondary reading.

*Consequence caught while implementing:* strict selection made **V060**
fire a bogus "word-count (0)" on a variant-only S — piling onto a shape
V149 already reports. V060's guard now skips when there is no base FORM.

**RULING 2 — NTU's 191 legacy `kindOf="alternate"` FORMs are migrated by
fixing the generators and re-running `build.sh`**, not by an in-place
attribute rename. NTU's `build.sh` creates alternates (`resolve_slash_
alternatives`, line 62) *before* `standardize.py` runs (line 68), so
POL-028 derivation adds the 191 matching `standard ver="alt"` FORMs for
free, and `CodeAndDocs` keeps genuinely reproducing `XML/` per POL-047.

### Why NTU needs this at all

PR **#224** (`d4d7bf53e`, merged 2026-09-10) landed one day after POL-028
was revised, so NTU's rebuilt XML uses the deprecated spelling. Measured:

    NTU alternates on main BEFORE #224 (d4d7bf53e^1):   0
    NTU alternates AFTER  (current main):             191
    published total: NTU 191 + Latham-1862 8        = 199

That takes bank-wide **V157 from 8 back to 199** (the variant-rework stack
had driven it 116 -> 8). Confirmed live: `validate_xml.py` on
`Sentences/Bunun/Bunun.xml` alone reports `V157 legacy_alternate_kindOf: 74`.

Every NTU alternate sits beside an `original`+`standard` pair and is spelled
to the **original** tier's conventions (it keeps the segmentation hyphens
`vcongu-si`, `mi-ta` that the standard tier strips), so the target spelling
is unambiguously `kindOf="original" ver="alt"`. Five emit sites:
`pipeline_sentences.py:649,764`, `pipeline_stories.py:578,723`,
`resolve_slash_alternatives.py:124`.

**Latham-1862's 8 stay deferred** on the existing ruling — its `make_xml.sh`
rebuilds from the POL-035 snapshot and never runs `build_lexical_xml.py`,
and 6 of the 8 are competing lexemes awaiting POL-027 remediation.

### Branch 1: `qa/ver-blind-form-lookups`

A new top-level `QC/xml_forms.py` (`iter_base_forms` / `find_base_form` /
`base_form_text`) is now the single place that knows base-vs-variant;
~13 first-match lookups across `corpus_counts.py`, `rules/gloss.py`,
`rules/text.py`, `rules/gloss_scrape.py`, `_source_align.py`,
`validate_audio.py` and `validate_audio_quality.py` route through it.

**A second, independent defect was found and fixed in `_source_align.py`:**

    wf = w.find('./FORM[@kindOf="original"]') or w.find("./FORM")

`bool()` on a *childless* lxml element is `False` (with a FutureWarning),
so for every normal text-only FORM the `or` discarded the `kindOf` filter
and the first FORM of any tier won. Verified in the interpreter and by a
regression test.

**Evidence that this changes nothing on today's data:**
- `count_tokens.py` over all of `Corpora/`: main code vs branch code =
  **identical** (152-line JSON, no diff). The CI token gate will not move.
- `validate_glosses.py` and `validate_text.py` on WakelinTexts (the corpus
  that actually has `ver` variants): findings CSVs **byte-identical**.

### Deliberately left alone (checked, not bugs)

- `standardize.py`'s `findall("FORM[@kindOf='standard']")` loops — POL-028
  requires transliterating variants too, so including them is correct.
- `manual_edits_common.render_s` — renders every original-tier reading into
  a human changelog line; showing a variant there is defensible.
- V148's `s.find("./FORM") is not None` — asks "has any text to segment at
  all", a genuinely different question from "which FORM is canonical".
- `orthography_detector.py` — a variant is real attested spelling, so
  including it in an orthography inventory is wanted.

### Addendum (same day) — the sweep found two more things, one of them live corruption

**The sweep was wider than the 13 sites first reported.** Grepping only for
`.find(` missed four more shapes. Final count: **18 call sites in 12 files**,
all now routed through `QC/xml_forms.py`. The four late additions:

| site | what it did |
|---|---|
| `sample_sentences._collect_forms` | builds `{kindOf: text}`, so a variant **overwrote its own base** — the human expert reviewed the wrong string |
| `find_duplicate_sentences` / `validate_duplicate_sentences` / `remove_duplicate_sentences` | `break` on the first FORM of the kind — two sentences whose *variants* coincided would read as duplicates |
| `classify_quotes._sentence_records`, `dialect_detector.extract_standard_text`, `rules/text.py`'s three `_*_form_text` helpers, `orthography_extract.generate_corpus` | same first-match idiom |
| **`add_phonology.py:362`** | see below |

**`add_phonology.py` was writing the VARIANT's phonology into the base's PHON.**
It looped over *every* `FORM[@kindOf=X]` and each wrote into the single
`PHON[@kindOf=X]`, so the last in document order won. `PHON_Type` has no
`@ver` in the XSD — a tier has exactly one PHON and it must spell the base.

#### This is live in published WakelinTexts — 48 wrong PHON values

Re-running the *fixed* `add_phonology.py` over the published XML:

    total PHON elements            : 4378
    variant-bearing nodes          : 25
    PHON values changed by the fix : 48
      ...of which on a variant node: 48
      ...elsewhere (should be 0)   : 0
    PHON on variant nodes          : 50
      unchanged (base==variant IPA): 2

Worked examples (published -> correct):

    Kalaku1 S7W1M3   FORM base 'am'    variant 'namen'
                     PHON 'namən'  ->  'am' phonologised   (nothing like it)
    Kalaku1 S13W1M2  FORM base 'nem'   variant 'namen'
                     PHON 'namən'  ->  'nəm'
    Kalaku1 S12W1    PHON 'malofotnamənɻanam' -> 'malofotnəməɻanam'

So **WakelinTexts needs a PHON regeneration** once the tooling fix lands. That
is a third branch, `corpus/wakelin-phon-from-base`, and it is a pure data
correction: re-run `generate_xml.sh` (whose step 6 is `add_phonology.py`).

**Also noticed, not fixed:** `WakelinTexts/CodeAndDocs/generate_xml.sh`'s header
comment still says steps 4 and 5 — `standardize.py` and `add_phonology.py` —
are "DELIBERATELY ABSENT" and that the corpus "publishes only the original
tier". The body runs both (steps 4 and 6) and the corpus publishes 2189
standard FORMs and 4378 PHONs. Stale since the 2026-09-09 rework; flagged for
a ruling rather than edited.

#### Ordering of the three branches

1. `qa/ver-blind-form-lookups` — the tooling fix. Must merge first.
2. `corpus/ntu-migrate-alternate-ver` — **stacked on 1**, because the NTU
   rebuild runs `add_phonology.py`. Built against main alone it produced
   variant-derived PHON (e.g. Rukai `20200508-CL-7_S_19`
   `nawsiuɭi` -> `nawɭisiuɭi`), which is exactly the bug 1 fixes.
3. `corpus/wakelin-phon-from-base` — also stacked on 1.

#### Evidence that branch 1 is inert on today's data (re-verified after every addition)

- `count_tokens.py` over all of `Corpora/`: identical to main. CI token gate
  will not move.
- `validate_glosses.py` and `validate_text.py` on WakelinTexts: findings CSVs
  byte-identical to main.
- The one intended data change is the 48 Wakelin PHON values, and those are
  fixed in branch 3, not branch 1 — branch 1 touches no XML at all.

### Addendum 2 — POL-056 changed published data after all (WakelinTexts)

Investigating the Wakelin PHON branch turned up something separate and more
important, and your steer ("this should be a data-driven decision — a different
Claude made the table, find what it intended") is what found it.

**`Orthographies/Wakelin/README.md` records the intent explicitly.** The section
"The glide rows, and why the table's order matters" said:

> `standardize.apply_standard` iterates the conversion table's rows **in order**
> and does a plain string replacement for each... they are placed **after**
> `ǥ → h` and `ch → c` (so that the digraphs are computed on the
> post-substitution alphabet, **which is what lets `panchy-` reach `panci`**)
> ... **The row order in `Yami_Wakelin_113.tsv` is load-bearing.**

That was written 2026-09-08 and was true then. **POL-056 (`307868c60`,
2026-09-09) made it false the next day** — a table became a *set* of rules,
staged longest-source-first, with a rule's output never re-matched. So
`ch → c` can no longer feed `cy → ci`, and `chya` stops at `cya`.

#### POL-056's "no published data changed" is incorrect

The entry says the change "corrected 12 misconversions across four tables...
none was in use by a published corpus, so no published data changed", and the
commit adds "Huteson-Rukai-Survey does use a table and is published; rebuilt
under the new code it is byte-identical."

**WakelinTexts is also published and also uses a table, and it did change:**
29 standard FORMs plus their 29 PHONs (`cia` → `cya`, `maciora` → `macyora`,
`ciaa` → `cyaa`). The verification swept **single symbols** — 342 of them — so a
**chained sequence** like `chy` was outside what it could see. Confirmed not to
be my doing and not #227's: rebuilding with pre-#227 tooling gives the identical
58-line drift.

#### Fix taken: the one POL-056 itself prescribes

Express the intent directly instead of relying on chaining — the same migration
`Amis_Church_113` got when the escape-and-restore idiom was retired. One row:

    chy → ci

`chy` is the **only** affected sequence: it is the only glide row whose source an
earlier rule can produce (`ǥ → h` yields `h`, and there is no `hw`/`hy` row).
Row order stays irrelevant. `Orthographies/Wakelin/README.md` is amended with
the old rationale kept and marked superseded, per POL-050.

Result — `generate_xml.sh` now reproduces the published XML exactly, except the
intended PHON correction:

    FORM texts changed          : 0
    elements added/removed      : 0
    PHON values changed         : 48
      ...not on a variant node  : 0

**Worth a wider check (not done here):** POL-056's sweep tested symbols, not
sequences. Any other published corpus whose table has a rule that could feed
another rule may have drifted the same way. WakelinTexts and
Huteson-Rukai-Survey are the two table-using published corpora that were named;
Huteson was verified byte-identical, Wakelin was not checked.

**A pgrep trap worth remembering.** `pgrep -c pytest` returns 0 while pytest is
running — pgrep matches the process *name*, which is `python`. Worse,
`pgrep -f "pytest tests/ -q"` matches the *monitor wrappers* that contain that
string in their own command lines, so monitors waiting on it wait on each other
and time out instead of firing. Wait on the wrapper PID (`kill -0 <pid>`)
instead. This produced one near-miss where a healthy run at 93% was almost
reported as a third OOM kill.

### POL-047 step numbering — answering "what are steps 4 and 5?"

**POL-047 is the convention.** It fixes a five-step canonical order and the
numbers are POL-047's, not the script's:

    1. generate_xml.py                     (corpus-local; original tier)
    2. QC/cleaning/apply_manual_edits.py   (optional)
    3. QC/cleaning/clean_xml.py
    4. QC/utilities/standardize.py
    5. QC/utilities/add_phonology.py

So `WakelinTexts/CodeAndDocs/generate_xml.sh`'s "Steps 4 and 5 … are
DELIBERATELY ABSENT" means **standardize.py and add_phonology.py**.

**Why it reads as nonsense:** the script also numbers its own steps, and the two
schemes do not align.

| POL-047 | Wakelin's local `step "…"` |
|---|---|
| 1 generate_xml.py | `1. generate_xml.py` |
| 2 apply_manual_edits.py | — none (correct; no manual_edits.xml) |
| 3 clean_xml.py | `2. clean_xml` |
| — | `3. resolve_parentheses` (extra) |
| **4 standardize.py** | `4. standardize` |
| — | `5. apply_r_caron_words` (extra) |
| **5 add_phonology.py** | `6. add_phonology` |

POL-047's 4 coincides with local 4; POL-047's 5 is local **6**.

**Three defects in that header, none caught by CI:**

1. **The claim is false.** Both steps run; the corpus publishes 2189 standard
   FORMs and 4378 PHONs. True at `f64dc5c0a` (2026-08-12, "publish original
   tier only"), stale since `282c49e31` (2026-09-08, "add the standard and PHON
   tiers").
2. **Not in the required form.** POL-047 wants `**POL-047 deviation:**` as a
   findable line **in the corpus README**. Wakelin's README cites POL-047 three
   times and declares no deviation; Wakelin is not in
   `generate_xml_pending.txt`, so it is fully held to the policy.
3. **Its two real deviations are undeclared** — `resolve_parentheses` and
   `apply_r_caron_words`. The second matters: POL-047 says a corpus-local
   systematic-corrections script "belongs after step 5, not in place of it", but
   this one runs **before** `add_phonology`. The reason is sound (PHON must come
   from the corrected standard forms) and is written down nowhere.

`tests/corpora/test_generate_xml.py` cannot catch any of this: it checks
canonical *relative* order (clean → standardize → add_phonology), which Wakelin
satisfies, and does not read header prose.

**Awaiting a ruling:** whether to delete the false paragraph and add a proper
`**POL-047 deviation:**` line to the README. Docs-only, would go on
`corpus/wakelin-phon-from-base`. Not done unasked — it is a statement about how
the corpus describes itself.

### xml-validation failure on the NTU PR — a duplicated finding, not a new one

**Symptom:** `xml-validation / Validate XML files changed by this PR` failed.
Reproduced the job locally over all 21 changed files; exactly one new HARD:

    ### NEW HARD (validate_text) in .../Sentences/Rukai/Rukai.xml
        1 x rule_id='V121', location='W=20200531-FW-Lixing_S_19_W4'

**Mechanism worth remembering.** `compare_findings.py` fingerprints on
`(rule_id, location, language, character)` — message excluded — and subtracts
**Counters**. So the same finding appearing *twice* where it appeared once
counts as new. On main the slash sits on one legacy
`FORM[@kindOf='alternate']`, V121 fires once; after the POL-028 migration
`standardize.py` correctly derives a standard-tier counterpart, so the same
defect is reported twice at the same location: 1 -> 2 -> "one new HARD".

This is the same doubling already recorded for V150 (3 -> 6) and dismissed as
benign — correctly, since V150 is SOFT. **The gap was never checking whether a
HARD rule doubles the same way.** Whole-directory validation cannot show it;
CI validates each file in isolation against its base, which is what surfaces a
count delta.

**Root cause, traced to the source rather than inferred.** The record is
`ngu-/mu-(a-)drusa` (gloss `NGU/go-(RLS-)two`) — a slash alternation whose
*second* reading carries the optional material. Step 14 of the builders records
word-internal optional material as a `ver="alt"` variant, but runs long before
`resolve_slash_alternatives`, so it split the whole slashed string into base
`ngu-/mu-drusa` and variant `ngu-/mu-a-drusa`. Slash resolution then de-slashed
only the base. The `(a-)` lived entirely inside the *discarded* reading, so the
variant asserted an alternation the word does not have (a variant of nothing,
POL-028) and kept the slash (V121).

**Maintainer ruling:** fix the generator, not the output. My first attempt was
a post-hoc cleanup in `resolve_slash_alternatives.py` that deleted the vacuous
variant; correctly rejected as treating the symptom, and reverted.

**The gate has to be narrow.** A blanket "skip step 14 when the form contains a
slash" would *break* the trailing-slash case: `hinolaong(-an),/` is ONE real
reading with nothing discarded, so step 14 is right there, and skipping it would
leave parentheses in a W FORM and create a NEW V121. Measured across every
source JSON: **153** strings mix optional material with a slash, and all but a
handful are `#c`/`#e`/`#n` translations and notes; the only word forms are this
record and trailing-slash artefacts. So:

    def spans_slash_alternation(form: str) -> bool:
        return len([p for p in (form or "").split("/") if p.strip()]) > 1

Applied to `pipeline_sentences.py` and `pipeline_stories.py` (both carry step
14). Commit `0c48fc358`.

**Result — three lines in one node**, and a fidelity gain: the `@notes` now
records the discarded reading as the source wrote it, `mu-(a-)drusa`, with the
`(a-)` the old path silently dropped.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| local reproduction of the CI job, 21 files | **job would exit 0** |
| `validate_text` Rukai.xml | V121 **9 -> 8** (one fewer than base) |
| `compare_findings` | **No new HARD findings** |
| `tests/corpora/test_ntu_alternate_ver.py` | 7 passed (incl. new corpus-wide invariant, RED before) |
| full suite | **1790 passed, 137 skipped, 0 failed** |

#### hf-audio-parity was gating audio-free corpora on Hugging Face

The WakelinTexts PR went red on `hf-audio-parity`. Reproduced locally:

    audio parity error: 429 Client Error: Too Many Requests for url:
    https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/FormosanBank/formosan-mt/tree/main...

Nothing to do with the PR. WakelinTexts has **0 AUDIO elements, no
download_audio_data.sh, and is absent from audio_sources.json**; only **9** of
the bank's corpora have public audio. The job triggers on any
`Corpora/**/*.xml` and then runs `validate_hf_audio.py` **with no arguments**,
validating the whole organisation — anonymously (`HF_TOKEN: ''`, deliberate:
it tests the *public* contract), across 21 datasets plus every model and space,
with no retry. That traffic shape is exactly what the Hub rate limits.

**Fix built on `ci/hf-audio-parity-scope-and-backoff`** (maintainer asked for
skip + backoff):

- **Skip** — new `QC/validation/hf_audio_scope.py` decides from
  `audio_sources.json`, which already names each dataset's corpus, so a new
  audio corpus is covered the moment it is manifested with no workflow edit.
  Only `pull_request` is scoped; push, schedule and dispatch always run, since
  those are the longitudinal signal on the Hub's state rather than a check on
  a diff.
- **Backoff** — `with_retry()` wraps all five HF API calls: 429 and 5xx get
  exponential backoff with jitter, 5 attempts; 401/403/404 are **not** retried,
  and a persistent 429 still raises. It makes a flaky run succeed, not a broken
  one pass.

**A design error worth remembering.** My first version treated any
unclassifiable path as "run to be safe", which silently defeated the whole
thing: the real Wakelin PR touches `Orthographies/`, so it still came out
`run=true`. But `Orthographies/` is not a trigger path — it merely rides along
in the diff. The rule is now: run if a contract file changed or a touched
corpus has audio; skip if every touched corpus lacks audio; run if the diff
names **neither** a corpus nor a contract file, because then nothing explains
why the job triggered. That last branch is what catches a trigger path added to
the workflow but not to `CONTRACT_PATHS`, and a test parses the workflow YAML
to assert the two cannot drift apart.

Verified against the three real diffs: Wakelin `run=false`, NTU `run=true`
(NTUFormosanCorpus has audio), `audio_sources.json` `run=true`.

  short placeholder and succeeded; the follow-up heredoc attempts then failed
  with *"No commits between main and docs/…"*, which is the "already merged,
  nothing left to PR" error, not a broken command. **Do not hand the maintainer
  multi-line `$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)` blocks** — pasted into an interactive shell
  one stray newline leaves it in continuation state and swallows every
  subsequent command. Use a single-line `--body`, or `--body-file -`.

  carry the reasoning, which is what `git log`/`git blame` surface later.

#### OPEN: POL-056 still carries the claim the Wakelin work disproved

`POLICIES.md` line ~1035, inside POL-056:

> Generalizing the placeholder corrected **12 misconversions across four
> tables** (`Puyuma_Cauquelin` `L`/`ɭ`, `Puyuma_MinEd` `ll`, `Rukai_Church`
> `lh`, `Rukai_Li` `ə:`); **none was in use by a published corpus, so no
> published data changed.**

The four *named* tables were indeed unused. Generalizing that was wrong:
`Yami_Wakelin_113` is table-driven and published, and it relied on `ch → c`
feeding `cy → ci`. 29 standard FORMs and their 29 PHON values changed silently
when POL-056 landed, and nobody noticed for three days. The GitBook's
*standardize* page was corrected in GitBook `#115`, but **POLICIES.md itself
was not**, so the policy and its rendered copy still assert it.

Fixing it is a two-repo change, in this order:

1. FormosanBank: amend POL-056 with a POL-050-style supersession note — the
   five tables are still accurately described; what was wrong was the
   generalization. Say what the check actually swept (342 single **symbols**,
   which cannot see a rule whose source another rule *produces*) and what
   catches it (test chained rules; re-run the corpus's `generate_xml.sh`).
2. GitBook: re-run `sync_upstream_docs.py`, or `tests/test_upstream_doc_sync.py`
   fails on the byte comparison.

#### Smaller, all previously recorded, none blocking

- **Nobody has swept other conversion tables for chained rules.** Wakelin and
  Huteson-Rukai-Survey were the two published table-driven corpora named in
  POL-056; Huteson was verified byte-identical, Wakelin was not checked and had
  drifted. Any other table with a rule that can feed another may have drifted
  the same way. The check is re-running each corpus's `generate_xml.sh` and
  diffing — a symbol sweep will not find it.
- **V157 is down to 8**, all in Latham-1862, deliberately deferred: its

### 2026-09-30 (night) — NTU: Latin labels in Chinese glosses are not code-mixing

**RULED (maintainer's words), 2026-09-30:** "latin labels like 3SG that routinely are written in the
Chinese glosses in NTU should not count as code-mixing for purposes of switching."
(Context: the 14 mixed reversals of OPEN 1 above; 10 published Chinese as English because their Chinese
gloss kept a label such as 3SG.斜格.)
**IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-30 (night)** — commit 03c8a6395 (unpushed). Operationalised as: a Latin run inside a
Chinese gloss is mixing only if all lower case (an English word such as `that`); a run with a capital or
digit (3SG, 1IPL, FS, Ca in Ca重疊, names) is a label. Source count: 14,263 Chinese cells hold an all-caps
label, 509 Ca重疊, about 170 a lower-case word. Applied to the column-rule licence and the single-piece rule.
Effect (word diff vs 9661b64af, 4 files, 12 words): 5 reversals to their own slots ('inia., ka'an-in=ku,
mi-k,, iikita, iikua); 6 words (7 cells) get one crossed piece exchanged (put-PV=1SG.屬格 -> put-PV=1SG.GEN).
Those 6 were in the 4a "leave alone" class (Chinese inside the English gloss) but have their English
counterpart in the Chinese gloss; flagged on the page for the maintainer. No new HARD vs main from
validate_xml / validate_glosses; V154 68 -> 66; 3 pre-existing V121 unchanged.
Of the 14 held-back words: 9 right, 5 still Chinese-in-English (ʉsʉ’-ʉn=maku, koo=pa=maku, miana=pa=ku,
kal-kanayrin=mian: a Chinese word in the English gloss; kavay: lower-case "that" in the Chinese gloss).
Review page republished (version 5) with one card per word and buttons, at the maintainer's request.

build on that one file step by step: the builder writes "ma, 'ameten hiza, haysani ila sa' isaa."; QC/cleaning/clean_xml.py
(the first step after the builder) calls QC/utilities/classify_quotes.apply_quote_corrections on each sentence's
original-tier FORM and rewrites it to 'ma, "ameten hiza, haysani ila sa" isaa.' (rule c031). Quotation rule 4 fired:
exactly one word-initial ' after punctuation (", 'ameten") and one word-final ' (sa'), neither word in the Saisiyat
attestation list (QC/validation/reference/Saisiyat/attestation.txt, 584 words; 'amet/'ameten/sa' all absent), and the
TRANSLs carry quotation marks. Word FORMs keep the apostrophes, so sentence and words now disagree. NTU-wide (cleaner
run on the full builder output): 60 apostrophes in 29 sentences (Saisiyat 28, Amis 1). The cleaner writes a
quote_corrections.csv log, but in the NTU build it runs in a mktemp work dir that is deleted, so the log is lost; the
committed CodeAndDocs/quote_corrections.csv (45 lines) is from a 2026-09-09 run. Not changed; the rule is bank-wide.

  0 have a different number of " in original vs standard (20 corpora with " in either tier). So in the published data
  the correction already reaches both tiers; no cleaner change is needed for that.

  original+standard FORM text, never W/M, and keeps (default) only S-FORMs that are ONE word long (dictionary
  headwords) and begin or end with '. Saisiyat: 31,660 S-FORMs scanned -> 584 words. 'ameten is a token 22 times,
  'amet 18, sa' 224 -- but never as a one-word sentence, so none is in the list. With the existing
  --include-interior option (tokens inside running text, freq >= 3; off by default for "pollution risk") the list is
  1,259 words and contains all three. My earlier wording ("contains neither 'amet / 'ameten") wrongly implied a

### 2026-10-14 — quote cleaner: maintainer's new rules (verbatim), trial on its own branch
Maintainer: "Re: The quote cleaner. We should add additional rules that apply before any of the others:
1. If the translation is wrapped entirely in quotations (the final quote may come before or after sentence-final
punctuation), then if the utterance is also wrapped by single quotes (again the final quote may come before or after
sentence-final punctuation), change the single quotes to double quotes. Treat the translation-wrapping quotes as
"consumed"; they no longer provide evidence justifying additional '->" conversions. If there are no additional
translation-internal quotes, do not processing this item further.
2. If the translation is wrapped entirely in quotations (...), then if the utterance is also wrapped by double quotes
(...), treat the translation-wrapping quotes as "consumed"; they no longer provide evidence justifying additional '->"
conversions. If there are no additional translation-internal quotes, do not processing this item further.
Further rules ignore the consumed quotes.
In addition, our allow-list should include words that begin *and* end in single quotes. After adding those, we should
remove from the allow-list any words that start with a ' followed by a consonant or end with a consonant followed by
a '. Use a branch and new worktree to try this out and see whether it affects any other repos."
- Branch feat/quote-cleaner-wrap-rules, worktree .claude/worktrees/quote-cleaner-wrap-rules, off main 52524b1f8.
- Implementation reading: consumption happens only when rule 1 or 2 applies (the translation AND the utterance are
  wrapped), as written; a wrapped translation with an unwrapped utterance changes nothing. Supporting change: the
  word-list lookup now tries the whole word (the old one-sided lookup could never match a word with ' at both edges
  or inside, so the allow-list change would otherwise have no effect).
- FLAGGED before testing: NTU SaiNr-frog1 S_5 "'aehoe' mwai' ila kita' oyae'." is "wrapped by single quotes" by
  rule 1's definition (glottal-initial first word, glottal-final last word) and its English translation is wrapped,
  so rule 1 as written turns both outer glottals into " -- the same misreading as today.

## 2026-11-11 — `?` in Kanakanavu glosses

**RULED:**
- Wild-Lehmann-Kanakanavu gloss `?` marks — *"I didn't mean Wild-Lehmann-Kanakanavu, but let's fix it! I don't need a
  decision page, though. They mark uncertainty. Remove them from the gloss and put "uncertain" in the note for that
  TRANSL."* → generate_xml.py `strip_uncertain()`: 83 W/M TRANSLs (42 W, 41 M) lose `(?)`/`?` and get notes="uncertain";
  bare `?`/`??`/`???` (whole gloss or one hyphen piece) still become `<UNCLEAR/>` (POL-061). Branch
  `fix/wild-lehmann-uncertain-glosses` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/wl-uncertain`).
- ILCAA-Kanakanavu-Texts "noon?" free translation (file 009, ex. 13, PDF p. 61) — *"Leave it."*
